units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    In Matins, after Psalm 50 and the Liti, the Trisagion, the Apolytikion of the Saint and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikion twice and the Theotokion once; then the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata in order, the Anavathmi, the first Antiphon of Mode IV and the Prokimenon "Precious in the Lord." Then "Let all breath" and the Gospel; then Psalm 50 is read, Glory, "Through the intercessions of the Hierarch," Now and ever, "Through the intercessions of the Theotokos," the Verse "Have mercy on me, O God" and the 1. The other three Prosomia to the melody "Who shall we sing" are not sung because their author, Nicholas Malaxos, Presbyter of Peloponnisos and First-priest of Nafplion, who lived around 1640, a man versed in Greek literature, motivated by piety to become a melodist, composed these hymns, as well as hymns with the same melody in the Vespers of Saint Gregory, and of Saint John Chrysostom to the melody "Called from on high." He thereby communicated with Venice and arranged arbitrarily with the printers who were there at the time to have these hymns included in the newly published Minea, by arbitrary decision, wherefore, he was proclaimed by the Synod of Constantinople as an innovator, and it was decided that from that time on that the published hymns were not to be chanted in the Churches of Christ.

units.slavonic_incipit: δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ. Κανόνες ὁ
units.slavonic_diplomatic: δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ. Κανόνες ὁ τῆς Θεοτόκου ᾨδὴν ἐπινίκιον, καὶ ὁ τοῦ Ἁγίου Ἀπόρῳ γλώττῃ καὶ χείλεσιν, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον, ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τοῦ Ἁγίου, αἱ Καταβασίαι Χριστὸς γεννᾶται, εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, τὰ Ἐξαποστειλάρια τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ Προσόμοια εἰς δ΄, Δόξα Σαλπίσωμεν ἐν σάλπιγγι ᾀσμάτων, Καὶ νῦν Μακαρίζομέν σε [εἰς τὴν Παρακλητικήν, Ἑσπερινὸς Δευτέρας, ἦχος πλ. α΄], Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον.

Εἰ τύχοι ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου ς΄ τὰ Μύροις παροικήσας, Δόξα τοῦ Ἁγίου, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, τὸ Προκείμενον καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τοῦ Ἁγίου. units.slavonic_diplomatic: Idiomelon "Well done, O good and faithful servant." The Canons of the Theotokos "A song of victory" and of the Saint "Difficult to tongue and lips." After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma of the Saint and the Theotokion; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and the Minologion of the Saint. The Katavasie "Christ is born," then we sing "More honorable." Exapostilaria of the Saint and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Prosomia of the Saint, Glory "Let us blow the trumpets of praise," Now and ever, "We praise you" {to be found in the Paraklitiki: Vespers of Monday evening, Mode I Plagal}, Great Doxology and the Apolytikion.
units.english_cohort_translation: done, good and faithful servant"** (*Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ*). After the Third Ode: the Kathisma of the Saint and the Theotokion; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion, the Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Saint. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and the Beatitudes, hymns from the 3rd and 6th Ode of the Canon of the Saint. After the Entrance, the Apolytikion of the Saint, that of the Saint of the Church and the Kontakion "The Virgin today." Apostolos and Gospel of the Saint. At "Especially," "It is meet," Communion Hymn "In memorial" "We have seen the [true] light," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 3.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika and the Beatitudes, with Troparia from the Third and Sixth Odes of the Canon of the Saint. After the Little Entrance: the Dismissal Troparion of the Saint, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle [Heb. 13:17–21] and Gospel [Luke 6:17–23] of the Saint. At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance"** (*Εἰς μνημόσυνον αἰώνιον ἔσται δίκαιος*, Ps. 111:6 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    If the Feast of St. Nicholas occurs on a Sunday, in Vespers on Saturday evening following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" we sing 4 Stichira of the Resurrection, and 6 of the Saint, Glory of the Saint "Having dwelt in myrrh," Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode. Entrance, "O Gladsome Light," the Prokimenon and the Readings. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory of the Saint, Now and ever, "O Groomless Virgin, from where do you come?" The Apolytikia of the Resurrection, of the Saint, the Theotokion, and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    If the feast of Saint Nicholas occurs on a Sunday: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira and 6 of the Saint: **"Having dwelt in Myra"** (*Μύροις παροικήσας*); **"Glory"**: of the Saint; **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings of the Saint. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: of the Saint; **"Both now and ever"**: Forefeast Theotokion: **"O unwedded Virgin, whence art thou come?"** (*Ἀνύμφευτε Παρθένε, πόθεν ἥκεις;*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saint, the Sunday Dismissal Theotokion of the Tone, and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 5.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon, the Liti of the Saint and the Triadic "It is meet"; then the Trisagion, the Apolytikion of the Saint and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikia as in Vespers; then the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos of the Saint. Kathismata in the first two Stichologie are said thus: after the Resurrection, we do one of the Saint and the Theotokion; in the 3rd Stichologia we do the Saint's Kathisma and the Theotokion. The Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon. The Canons of the Resurrection and of the Saint. After the 3rd Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection (read), the Kathisma of the Saint and the Theotokion; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and the Minologion. The Katavasie "Christ is born," and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing "More honorable." Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection and of the Saint, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Saint, Glory of the Saint "Let us blow the trumpet of praise," Now and ever, "Most blessed," Great Doxology and "Today salvation."
units.english_cohort_translation: 5.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon, the Litiya of the Saint, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Saint, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos of the Saint. The Kathismata across the first two stichologiai are said thus: after the Resurrection Kathisma, we sing one of the Saint with its Theotokion; at the Third Stichologia, we sing the Kathisma of the Saint with its Theotokion. The Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and that of the Saint. After the Third Ode: the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos (recited plain), then the Kathisma of the Saint and the Theotokion; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and the Synaxarion from the Menaion. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Saint, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Saint; **"Glory"**: of the Saint: **"Let us blow the trumpet of praise"** (*Σαλπίσωμεν ἐν σάλπιγγι ᾀσμάτων*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*);...[^188]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τῆς Ἁγίας καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς, καὶ τὸ τῆς Ἁγίας ἅπαξ· εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος· τὰ δύο ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ ἓν τῆς Ἁγίας Ὁ νέος οὐρανὸς, αὖθις δύο Ἀναστάσιμα καὶ τῆς Ἁγίας Ἀναβόησον Δαυίδ· εἶτα τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τῆς Ἁγίας Τὴν σύλληψιν σήμερον. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Κάθισμα Χορὸς προφητικός, Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Ἰωακεὶμ ὁ Ἱερεὺς καὶ ἡ Ἄννα. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    If the Feast occurs on a Sunday, in Vespers on Saturday evening following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" we sing 6 Stichira of the Resurrection, and 4 of Saint Anna. Glory of the Saint "That which is inexpressible to Angels," Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode. Entrance, "O Gladsome Light," and the Prokimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory, Now and ever, "Today from the root of David." The Apolytikia of the Resurrection, of the Saint "Today the bonds of barrenness are loosed" once, and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 2.    If the feast occurs on a Sunday: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of Saint Anna; **"Glory"**: of Saint Anna: **"That which was inexpressible to the Angels"** (*Τὸ ἀπόρρητον τοῖς Ἀγγέλοις*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon, and the Triadic "It is meet"; the Trisagion, the Apolytikion of the Saint and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Resurrection Apolytikion twice, and the Saint's once; then the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos; the 2 Resurrection Kathismata and the Saint's "The new heaven" then 2 Resurrection Kathismata and one of the Saint's "Cry out, David"; then the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon. The Canons of the Resurrection and of the Saint "Your conception today." After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma "Prophetic chorus," Glory, Now and ever, "Joachim the Priest and Anna." After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection, and the Minologion of the Saints. The Katavasie "Christ is born," and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing "More honorable." Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, and of the Saint "He heard your sighing" once. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Saint "Confide Adam," Glory the Eothinon, Now and ever, "Most
units.english_cohort_translation: 3.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of Saint Anna, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion twice and that of Saint Anna once; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos. The 2 Resurrection Kathismata and one of Saint Anna: **"The new heaven"** (*Ὁ νέος οὐρανός*); again 2 Resurrection Kathismata and one of Saint Anna: **"Cry aloud, O David"** (*Ἀναβόησον, Δαυίδ*); then the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and that of Saint Anna: **"Thy conception today"** (*Τὴν σύλληψιν σήμερον*). After the Third Ode: the Kathisma: **"The prophetic choir"** (*Χορὸς προφητικός*); **"Glory; Both now and ever"**: **"Joachim the Priest and Anna"** (*Ἰωακεὶμ ὁ Ἱερεὺς καὶ ἡ Ἄννα*). After the Sixth Ode: the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Saints. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, and that of Saint Anna: **"He hath heard thy groaning"** (*Εἰσήκουσε τοὺς στεναγμοὺς*) once. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of Saint Anna: **"Rejoice, O Adam"** (*Πληροφοροῦ, Ἀδάμ*); **"Glory"**: the appointed Sunday Eothinon Doxastikon; **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most...**[^189]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῆς Ἁγίας. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τῆς Ἁγίας, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ Κοντάκιον Ἑορτάζει σήμερον ἡ Οἰκουμένη (ζήτει ἀφ’ ς΄ Ὠδῆς). Ἀπόστολος τῆς Ἁγίας καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ τὸ τῶν Ἁγίων ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τῶν Ἁγίων Πατράσιν αἶνον προσάξωμεν· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Εἰς δρόσον τοῖς παισὶ, καὶ τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον· ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῶν Προπατόρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Προπατόρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι Χριστὸς γεννᾶται, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Προπατόρων καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων δ΄ τὴν τῶν σεπτῶν. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος* τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ τὸ τῶν Ἁγίων ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τῶν Ἁγίων *Πατράσιν αἶνον προσάξωμεν*· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ *Εἰς δρόσον τοῖς παισὶ*, καὶ τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον· ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῶν Προπατόρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Προπατόρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι *Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Προπατόρων καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων δ΄ τὴν τῶν σεπτῶν. *Δόξα* *Δεῦτε ἅπαντες*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Mode and 4 hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Saint. units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of Saint Anna. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 1.    In Vespers, on Saturday evening following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" we sing 6 Stichira of the Resurrection, and 4 of the Forefathers, Glory "O faithful, let us sing a hymn of praise to all the Ancestors who preceded the Law," Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode. Entrance, "O Gladsome Light," the Prokimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory, "The system of the Forefathers" Now and ever "You have conceived by the Holy Spirit." The Apolytikia of the Resurrection, of the Forefathers "Through faith, You have justified your Ancestors," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 1.    At Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Forefathers; **"Glory"**: **"The Fathers before the Law"** (*Τοὺς πρὸ τοῦ νόμου Πατέρας*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of the Forefathers"** (*Τῶν Προπατόρων τὸ σύστημα*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Seedlessly from the Divine Spirit"** (*Ἀσπόρως ἐκ θείου Πνεύματος*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, **"Through faith Thou didst justify the Forefathers"** (*Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας ἐδικαίωσας*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 the Triadic Canon and the Triadic "It is meet"; the Trisagion, the Apolytikion of the Saints and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Resurrection Apolytikion twice and that of the Saint once, the Psalter of the day and the Amomos. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon. The Canons of the Resurrection and of the Saints "To the Fathers let us bring praises." After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoi "In dew the Children" and the Resurrection Kontakion; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Forefathers, the Minologion of the Saints of the day and the Postscript of the Sunday of the Forefathers. The Katavasia "Christ is born," and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing "More honorable." Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Forefathers and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Forefathers, "Let us all celebrate," Glory, "Come. let us all celebrate," Now and ever "Most blessed," Great Doxology and "Today salvation."
units.english_cohort_translation: 2.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Saints, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion twice and that of the Saints once; then the daily Psalter and the Amomos [Psalm 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: the Resurrection Canon and that of the Saints: **"Let us offer praise to the Fathers"** (*Πατράσιν αἶνον προσάξωμεν*). After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"Unto dew for the Children"** (*Εἰς δρόσον τοῖς παισὶ*), and the Resurrection Kontakion; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Forefathers, the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Forefathers. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Forefathers, and the Theotokion. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    Εἰ τύχοι τῇ Κυριακῇ τῶν Προπατόρων, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τῶν Προπατόρων γ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου γ΄, Δόξα Τοὺς πρὸ τοῦ νόμου Πατέρας, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου. Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον [Καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα· τὸ Τυπικὸν δὲν ἀναφέρει Ἀναγνώσματα, ἀλλὰ τὸ Μηναῖον συνιστᾷ, ὅτι, ἐὰν ἐπιθυμοῦνται τοιαῦτα, νὰ λέγωνται τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τῆς ς΄ Δεκεμβρίου]. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα τοῦ Ἁγίου Ἱεραρχῶν τὸ θεῖον κειμήλιον, Καὶ νῦν Τῶν Προπατόρων τὸ σύστημα, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
units.english_cohort_translation: 2. units.verbatim_section_rubric: *(Note: The service of the Holy Martyr is chanted at Small Compline; if, however, the Saint is celebrated in the temple: at **"Lord, I have cried"** we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Forefeast, and 3 of the Saint. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τῶν Προπατόρων. Εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς Ὀκτωήχου κατὰ σειρὰν καὶ ἡ γ΄ Στιχολογία τοῦ Ἁγίου, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος, ὁ τῶν Προπατόρων καὶ ὁ τοῦ Ἁγίου· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Εἰς δρόσον τοῖς παισὶ καὶ τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον μετὰ τοῦ Οἴκου χῦμα· ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῶν Προπατόρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας, εἶτα τῶν Προπατόρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι Χριστὸς γεννᾶται, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν,

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Mode and 4 hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Forefathers. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Apolytikion, that of the Forefathers, that of the Saint of the Church, Kontakion "Today the Virgin." Apostolos "When Christ our life appeared" (29th Sunday) and Gospel "A certain man gave a dinner." At "Especially," "It is meet," Communion Hymn "Praise" "We have seen the [true] light," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 3.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Forefathers. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Forefathers, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle: **"When Christ our life shall appear"** (*Ὅταν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν*, 29th Sunday, Col. 3:4–11), and the Gospel: **"A certain man made a great supper"** (*Ἄνθρωπός τις ἐποίησε δεῖπνον μέγαν*, Luke 14:16–24). At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    If the Feast occurs on the Sunday of the Forefathers, in Vespers on Saturday evening following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" we sing 4 Stichira of the Resurrection, and 3 of the Forefathers and 3 of the Saint. Glory, "To all the Ancestors who preceded the Law," Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode. Entrance, "O Gladsome Light," the Prokimenon. {And the Readings: there is no mention of the Readings in the Typikon; however, the Mineon indicates that, if Readings are desired, those of December 6 should be read}. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory of the Saint "The divine heirloom of Hierarchs," Now and ever, "The system of the Forefathers." The Apolytikia: of the Resurrection, of the Saint, of the Forefathers "Through faith, You have justified Your Ancestors," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 2.    If the feast occurs on the Sunday of the Forefathers: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Forefathers, and 3 of the Saint; **"Glory"**: **"The Fathers before the Law"** (*Τοὺς πρὸ τοῦ νόμου Πατέρας*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. [And the Readings: the Typikon makes no mention of Readings; however, the Menaion recommends that, if such are desired, the Readings of December 6th are read]. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: of the Saint: **"The divine treasure of hierarchs"** (*Ἱεραρχῶν τὸ θεῖον κειμήλιον*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The assembly of the Forefathers"** (*Τῶν Προπατόρων τὸ σύστημα*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saint, and that of the Forefathers: **"Through faith Thou didst justify the Forefathers"** (*Ἐν πίστει τοὺς Προπάτορας*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Forefathers, of the Saint and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 2 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Forefathers, and 3 of the Saint, Glory, "Come, let us all celebrate," Now and ever, "Most blessed," Great Doxology and "Today salvation."
units.english_cohort_translation: Saint, and the Theotokion. At the Praises: 2 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Forefathers, and 3 of the Saint; **"Glory"**: **"Come, all ye faithful, let us feast"** (*Δεῦτε ἅπαντες πιστοὶ πανηγυρίσωμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Mode and 4 hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Forefathers. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Apolytikion, that of the the Forefathers, that of the Saint, and that of the Saint of the Church. Kontakion "Today the Virgin." The Apostolos of the Saint and the Gospel of the Sunday of the Forefathers. At "Especially," "It is meet," Communion Hymn "Praise," "We have seen the [true] light," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Forefathers. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Forefathers, that of the Saint, and that of the Patron Saint of the temple. The Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle of the Saint [2 Tim. 1:8–18] and the Gospel of the Sunday of the Forefathers [Luke 14:16–24]. At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    Εἰ τύχοι τῇ Κυριακῇ πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως, ἡ Ἀκολουθία τοῦ Ἁγίου μετατίθεται καὶ προψάλλεται τῷ Σαββάτῳ, ἤτοι τῇ ΙΘ΄ τοῦ μηνὸς οὕτω· Τῇ Παρασκευῇ ἑσπέρας εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα, Προσόμοια τοῦ ἁγίου Ἰγνατίου γ΄ καὶ γ΄ τοῦ ἁγίου Βονιφατίου. Δόξα Θεοφόρε Ἰγνάτιε, Καὶ νῦν Ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν οὐρανῶν. (Αὐτὸς ὁ ὕμνος εἶναι τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ Μ. Ἑσπερινοῦ τοῦ Σαββάτου, ἦχος πλ. Δ΄. Ἐγείρεται τὸ ἐρώτημα διατὶ ἀναφέρεται εἰς τὴν παροῦσαν περίπτωσιν αὐτὸ τὸ Θεοτοκίον καὶ ὄχι τὸ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ τυχόντος ἤχου τῆς ἑβδομάδος (Προθεωρία §8).) Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ τῆς Παρακλητικῆς Στιχηρὰ, Δόξα Ὦ τῆς στερεᾶς καὶ ἀδαμαντίνου σου ψυχῆς, Καὶ νῦν Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις προσδεχομένη, (τὸ Θεοτοκίον τῶν Ἀποστίχων Ἑσπερινοῦ Δευτέρας, ἦχος Α΄). Ἀπολυτίκια, τὸ τοῦ ἁγίου Ἰγνατίου καὶ τὸ τοῦ ἁγίου Βονιφατίου, τὸ Θεοτοκίον Τὸ ἀπ’ αἰῶνος ἀπόκρυφον καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ πρωΐ, μετὰ τὴν συνήθη Ἀκολουθίαν τοῦ Ὄρθρου, οἱ Κανόνες χῦμα, εἰς τὴν η΄ Ὠδὴν ψάλλεται ὁ Εἱρμὸς καὶ στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, τὰ ἐξαποστειλάρια ἀμφότερα καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Οἱ Αἶνοι τῆς Ὀκτωήχου. Σοὶ Δόξα πρέπει χῦμα. Τὰ ἀπόστιχα τῆς Ὀκτωήχου, Δόξα Στήλη ἔμψυχος. Καὶ νῦν Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις, Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ, τὸ Τρισάγιον καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ Ἁγίου. Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι κτλ. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, Ἀπολυτίκια Καὶ τρόπων μέτοχος ... Ὁ Μάρτυς σου Κύριε καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Κοντάκιον Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως, ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Σαββάτου πρὸ τῆς Χρ. Γεννήσεως, τὸ Κοινωνικὸν Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 19th of the month, i.e. Saturday and performed as follows: On Friday evening at "Lord, I have cried" 3 Prosomia of Saint Ignatios and 3 of Saint Boniface. Glory, "God-bearing Ignatios," Now and ever "The King of Heaven." {This is the first Theotokion of Great Vespers of Saturday, Mode IV Plagal; the question arises why this Theotokion was selected in this instance and not the Theotokion of the Mode of the week as is normally done [Protheoria, Para. 8]}. Entrance, "O Gladsome Light," and the Prokimenon of the day. At the Aposticha: the Stichira of the Paraklitiki, Glory "O your solid and firm soul," Now and ever, "Receiving the petitions of sinners" {the Theotokion of the Aposticha of Vespers, Monday evening, Mode I}. Apolytikia of Saint Ignatios and of Saint Boniface and the Theotokion "The mystery hidden," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 19th of the month, that is Saturday, and celebrated as follows: On Friday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 3 Prosomoia of Saint Ignatius and 3 of Saint Boniface; **"Glory"**: **"God-bearing Ignatius"** (*Θεοφόρε Ἰγνάτιε*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The King of heaven"** (*Ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν οὐρανῶν*). (This hymn is the First Dogmatic Theotokion of Great Vespers of Saturday, Tone Plagal 4 [Tone 8]; the question arises why this Theotokion was designated in the present instance and not the Theotokion of the current Tone of the week [Protheoria § 8]). Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon of the day. At the Aposticha: the Stichira of the Parakletike; **"Glory"**: **"O thine unyielding and adamantine soul"** (*Ὦ τῆς στερεᾶς καὶ ἀδαμαντίνου σου ψυχῆς*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Receiving the supplications of sinners"** (*Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις προσδεχομένη*, the Theotokion of the Aposticha of Monday Vespers, Tone 1). Dismissal Troparia: that of Saint Ignatius, that of Saint Boniface, the Theotokion: **"The mystery hidden from the ages"** (*Τὸ ἀπ’ αἰῶνος ἀπόκρυφον*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    On Saturday morning, after the customary Service of Matins, the Canons are read, at the 8th Ode the Irmos is sung and we sing "More honorable"; then both the Exapostilaria and the Theotokion. The Praises of the Octoichos. "To you belong Glory" read, the Aposticha of the Octoichos, Glory, "Living buttress," Now and ever, "Receiving the petitions of sinners." "It is good to confess to the Lord," the Trisagion and the Apolytikion of the Saint. In the Liturgy, the Antiphons "It is good to confess to the Lord" etc. After the Entrance, the Apolytikia: "You lent yourself to the Apostles' way," "Your martyr, O Lord," that of the Saint of the Church and the Kontakion "As first-fruit of nature." The Apostolos and Gospel of the Saturday before Christ's Nativity, Communion Hymn "Blessed are those whom you have chosen," "We have seen [true] the light," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 3.    On Saturday morning: after the customary service of Matins, the Canons are recited plain; at the Eighth Ode the Heirmos is sung and we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*); then both Exapostilaria and the Theotokion. The Praises of the Octoechos; **"To Thee glory is due, O Lord our God"** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) recited plain; the Aposticha of the Octoechos; **"Glory"**: **"A living pillar"** (*Στήλη ἔμψυχος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Receiving the supplications of sinners"** (*Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις*). **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ*, Ps. 91:2 LXX), the Trisagion, and the Dismissal Troparion of the Saint. At the Divine Liturgy: the Antiphons: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord"**, etc. After the Little Entrance: Dismissal Troparia: **"Thou didst share their ways"** (*Καὶ τρόπων μέτοχος*), **"Thy Martyr, O Lord"** (*Ὁ Μάρτυς σου, Κύριε*), that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"As the first-fruits of nature"** (*Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως*). The Epistle [Gal. 3:8–12] and Gospel [Luke 13:19–29] of the Saturday before the Nativity of Christ; Communion Verse: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω*, Ps. 64:5 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

The Praises of the Octoechos; **"To Thee glory is due, O Lord our God"** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) recited plain; the Aposticha of the Octoechos; **"Glory"**: **"A living pillar"** (*Στήλη ἔμψυχος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Receiving the supplications of sinners"** (*Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις*). **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ*, Ps. 91:2 LXX), the Trisagion, and the Dismissal Troparion of the Saint. At the Divine Liturgy: the Antiphons: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord"**, etc. After the Little Entrance: Dismissal Troparia: **"Thou didst share their ways"** (*Καὶ τρόπων μέτοχος*), **"Thy Martyr, O Lord"** (*Ὁ Μάρτυς σου, Κύριε*), that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"As the first-fruits of nature"** (*Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως*). The Epistle [Gal. 3:8–12] and Gospel [Luke 13:19–29] of the Saturday before the Nativity of Christ; Communion Verse: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω*, Ps. 64:5 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 3.    On Saturday morning, after the customary Service of Matins, the Canons are read, at the 8th Ode the Irmos is sung and we sing "More honorable"; then both the Exapostilaria and the Theotokion. The Praises of the Octoichos. "To you belong Glory" read, the Aposticha of the Octoichos, Glory, "Living buttress," Now and ever, "Receiving the petitions of sinners." "It is good to confess to the Lord," the Trisagion and the Apolytikion of the Saint. In the Liturgy, the Antiphons "It is good to confess to the Lord" etc. After the Entrance, the Apolytikia: "You lent yourself to the Apostles' way," "Your martyr, O Lord," that of the Saint of the Church and the Kontakion "As first-fruit of nature." The Apostolos and Gospel of the Saturday before Christ's Nativity, Communion Hymn "Blessed are those whom you have chosen," "We have seen [true] the light," and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὸ Δόξα Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες, Καὶ νῦν Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις (τὸ Θεοτοκίον τῶν Ἀποστίχων ἑσπερινοῦ Δευτέρας, ἦχος Α΄), τα Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Μηναίου Κύματι θαλάσσης, ὁ στίχος τοῦ α΄ μετὰ τὸν Εἱρμὸν Τροπαρίου Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου Κύριε, τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν Ἅγιοι τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰς τὰ τελευταῖα δύο Τροπάρια Δόξα Καὶ νῦν· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον καὶ τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον χῦμα· ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῶν Πατέρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῶν Πατέρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι Χριστὸς γεννᾶται, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Πατέρων καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον τῆς Ὀκτωήχου. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῶν Πατέρων δ΄, Δόξα, Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος, Καὶ νῦν Ὑπερευλογημένη. Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον Σωτηρία.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 2.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon and Glory, "Shining like meteors," Now and ever, "Receiving the petitions of sinners" {Theotokion of Aposticha of Vespers Monday evening, Mode I}, the Triadic "It is meet"; the Trisagion, the Apolytikion "Great are the accomplishments of faith" and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikia as in Vespers, the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon. The Canon of the Mineon "Waves of the sea"; the Verse of the first hymn after the Irmos is "Glory to Your holy Resurrection, O Lord"; for the rest of the hymns, the Verse "Saints of God" is sung; and at the last two hymns we use Glory Now and ever. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoi "An angel dampened the fire of the Children" and the Resurrection Kontakion; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Fathers, the Minologion of the Saints of the day and the Postscript of the Fathers. The Katavasie "Christ is born," and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing "More honorable." Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers, and the Theotokion of the Octoichos. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers. Glory, "The collection of Mosaic teachings," Now and ever, "Most blessed," Great Doxology and "Today salvation."
units.english_cohort_translation: 2.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon; **"Glory"**: **"Flashing like lightning bolts"** (*Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Receiving the supplications of sinners"** (*Ἁμαρτωλῶν τὰς δεήσεις*, the Theotokion of the Aposticha of Monday Vespers, Tone 1); the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); the Dismissal Troparion: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canon from the Menaion: **"By the wave of the sea"** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*); the verse before the first Troparion following each Heirmos is **"Glory to Thy holy Resurrection, O Lord"** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου, Κύριε*); for the remaining Troparia, the verse is **"Saints of God, intercede for us"** (*Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρεσβεύσατε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν*); at the final two Troparia we chant **"Glory"** and **"Both now and ever"**. After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"** (*Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*), and the Resurrection Kontakion (recited plain); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Fathers, the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Fathers. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Fathers, and the Sunday Dismissal Theotokion of the Octoechos. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers; **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of legal teachings"** (*Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 3.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Mode and 4 hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Forefathers. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Apolytikion, that of the Fathers "Great are the accomplishments of Faith," that of the Saint of the Church and the Kontakion "Today the Virgin." Apostolos "Brethren by faith Abraham" and Gospel "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ." At "Especially," "It is meet," Communion Hymn "Praise," "We have seen the [true] light," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 3.    At the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone and 4 Troparia from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Forefathers. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Fathers: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle: **"Brethren, by faith Abraham sojourned"** (*Ἀδελφοί, πίστει παρῴκησεν Ἀβραάμ*, Heb. 11:9–10, 32–40) and the Gospel: **"The book of the generation of Jesus Christ"** (*Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ*, Matt. 1:1–25). At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.[^194]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως Κυριακὴ ἀπὸ τῆς κ΄ μέχρι τῆς κγ΄ τοῦ μηνὸς, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, Προεόρτια Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ γ΄ καὶ γ΄ τῶν Πατέρων Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοὶ, Δόξα Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν, Καὶ νῦν τὸ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν, τὸ Προκείμενον καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τῶν Πατέρων. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, Δόξα Χαίρετε προφῆται τίμιοι, Καὶ νῦν Ἰδοὺ καιρὸς ἤγγικε, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Πατέρων, τὸ Προεόρτιον Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 5.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὸ Δόξα τῆς Λιτῆς Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες, Καὶ νῦν Προεόρτιον Ἄκουε οὐρανὲ, τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, Καθίσματα ἀναστάσιμα δύο καὶ ἓν προεόρτιον Τῶν προφητῶν αἱ ῥήσεις καὶ αὖθις Ἀναστάσιμα δύο καὶ ἕτερον Προεόρτιον Αὐλῶν ποιμενικῶν (ζήτει ἀμφότερα τῇ κδ΄ τοῦ μηνός)· εἶτα τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον· ὁ Κανὼν τῶν Πατέρων Κύματι θαλάσσης, μετὰ δὲ τὸν Εἱρμὸν ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς, λέγεται Στίχος Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ ἀναστάσει σου Κύριε, εἰς τὰ λοιπὰ Τροπάρια Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ εἰς τὰ τελευταῖα δύο Δόξα Καὶ νῦν· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Ἄγγελος παίδων καὶ τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον χῦμα, ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ ὁ Οἶκος Τῆς σῆς Παρθένε κυήσεως, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς, αἱ Καταβασίαι Χριστὸς γεννᾶται καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν. Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Πατέρων καὶ τὸ Προεόρτιον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῶν Πατέρων δ΄, Δόξα Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος, Καὶ νῦν Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    If the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ is celebrated from the 20th until the 23rd of the month, in Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at “Lord, I have cried,” we sing 4 Stichira of the Resurrection, 3 of the Pre-feast “Most immaculate Virgin of God,” and 3 of the Fathers “We celebrate today the memory of the ancestors of Christ,” Glory, “Daniel the man of desires,” Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode. Entrance, “O Gladsome Light,” the Prokimenon and the Readings of the Fathers. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory “Rejoice, O honored prophets,” Now and ever, “Behold, the time of our salvation.” The Apolytikia of the Resurrection, of the Fathers, and of the Pre-feast “Make ready, Bethlehem,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    If the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ occurs between the 20th and the 23rd of the month: at Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 Forefeast Prosomoia: **"O all-blameless Virgin of God"** (*Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ*), and 3 of the Fathers: **"Today, ye faithful, let us celebrate the memory of the Fathers"** (*Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοί*); **"Glory"**: **"Daniel, a man of desires"** (*Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings of the Fathers [Gen. 14:14–20; Deut. 1:8–11, 15–17; Deut. 10:14–21]. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"Rejoice, ye honored Prophets"** (*Χαίρετε, προφῆται τίμιοι*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Behold, the time is at hand"** (*Ἰδοὺ καιρὸς ἤγγικε*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Fathers: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion: **"Make ready, O Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*), and Dismissal.

On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon and the Glory of the Liti “Shining like meteors,” Now and ever, “Listen, O heaven,” the Triadic “It is meet”; the Trisagion, the Apolytikion “Make ready, Bethlehem” and the Exapsalmos. At “God is the Lord”: the Apolytikia as in Vespers, the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata: two of the Resurrection and one of the Pre-feast “The sayings of the prophets,” and immediately two Resurrection Kathismata and another of the Pre-feast “As shepherds were piping” (these are both found on the 24th of this month); then the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon; the Canon of the Fathers “Waves of the sea,” the Verse of the first hymn after the Irmos being “Glory to your holy Resurrection O Lord”; for the rest of the hymns, the Verse “Saints of God”; and for the last two hymns Glory, Now and ever. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoi “An angel dampened the fire of the children” and the Resurrection Kontakion (read); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion “Rejoice, Bethlehem” and the Ikos “Of your conception, O Virgin,” the Minologion of the Saints of the day and the Postscript of the Sunday. The Katavasie “Christ is born,” and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing “More honorable.” Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers and of the Pre-feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers, Glory, “The collection of Mosaic teachings,” Now and ever, “Most blessed,” Great Doxology and “Today salvation.”
units.english_cohort_translation: 5.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Glory of the Lite: **"Flashing like lightning bolts"** (*Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες*); **"Both now and ever"**: Forefeast: **"Hear, O heaven"** (*Ἄκουε οὐρανέ*); the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); the Trisagion, the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion: **"Make ready, O Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*), and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata: two of the Resurrection and one Forefeast Kathisma: **"The sayings of the Prophets"** (*Τῶν προφητῶν αἱ ῥήσεις*), and again two Resurrection Kathismata and another Forefeast Kathisma: **"While shepherds were piping"** (*Αὐλῶν ποιμενικῶν*, look for both on the 24th of this month); then the Sunday Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canon of the Fathers: **"By the wave of the sea"** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*); the verse before the first Troparion of each Ode following the Heirmos is **"Glory to Thy holy Resurrection, O Lord"** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ ἀναστάσει σου, Κύριε*); for the remaining Troparia we chant the verse **"Saints of God, intercede for us"** (*Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρεσβεύσατε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν*); and at the final two Troparia we chant **"Glory"** and **"Both now and ever"**. After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"** (*Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*), and the Resurrection Kontakion (recited plain); after the Sixth Ode: the Forefeast Kontakion: **"Be glad, O Bethlehem"** (*Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεέμ*) and the Ikos: **"Of Thy conception, O Virgin"** (*Τῆς σῆς, Παρθένε, κυήσεως*), the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Fathers, and that of the Forefeast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers; **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of legal teachings"** (*Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 7.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως Κυριακὴ τῇ κδ΄ τοῦ μηνὸς, ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ οὐδὲν τῶν Ἀναστασίμων ψάλλομεν, ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν Πατέρων μετὰ τῶν Προεορτίων οὕτω· Μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν Προσόμοια τῶν Πατέρων Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοὶ εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ Προεόρτια Προεορτάσωμεν λαοὶ Χριστοῦ τὰ γενέθλια (ζήτει τῇ κ΄ τοῦ Μηνός). Δόξα Δανιὴλ ἐπιθυμιῶν, Καὶ νῦν Σπήλαιον εὐτρεπίζου. Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν, τὸ Προκείμενον καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ ἀπόστιχα, τὰ γ΄ Προσόμοια Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ (ζήτει ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ), οἱ Στίχοι Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος Καὶ ὁ ἕτερος Κύριε εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην. Κύριε κατενόησα τὰ ἔργα σου καὶ ἐξέστην. Δόξα Χαίρετε προφῆται τίμιοι, Καὶ νῦν Ἰδοὺ καιρὸς ἤγγικε τῆς σωτηρίας ἡμῶν. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 8.    Εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ἀντὶ τοῦ Τριαδικοῦ κανόνος ψάλλεται ὁ μετὰ τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν τῆς κδ΄ κείμενος Κανὼν Κύματι θαλάσσης, εἶτα Δόξα Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες, Καὶ νῦν Ἄκουε οὐρανὲ (ζήτει ἀμφότερα ἐν τῇ ιη΄ τοῦ μηνός)· εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ ἀναστάσιμον τοῦ ἤχου Ἀπολυτίκιον, τῶν Πατέρων, τὸ Προεόρτιον, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος. Καθίσματα εἰς τὴν α΄ Στιχολογίαν Ἀναστάσιμα δύο καὶ τὸ Προεόρτιον Τῶν προφητῶν αἱ ῥήσεις· εἰς τὴν β΄ Στιχολογίαν αὖθις Ἀναστάσιμα δύο καὶ τὸ Προεόρτιον Αὐλῶν ποιμενικῶν (ζήτει ἀμφότερα ἐν τῇ κδ΄)· εἶτα ἡ Αἴτησις καὶ ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοί, τὸ Προκείμενον, ὁ Κανὼν Κύματι θαλάσσης. Εἰς τὸ πρῶτον

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 7.    If the Sunday before Christ’s Nativity occurs on the 24th of the month, in Vespers we sing none of the Resurrection Hymns, but only those of the Fathers with the Pre-feast as follows: Following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at “Lord, I have cried” we sing 4 Prosomia Stichira of the Fathers “We celebrate today the memory of the ancestors of Christ,” 4 of the Pre-feast “Let us celebrate, O people the birth” (these are found on December 20), Glory, “Daniel the man of desires,” Now and ever, “Prepare O cave.” Entrance, “O Gladsome Light,” the Prokimenon and the Readings. At the Aposticha: the 3 Prosomia Stichira “Most immaculate Virgin of God” (these are found in the Vespers of the Sunday before Christmas), the Verses “God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed by the forest” (Habakkuk 3:3) and the following “O Lord, I have heard the report of You and was afraid. Lord, I considered Your works and was amazed” (Habakkuk 3:1-2) Glory, “Rejoice, O honored prophets,” Now and ever, “Behold, the time of our salvation.” The Apolytikia of the Fathers “Great are the accomplishments of faith,” and of the Pre-feast “Mary once, with aged Joseph, was registered in a census” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 7.    If the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ occurs on the 24th of the month: at Vespers we sing none of the Resurrection hymns, but only those of the Fathers combined with the Forefeast as follows: Following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Prosomoia Stichira of the Fathers: **"Today, ye faithful, let us celebrate the memory of the Fathers"** (*Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοί*), and 4 of the Forefeast: **"Let us celebrate beforehand, O ye peoples, the Nativity of Christ"** (*Προεορτάσωμεν λαοὶ Χριστοῦ τὰ γενέθλια*, look on December 20); **"Glory"**: **"Daniel, a man of desires"** (*Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Prepare thyself, O cave"** (*Σπήλαιον εὐτρεπίζου*). Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings of the Fathers [Gen. 14:14–20; Deut. 1:8–11, 15–17; Deut. 10:14–21]. At the Aposticha: 3 Prosomoia: **"O all-blameless Virgin of God"** (*Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ*, look at Vespers of Dec 20); the Verses: **"God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ Ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος*, Habakkuk 3:3 LXX), and the second: **"O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid; O Lord, I considered Thy works, and was astonished"** (*Κύριε, εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην· Κύριε, κατενόησα τὰ ἔργα σου καὶ ἐξέστην*, Habakkuk 3:1–2 LXX); **"Glory"**: **"Rejoice, ye honored Prophets"** (*Χαίρετε, προφῆται τίμιοι*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Behold, the time of our salvation is at hand"** (*Ἰδοὺ καιρὸς ἤγγικε τῆς σωτηρίας ἡμῶν*). Dismissal Troparia: that of the Fathers: **"Great are the accomplishments of faith"** (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion: **"Mary once, with aged Joseph, went to be enrolled"** (*Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: Τροπάριον ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς μετὰ τὸν Εἱρμὸν
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Τροπάριον ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς μετὰ τὸν Εἱρμὸν λέγεται στίχος Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ ἀναστάσει σου Κύριε. Εἰς δὲ τὰ λοιπὰ Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ὁ προεόρτιος Κανὼν Χριστὸν σαρκὶ νηπιάσαντα, οὗ ὁ Στίχος Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Ὑπακοὴ Ἄγγελος παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον· ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον Χειρόγραφον εἰκόνα καὶ ὁ Οἶκος Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα. Εἶτα τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς· αἱ Καταβασίαι Χριστὸς γεννᾶται καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν. Ἐξαποστειλάρια, τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Πατέρων Πατέρων θείων σήμερον καὶ τὸ Προεόρτιον Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ σύ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ καὶ τὰ τροπάρια Ἄρόν σου τὴν φωνὴν ἀληθῶς εἰς δ΄. Δόξα Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος, Καὶ νῦν Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 9.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοί, Τροπάρια ἐκ τῆς γ΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῶν Πατέρων, καὶ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Προεορτίου. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τῶν Πατέρων, τὸ Προεόρτιον καὶ τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ. Κοντάκιον Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

Εἰς τὸ *Ἐξαιρέτως* *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Κοινωνικὸν *Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_incipit: Anavathmi, and the Prokimenon. The Canon
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Anavathmi, and the Prokimenon. The Canon “Waves of the sea.” The Verse of the first hymn of each Ode after the Irmos is “Glory to Your holy Resurrection, O Lord”; for the rest of the hymns we use the Verse “Saints of God.” Also the Canon of the Pre-feast “Christ being an infant in the flesh,” whose Verse is “Glory to You, our God, glory to You.” After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoi “An angel dampened the fire of the Children”; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion “Handwritten icon” and the Ikos “Stretch out Your hand.” Then the Minologion of the Saints of the day and the Postscript of the Sunday. The Katavasie “Christ is born,” and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing “More honorable.” Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers “Let us come together, O lovers of the Fathers,” and of the Pre-feast “Rejoice, O Bethlehem.” At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers “In truth raise your voice, O Zion,” Glory, “The collection of Mosaic teachings,” Now and ever, “Most blessed,” Great Doxology and “Today salvation.”
units.english_cohort_translation: Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canon: **"By the wave of the sea"** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*). The verse before the first Troparion of each Ode following the Heirmos is **"Glory to Thy holy Resurrection, O Lord"** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου, Κύριε*); for the remaining Troparia we chant the verse **"Saints of God, intercede for us"** (*Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρεσβεύσατε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν*); also the Forefeast Canon: **"Christ being an infant in the flesh"** (*Χριστὸν σαρκὶ νηπιάσαντα*), whose verse is **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι*). After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"** (*Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion: **"Refusing to worship the graven image"** (*Χειρόγραφον εἰκόνα μὴ σεβασθέντες*) and the Ikos: **"Stretch out Thy hand"** (*Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα*). Then the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day and the Hypomnema of the Sunday. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Fathers: **"Today let us praise the divine Fathers"** (*Πατέρων θείων σήμερον*), and that of the Forefeast: **"Rejoice, O Bethlehem, thou also"** (*Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ σύ*). At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 Troparia of the Fathers: **"In truth lift up thy voice, O Zion"** (*Ἆρόν σου τὴν φωνὴν ἀληθῶς*); **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of legal teachings"** (*Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe: **"An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"** (*Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον*); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion: **"Refusing to worship the graven image"** (*Χειρόγραφον εἰκόνα μὴ σεβασθέντες*) and the Ikos: **"Stretch out Thy hand"** (*Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα*). Then the Menaion Synaxarion of the Saints of the day and the Hypomnema of the Sunday. The Katavasiai: **"Christ is born, give ye glory"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*), and the entire order of the Sunday Morning Gospel. Then we sing biblical canticles with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: the Resurrection Exapostilarion, that of the Fathers: **"Today let us praise the divine Fathers"** (*Πατέρων θείων σήμερον*), and that of the Forefeast: **"Rejoice, O Bethlehem, thou also"** (*Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ σύ*). At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 Troparia of the Fathers: **"In truth lift up thy voice, O Zion"** (*Ἆρόν σου τὴν φωνὴν ἀληθῶς*); **"Glory"**: **"The assembly of legal teachings"** (*Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art Thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation has come into the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Anavathmi, and the Prokimenon. The Canon “Waves of the sea.” The Verse of the first hymn of each Ode after the Irmos is “Glory to Your holy Resurrection, O Lord”; for the rest of the hymns we use the Verse “Saints of God.” Also the Canon of the Pre-feast “Christ being an infant in the flesh,” whose Verse is “Glory to You, our God, glory to You.” After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoi “An angel dampened the fire of the Children”; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion “Handwritten icon” and the Ikos “Stretch out Your hand.” Then the Minologion of the Saints of the day and the Postscript of the Sunday. The Katavasie “Christ is born,” and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing “More honorable.” Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers “Let us come together, O lovers of the Fathers,” and of the Pre-feast “Rejoice, O Bethlehem.” At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers “In truth raise your voice, O Zion,” Glory, “The collection of Mosaic teachings,” Now and ever, “Most blessed,” Great Doxology and “Today salvation.”

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 9.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes from the 3rd Ode of the Canon of the Fathers, and from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Pre-feast. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Apolytikion, that of the Fathers, that of the Pre-feast, that of the Saint of the Church, Kontakion “Today the Virgin.” Apostolos and Gospel of the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ. At “Especially,” “It is meet,” Communion Hymn “Praise,” “We have seen the [true] light,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 9.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Typika, and Beatitudes consisting of Troparia from the Third Ode of the Canon of the Fathers and from the Sixth Ode of the Forefeast Canon. After the Little Entrance: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of the Fathers, that of the Forefeast, and that of the Patron Saint of the temple; Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ [Heb. 11:9–10, 32–40; Matt. 1:1–25]. At the Megalynarion: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: πρωΐας (7 π.μ.) κατέρχεται ὁ Πατριάρχης (ἢ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς) ἐν τῷ Ναῷ καὶ εὐλογήσαντος τοῦ Ἱερέως ἄρχεται ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι . . . Βασιλεῦ Οὐράνιε Παράκλητε . . . κτλ. ὁ Ἀναγνώστης λέγει τὸ Τρισάγιον, μετὰ δὲ τὸ Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν τὸ Κύριε ἐλέησον ιβ΄. Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν καὶ εὐθὺς τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς Α΄ ὥρας· εἰς τὸ τέλος Δόξα Πατρί, τὸ Τροπάριον Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε, Καὶ νῦν καὶ ἀεί, Τί σε καλέσωμεν, ὦ Κεχαριτωμένη; καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Βηθλεὲμ ἑτοιμάζου. Εἶτα ὁ β΄ Χορὸς τὸν Στίχον Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ Ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Νῦν προφητικὴ πρόρρησις, ὁ α΄ Χορὸς Δόξα, ὁ β΄ Καὶ νῦν, ὁ α΄ Τάδε λέγει Ἰωσὴφ πρὸς τὴν Παρθένον· μετὰ τοῦτο, ὁ α΄ Κανονάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ τὸν Ἀπόστολον, εἶτα ὁ Διάκονος Σοφία ὀρθοὶ κτλ. ὁ δὲ Ἱερεὺς πρὸ τῆς ὡραίας Πύλης ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ τὸ τέλος τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου ὁ Ἀναγνώστης εὐθὺς λέγει τὰ διαβήματά μου κατεύθυνον καὶ τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἱερεὺς Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον· τὸ Κύριε ἐλέησον μ΄, Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ, τὸ Κύριε ἐλέησον γ΄. Δόξα πατρί, Καὶ νῦν καὶ ἀεί, Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ, Ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ Ὁ Θεὸς οἰκτιρήσαι ἡμᾶς ἐπισυνάπτων καὶ τὴν εὐχὴν Χριστὲ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν, εἶτα ἄρχεται εὐθὺς ἡ Γ΄ Ὥρα.

units.english_cohort_translation: the Patriarch (or the Hierarch) descends into the nave of the temple, and the Priest having given the blessing, the Patriarch begins: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee... O Heavenly King, the Comforter..."** (*Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι... Βασιλεῦ Οὐράνιε, Παράκλητε...*), etc. The Reader says the Trisagion Prayers, and after the Priest's ecphonesis: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."** (*Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*), **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*), and immediately the appointed psalms of the First Hour [Psalms 5, 44, and 45 LXX]. At the conclusion: **"Glory to the Father..."**, the Troparion: **"Mary once, with aged Joseph, went to be enrolled"** (*Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε*); **"Both now and ever..."**, **"What shall we call thee, O thou who art full of grace?"** (*Τί σε καλέσωμεν, ὦ Κεχαριτωμένη;*). And the First Choir begins chanting the Idiomelon: **"Make ready, O Bethlehem"** (*Βηθλεὲμ ἑτοιμάζου*). Then the Second Choir chants the Verse: **"God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ Ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος*, Habakkuk 3:3 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"Now the prophetic utterance"** (*Νῦν προφητικὴ πρόρρησις*); the First Choir chants **"Glory to the Father..."**; the Second Choir chants **"Both now and ever..."**; the First Choir chants the Idiomelon: **"Joseph spoke thus unto the Virgin"** (*Τάδε λέγει Ἰωσὴφ πρὸς τὴν Παρθένον*). Following this, the First Canonarch reads the Old Testament Prophecy [Micah 5:2–4] and the Epistle [Hebrews 1:1–12]; then the Deacon intones: **"Wisdom! Let us attend!"** (*Σοφία, ὀρθοί*), etc., and the Priest reads the Holy Gospel [Matthew 1:18–25] before the Holy Doors. Following the Gospel, the Reader immediately recites: **"Order my steps in Thy word"** (*Τὰ διαβήματά μου κατεύθυνον*, Ps. 118:133 LXX) and the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest intones: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; then the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes unto the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*); **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times); **"Thou Who at all times and at every hour"** (*Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ*); **"Lord, have mercy"** (3 times); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*); **"In the name of the Lord, Father, bless"** (*Ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου*). The Patriarch recites: **"May God be gracious unto us and bless us"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς οἰκτιρήσαι ἡμᾶς*), joining also the prayer: **"O Christ, the true light"** (*Χριστὲ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν*). Then immediately begins the Third Hour.

units.english_cohort_translation: *Note.* While the Idiomela of the Third Hour are being chanted, the Great Archdeacon (or the Deacon, or in their absence the Priest who read the Holy Gospel) comes forth from the North Door of the Sanctuary dressed in a black mandyas, bearing a katzion [hand-censer] and preceded by a Lambadouchos [taper-bearer], and censes the people. This is likewise repeated during the remaining two Hours—the Sixth and the Ninth—by other Deacons. (In the absence of a Hierarch, the Priest censes robed in a phelonion).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: a.m.} the Patriarch (or the Archpriest) comes down into the Church, and the Priest having given the blessing, the Patriarch begins “Glory to You our God, glory to you . . . O heavenly King . . . etc.” The Reader says the Trisagion, and after “For Yours is,” “Lord, have mercy (12 times). Glory, Now and ever, “O come let us worship,” and the psalms of the First Hour; at the end Glory the Hymn “Mary once,” Now and ever, “What shall we call you, O full of grace?” and The first Choir chants the Idiomelon “Make ready, O Bethlehem.” Then the second Choir sings the Verse “God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed by the forest” (Habakkuk 3:3) and the Idiomelon “Now the prophecy,” the first Choir Glory, the second Choir Now and ever the first “Joseph spoke thus to the Virgin.” After this, the Canonarch reads the Prophecy and the Apostolos; then the Deacon “Wisdom arise” etc. and the Priest, before the Royal Gate, reads the Gospel. After the Gospel, the Reader immediately says: “Order my steps” and the Trisagion; the Priest “For Yours is,” and the Kontakion “Today the Virgin”; then “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “You who at every season,” “Lord, have mercy” (3 times) Glory, Now and ever, “More honorable than the Cherubim” and “In the name of the Lord.” Then the Patriarch says the “May God have pity for us” adding also the prayer “Christ the true light”; then begins immediately the 3rd hour.

units.slavonic_incipit: Ἰδιόμελον Ἰωσὴφ εἰπὲ ἡμῖν. Εἶτα λέγεται

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    Ὁ Ἀναγνώστης μετὰ τὸ Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν, ἀναγινώσκει τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς ς΄ Ὥρας καὶ μετὰ τὸ Ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν παρρησίαν, ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως, εἶτα ὁ β΄ Χορὸς τὸν Στίχον Κύριε εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Ἄκουε Οὐρανὲ, ὁ α΄ Χορὸς Δόξα Καὶ νῦν, ὁ β΄ καὶ α΄ Χορὸς τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Δεῦτε Χριστοφόροι λαοὶ, μετὰ τοῦτο ὁ Κανονάρχης τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ τὸν Ἀπόστολον, καὶ ὁ Ἱερεὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ δὲ τὴν εὐχὴν τῆς ς΄ Ὥρας Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων, ἄρχεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὥρα.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    Ὁ Ἀναγνώστης μετὰ τὸ *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*, ἀναγινώσκει τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς ς΄ Ὥρας καὶ μετὰ τὸ *Ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν παρρησίαν*, ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως*, εἶτα ὁ β΄ Χορὸς τὸν Στίχον *Κύριε εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην* καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Ἄκουε Οὐρανὲ*, ὁ α΄ Χορὸς *Δόξα* *Καὶ νῦν*, ὁ β΄ καὶ α΄ Χορὸς τὸ Ἰδιόμελον *Δεῦτε Χριστοφόροι λαοὶ*, μετὰ τοῦτο ὁ Κανονάρχης τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ τὸν Ἀπόστολον, καὶ ὁ Ἱερεὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ δὲ τὴν εὐχὴν τῆς ς΄ Ὥρας *Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*, ἄρχεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὥρα.

Ὁ Ἀναγνώστης Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν γ΄ καὶ τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς Θ΄ Ὥρας· μετὰ δὲ τὸ Ὁ δι’ ἡμᾶς γεννηθείς, ἄρχεται ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Ἐξεπλήττετο ὁ Ἡρώδης, εἶτα ὁ α΄ Χορὸς τὸν Στίχον Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Ὅτε Ἰωσὴφ, Παρθένε, τὸ τέλος τοῦ Ἰδιομέλου Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι λαμβάνει ὁ β΄ Χορὸς· ὁ δὲ α΄ ἄρχεται τοῦ Δόξα πατρὶ, ὁ β΄ Χορὸς λέγει τὸ Καὶ νῦν ὁ δὲ Κανονάρχης ἱστάμενος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ βλέπων πρὸς ἀνατολὰς ἀναγινώσκει εὐλαβῶς καὶ κατὰ τὸ ὕφος τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχων κτίσιν, ὃ ἐπαναλαμβάνει τρὶς, εἶτα ἐξακολουθεῖ Ῥάκει καθάπερ βροτὸς κτλ., τὸ δὲ Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὴν γέννησιν Χριστὲ ἐπαναλαμβάνει ἐπίσης τρὶς, τὸ Δεῖξον ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ θεῖά σου θεοφάνεια ἅπαξ, καὶ τότε ἄρχονται οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλειν τὸ Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ἀργῶς καὶ μετὰ μέλους· μετὰ τοῦτο ὁ Κανονάρχης λέγει τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ τὸν Ἀπόστολον καὶ ὁ Ἱερεὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ δὲ τὴν Εὐχὴν τῆς Θ΄ Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ, γίνεται Ἀπόλυσις³. καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ Μέγας Ἑσπερινὸς μετὰ τῆς Λειτουργίας τοῦ Μεγάλου Βασιλείου.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    The Reader, after “O Come, let us worship,” reads the psalms of the 6th Hour and after “As there is no boldness in us,” the first Choir chants the Idiomelon “Come, O you faithful, inspired by God.” Then the second Choir chants the Verse “Lord, I have heard the report of You and was afraid” and the Idiomelon “Hearken, O heaven”; the first Choir Glory, the second Choir Now and ever then the first Choir the Idiomelon “Come you people, bearers of Christ.” After this the Canonarch reads the Prophecy and the Apostolos, and the Priest reads the Gospel; after the Prayer of the 6th Hour “O God the Lord of hosts,” the 9th Hour begins.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    The Reader, after **"O come, let us worship"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*), reads the psalms of the Sixth Hour [Psalms 71, 131, and 90 LXX]; and after **"Forasmuch as we have no boldness"** (*Ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν παρρησίαν*), the First Choir begins chanting the Idiomelon: **"Come, ye faithful, let us be inspired divinely"** (*Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως*). Then the Second Choir chants the Verse: **"O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid"** (*Κύριε, εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου καὶ ἐφοβήθην*, Habakkuk 3:2 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth"** (*Ἄκουε, οὐρανέ*); the First Choir chants **"Glory to the Father... Both now and ever..."**; then the Second and First Choirs together chant the Idiomelon: **"Come, ye Christ-bearing peoples"** (*Δεῦτε, χριστοφόροι λαοί*). After this, the Canonarch reads the Old Testament Prophecy [Isaiah 7:10–16; 8:1–4, 9–10] and the Epistle [Hebrews 2:11–18], and the Priest reads the Holy Gospel [Matthew 2:1–12]. After the Prayer of the Sixth Hour: **"O God and Lord of powers"** (*Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*), the Ninth Hour begins.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 5.    The Reader, after “O Come, let us worship” (3 times), reads the psalms of the 9th Hour; after “O good Lord, for our sakes you were born of a Virgin,” the second Choir chants the Idiomelon “Herod was struck with amazement,” then the first Choir the Verse “God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed by the forest” and the Idiomelon “O Virgin, when Joseph”; the second Choir sings the conclusion of the hymn “With the Father and the Holy Spirit”; the first Choir begins Glory, the second Choir says Now and ever. Then, the Canonarch, standing in the middle of the Church and looking towards the East, recites piously and with the style of the Gospel [recitative] the Idiomelon “Today is born of a Virgin he who holds the whole creation” (3 times); he then continues “He is wrapped in swaddling” etc. The Verse “We worship your birth O Christ” (3 times) and then “Show us also your divine Epiphany” (once). Then the Choirs chant “Today is born of a Virgin” slowly and with melody. After this the Canonarch recites the Prophecy and the Apostolos, and the Priest recites the Gospel; after the Prayer of the 9th Hour “O Master and Lord, Jesus Christ,” follows the Dismissal.³ Then the Great Vespers with the Liturgy of Basil the Great begins.
units.english_cohort_translation: 5.    The Reader recites **"O come, let us worship"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν*) thrice and reads the psalms of the Ninth Hour [Psalms 109, 110, and 85 LXX]; and after **"He Who for our sake was born of a Virgin"** (*Ὁ δι’ ἡμᾶς γεννηθείς*), the Second Choir begins chanting the Idiomelon: **"Herod was struck with amazement"** (*Ἐξεπλήττετο ὁ Ἡρώδης*). Then the First Choir chants the Verse: **"God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ Ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος*, Habakkuk 3:3 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"When Joseph, O Virgin, was wounded with sorrow"** (*Ὅτε Ἰωσήφ, Παρθένε*); the Second Choir takes up the conclusion of the Idiomelon: **"Together with the Father and the Holy Spirit"** (*Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι*); the First Choir begins **"Glory to the Father..."**; the Second Choir says **"Both now and ever..."**. Then the Canonarch, standing in the midst of the nave and facing eastward, recites reverently in the cantillation style of the Gospel the Idiomelon: **"Today He Who holds all creation in the hollow of His hand is born of a Virgin"** (*Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχων κτίσιν*), repeating it thrice; he then continues: **"He Who in essence cannot be touched is wrapped in swaddling clothes as a mortal..."** (*Ῥάκει καθάπερ βροτὸς*), etc.; he likewise repeats thrice: **"We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ"** (*Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὴν γέννησιν, Χριστέ*), and once: **"Show us also Thy divine Theophany"** (*Δεῖξον ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ θεῖά σου Θεοφάνεια*). And then the Choirs begin chanting **"Today He is born of a Virgin"** (*Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου*) slowly and solemnly with melody. Following this, the Canonarch reads the Old Testament Prophecy [Isaiah 9:6–7] and the Epistle [Hebrews 2:1–10], and the Priest reads the Holy Gospel [Matthew 2:13–23]. After the Prayer of the Ninth Hour: **"O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God"** (*Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ*), the Dismissal takes place.³ And Great Vespers joined with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great begins.

Then the First Choir chants the Verse: **"God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει, καὶ ὁ Ἅγιος ἐξ ὄρους κατασκίου δασέος*, Habakkuk 3:3 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"When Joseph, O Virgin, was wounded with sorrow"** (*Ὅτε Ἰωσήφ, Παρθένε*); the Second Choir takes up the conclusion of the Idiomelon: **"Together with the Father and the Holy Spirit"** (*Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι*); the First Choir begins **"Glory to the Father..."**; the Second Choir says **"Both now and ever..."**. Then the Canonarch, standing in the midst of the nave and facing eastward, recites reverently in the cantillation style of the Gospel the Idiomelon: **"Today He Who holds all creation in the hollow of His hand is born of a Virgin"** (*Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν

After the Prayer of the 9th [Hour] the order calls for the Typika to be read, that is, “Bless the Lord, O my soul” [Psalm 102 LXX, 103 RSV] “Praise the Lord” [Psalm 145 LXX, 146 RSV] the Beatitudes and finally the Dismissal. units.english_cohort_translation: *Note.* After the Prayer of the Ninth Hour, the liturgical order prescribes the Typika recited plain—namely, **"Bless the Lord, O my soul"** [Psalm 102 LXX], **"Praise the Lord, O my soul"** [Psalm 145 LXX], the Beatitudes, and finally the Dismissal. But because, for the sake of brevity, it has already become customary to omit them, for this reason the Dismissal is noted above immediately following the Prayer.[^199]

Ὁ Διάκονος Εὐλόγησον Δέσποτα, ὁ Ἱερεὺς Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία, ὁ Πατριάρχης (ἢ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς) τὸν Προοιμιακὸν, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ δ΄ Ἰδιόμελα Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ς΄. Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, Εἴσοδος μετὰ Εὐαγγελίου, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Κανονάρχης τὸ Α΄ Ἀνάγνωσμα Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, μετὰ τὸ τέλος ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλειν τὸ Τροπάριον Λαθὼν ἐτέχθης καὶ ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ἐπαναλαμβάνει Καὶ μάγους σοι προσήνεγκεν· τὸ αὐτὸ ἐπαναλαμβάνουσιν ἑκατέρωθεν οἱ Χοροὶ, ἕως οὗ ὁ Κανονάρχης πληρώσῃ τοὺς Στίχους τοῦ ψαλμοῦ· εἶτα ὁ α΄ Χορὸς Δόξα Καὶ νῦν καὶ ψάλλει αὖθις τὸ Τροπάριον ὁλόκληρον. Ἀκολούθως ὁ β΄ Κανονάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Ζ΄ Ἀνάγνωσμα Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν, μετὰ τὸ τέλος ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ψάλλει τὸ Τροπάριον Ἀνέτειλας Χριστὲ ἐκ Παρθένου, τὸ τέλος δὲ καὶ τούτου Μάγους ὁδηγήσας ἐπαναλαμβάνεται ὑπὸ τῶν δύο Χορῶν, ἕως οὗ ὁ Κανονάρχης πληρώσῃ τοὺς Στίχους τοῦ ψαλμοῦ ὡς ἀνωτέρω· εἶτα ὁ β΄ Χορὸς Δόξα Καὶ νῦν ἐπαναλαμβάνων ὁλόκληρον τὸ Τροπάριον, καὶ ὁ α΄ Κανονάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Η΄ Ἀνάγνωσμα Προέθετο Κύριος λαλῆσαι τῷ Ἄχαζ· μετὰ ταῦτα ἡ μικρὰ Συναπτὴ Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν κτλ. καὶ ψάλλεται ὁ Τρισάγιος ὕμνος, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον ἀπ’ Ἄμβωνος ὑπὸ τοῦ Διακόνου· μετὰ τὸ τέλος ὁ Πατριάρχης (ἢ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς) εὐλογεῖ τὸν λαὸν, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη· εἰδεμὴ, λέγεται τὸ, Δόξα σοι Κύριε, Δόξα σοι καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ Λειτουργία τοῦ Μ. Βασιλείου, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς ⁴ καὶ ἡ Ἀπόλυσις μετὰ τοῦ Ὁ ἐν σπηλαίῳ γεννηθεὶς καὶ ἐν φάτνῃ ἀνακληθεὶς διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινός . . . .
