units.slavonic_diplomatic: 6.    The Deacon: “Bless Master”; the Priest: “Blessed is the Kingdom”; the Patriarch (or the Archpriest): the Introductory Psalm. At “Lord, I have cried” we sing the 4 Idiomela “Come, let us greatly rejoice in the Lord” in 6 (i.e., repeat the first two). Glory, Now and ever, “When Augustus reigned alone on earth.” Entrance with the Gospel, “O Gladsome Light,” and immediately the Canonarch recites the First Reading “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” At the end, the first Choir sings the Hymn “You were born secretly in a cave,” and the second Choir repeats the refrain “And it brought to you the Magi”; this is repeated by each of the Choirs until the Canonarch has completed the verses of the Psalm; then the first Choir Glory, Now and ever and sings the entire hymn. Then the second Canonarch reads the 7th Reading “For unto us a child is born”; at the end the second Choir sings the Hymn “You have shone forth from a Virgin”; the refrain “You have led the Magi” is repeated by both Choirs until the Canonarch completes the Verses of the psalm as above; then the second Choir Glory, Now and ever and the entire hymn is repeated. Then the first Canonarch reads the 8th Reading “The Lord spoke again to Ahaz”; after this the small Litany “Let us pray to the Lord” etc., and the Trisagios Hymn is sung; the Apostolos, the Alleluia, and the Gospel recited by the Deacon, follows from the Pulpit.
units.english_cohort_translation: 6.    The Deacon: **"Master, bless"** (*Εὐλόγησον, Δέσποτα*); the Priest: **"Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit"** (*Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία*); the Patriarch (or the Hierarch) recites the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX]. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing the 4 Idiomela: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ*) in 6 (repeating the first two). **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"When Augustus reigned alone upon the earth"** (*Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς*). Entrance is made with the Holy Gospel; **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and immediately the Canonarch intones the First Old Testament Reading: **"In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth"** (*Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν*, Genesis 1:1–13). At the conclusion, the First Choir begins chanting the Troparion: **"Having been born secretly in a cave"** (*Λαθὼν ἐτέχθης ὑπὸ τὸ σπήλαιον*), and the Second Choir responds with the refrain: **"And brought the Magi unto Thee"** (*Καὶ μάγους σοι προσήνεγκεν*); this same refrain the Choirs repeat alternately on each side until the Canonarch completes the verses of the Psalm; then the First Choir chants **"Glory... Both now and ever..."** and sings the entire Troparion again from the beginning. Thereupon the Second Canonarch reads the Seventh Reading: **"A Child is born unto us, a Son is given unto us"** (*Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν*, Isaiah 9:6–7); at the conclusion, the Second Choir chants the Troparion: **"Thou didst dawn forth, O Christ, from a Virgin"** (*Ἀνέτειλας Χριστὲ ἐκ Παρθένου*), and the conclusion thereof: **"Having guided the Magi by a star"** (*Μάγους ὁδηγήσας*) is repeated by both Choirs until the Canonarch completes the verses of the Psalm as above; then the Second Choir chants **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, repeating the entire Troparion; and the First Canonarch reads the Eighth Reading: **"The Lord spoke again to Ahaz"** (*Προέθετο Κύριος λαλῆσαι τῷ Ἄχαζ*, Isaiah 7:10–16; 8:1–4, 9–10). After these readings, the Little Litany: **"Let us pray to the Lord"** (*Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*), etc., and the Trisagion Hymn is sung; then the Epistle [Hebrews 1:1–12], the Alleluia [Ps. 109:1 LXX], and the Holy Gospel [Luke 2:1–20] proclaimed from the Ambo by the Deacon. At the conclusion, the Patriarch (or the Hierarch) blesses the people, the Choirs chanting: **"Many years, Master"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, Δέσποτα*); otherwise, there is said: **"Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι, Κύριε, δόξα σοι*), and the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great follows in order; Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and the Dismissal with the proper festal incipit: **"May He Who was born in a cave and lay in a manger for our salvation, Christ our true God..."** (*Ὁ ἐν σπηλαίῳ γεννηθεὶς καὶ ἐν φάτνῃ ἀνακληθεὶς διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ γέννησίς σου ἐκ τρίτου, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος Αἰνεῖτε τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου, τὰ γ΄ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ, τὸ α΄ Ἀντίφωνον τοῦ δ΄ Ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε, ὤμοσε Κύριος καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται, τὸ Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, εἶτα ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, Δόξα Τὰ σύμπαντα σήμερον χαρᾶς πληροῦνται, Καὶ νῦν τὸ αὐτό, Στίχος Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεὸς καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ (ζήτει ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τῆς ΚΣΤ΄). Οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἀνὰ δ΄ Τροπάρια ἄνευ Στίχων, εἰς τὰ δύο τελευταῖα Δόξα Καὶ νῦν· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ χῦμα, ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἑορτῆς· αἱ Καταβασίαι διπλαῖ μέχρις η΄ Ὠδῆς, εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων ὡς ἑξῆς·

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Lord”: the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ” (3 times), then the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos “Praise the Name of the Lord” (Psalm 134 LXX, 135 RSV). The three Kathismata are sung in order, the Anavathmi, the first Antiphon of Mode IV, and the Prokimenon “From the womb before the morning star have I begotten you, the lord has sworn and will not repent”; then, “Let everything that has breath” and the Gospel, then Psalm 50 read, Glory, “All things are filled with joy today,” Now and ever repeat the same. The Verse “Have mercy upon me O God” and the Idiomelon “Glory to God in the highest” (this is the Glory of the Vespers of December 26). Both Canons with four hymns each without Verses but at the last two hymns the Verse Glory, Now and ever. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoi (read); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion, the Ikos and the Minologion of the Feast. The two Katavasie until the 8th Ode; then the 9th Ode with the Megalynaria is sung as follows:
units.english_cohort_translation: Lord" (*Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*) thrice; then the daily Psalter and the Polyeleos: **"Praise ye the name of the Lord"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, Psalms 134–135 LXX). The three Kathismata are sung in order; the Anavathmoi: the First Antiphon of Tone 4; and the Prokeimenon in Tone 4: **"From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee; the Lord hath sworn, and will not repent"** (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε, ὤμοσε Κύριος καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται*, Ps. 109:3–4 LXX); then **"Let every breath praise the Lord"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*) and the Matins Gospel [Matthew 1:18–25]; then Psalm 50 [LXX] recited plain; **"Glory"**: **"All things are filled with joy today"** (*Τὰ σύμπαντα σήμερον χαρᾶς πληροῦνται*); **"Both now and ever"**: repeat the same. The Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy"** (*Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός*, Ps. 50:1 LXX) and the Idiomelon: **"Glory to God in the highest"** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*, look at Vespers of December 26). Both Canons are sung with four Troparia each without verses, but at the last two Troparia we chant the verse **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**. After the Third Ode: the Hypakoe (recited plain) [**"The heavens brought an offering"** / *Τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν*]; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes to the cave"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*), the Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Feast. The double Katavasiai are sung through the Eighth Ode; then the Ninth Ode is sung with the Megalynaria as follows:

The Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy"** (*Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός*, Ps. 50:1 LXX) and the Idiomelon: **"Glory to God in the highest"** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*, look at Vespers of December 26). Both Canons are sung with four Troparia each without verses, but at the last two Troparia we chant the verse **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**. units.slavonic_incipit: Εἰσοδικὸν Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Εἰσοδικὸν Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ γέννησίς σου, τὸ Κοντάκιον Ἡ παρθένος σήμερον τὸν Ὑπερούσιον τίκτει, ἀντὶ τοῦ Τρισαγίου τὸ Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 9.    Τῇ αὐτῇ Παρασκευῇ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ Ἰδιόμελα τῆς ἑορτῆς Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα εἰς ς΄. Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Δόξα ἐν Ὑψίστοις Θεῷ, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Μέγα Προκείμενον Τίς Θεὸς μέγας μετὰ τῶν στίχων αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ Ἰδιόμελα Παράδοξον Μυστήριον καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ β΄. units.slavonic_diplomatic: With You is dominion in the day of Your power: in the beauties of Your saints.
units.english_cohort_translation: Introit (Entrance Hymn): **"From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee"** (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε*, Ps. 109:3 LXX). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto Him Who is transcendent in essence"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν Ὑπερούσιον τίκτει*); instead of the Trisagion: **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*, Gal. 3:27). The Epistle [Galatians 4:4–7] and the Holy Gospel [Matthew 2:1–12]. At the Megalynarion: **"Magnify, O my soul... A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold"** (*Μυστήριον ξένον*). Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people. Alleluia"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε Κύριος τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 110:9 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 9.    On that Friday evening after the Introductory Psalm, at “Lord, I have cried” we sing the 4 Idiomela of the Feast “Come, let us greatly rejoice in the Lord” in 6 (i.e., repeat the first two). Glory, Now and ever “Glory to God in the highest.” Entrance, “O Gladsome Light,” and the Great Prokimenon “Who is so great a God” with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Idiomela “A marvelous wonder” and the other two. Glory, Now and ever, “The shepherds hastened to Bethlehem.” The Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ” (3 times), and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 9.    On that same Friday evening, after the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing the 4 Idiomela of the Feast: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*) in 6 (repeating the first two). **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"Glory to God in the highest"** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*). Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Great Prokeimenon in Tone 7: **"Who is so great a God as our God? Thou art the God Who doest wonders"** (*Τίς Θεὸς μέγας ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν; Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια*, Ps. 76:14 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Idiomela: **"A marvelous mystery"** (*Παράδοξον μυστήριον*) and the other two; **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"In Bethlehem the shepherds hastened"** (*Ἐν Βηθλεὲμ συνέδραμον ποιμένες*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (thrice), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: ψαλμὸς χῦμα· οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἄνευ
units.slavonic_diplomatic: ψαλμὸς χῦμα· οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἄνευ Στίχων ὡς χθές, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον Ὁ πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου Πατρὸς ἐκλάμψας, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι Ἔσωσε λαὸν καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ τῶν δύο Κανόνων μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ ἡ Καταβασία Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς ἐκ τρίτου. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ δ΄ Ἰδιόμελα Εὐφραίνεσθε δίκαιοι, Δόξα, Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις Καὶ νῦν Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς, (μέχρι τοῦ ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀκαταπαύστως βοῶμεν, καὶ ἄρχεται εὐθὺς ἡ) Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ γέννησίς σου.
units.english_cohort_translation: ψαλμὸς χῦμα· οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἄνευ Στίχων ὡς χθές, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον *Ὁ πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου Πατρὸς ἐκλάμψας*, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι *Ἔσωσε λαὸν* καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ τῶν δύο Κανόνων μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ ἡ Καταβασία *Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον *Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς* ἐκ τρίτου. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ δ΄ Ἰδιόμελα *Εὐφραίνεσθε δίκαιοι*, *Δόξα*, *Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις* *Καὶ νῦν* *Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς*, (μέχρι τοῦ *ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀκαταπαύστως βοῶμεν*, καὶ ἄρχεται εὐθὺς ἡ) Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 12.    Τῷ αὐτῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τῶν Θεοπατόρων τὸν Θεοπάτορα πάντες γ΄ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Στεφάνου γ΄, Δόξα Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, Δόξα τοῦ Ἁγίου Πρῶτος ἐν Μάρτυσιν ἐδείχθης, Καὶ νῦν Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ Ἁγίου, τὸ Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Ypakoi read; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion “He who before the morning star,” the Ikos and the Minologion of the Feast. The Katavasie “He saved the people” then the 9th Ode of both Canons with their Megalynaria and the Katavasia “It would be easier for us.” The Exapostilarion “Our Saviour visited us,” (3 times). At the Praises: the 4 Idiomela “Make glad, O you righteous,” Glory, “Today the invisible nature,” Now and ever, “Today Christ” until “we cry aloud without ceasing: Glory to God in the highest, and on Earth Peace, Good Will Among Men. { Note: the last line of the above Theotokion is sung by the Choir as the first line of the Great Doxology after which we sing the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ”}.
units.english_cohort_translation: Hypakoe recited plain; after the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion: **"He Who was begotten of the Father before the morning star"** (*Ὁ πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου Πατρὸς ἐκλάμψας*), the Ikos, and the Synaxarion of the Feast. The Katavasiai: **"He saved the people"** (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*); then the Ninth Ode of both Canons with their Megalynaria, and the Katavasia: **"Easier for us would it be"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*). The Exapostilarion: **"Our Savior, the Dayspring from on high, hath visited us"** (*Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς*) thrice. At the Praises: the 4 Idiomela: **"Be glad, O ye righteous"** (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); **"Glory"**: **"Today the invisible nature"** (*Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today Christ is born in Bethlehem of the Virgin"** (*Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς*) up to the cue words **"and we cry aloud without ceasing: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men."** (Note: the concluding phrase of the above Theotokion is sung by the choir as the opening proclamation of the Great Doxology); after which we sing the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 11.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast as yesterday. Entrance Hymn “From the womb before the morning star have I begotten You.” The Apolytikion “Your Nativity,” and the Kontakion “Today the Virgin gives birth to Him who is above all essence.” Instead of the Trisagios Hymn, “As many as have been baptized.” The Apostolos of the Saturday after Christmas “My son Timothy, flee these things” [Note: The Typikon has “Titus”; this is a typographical error because the citation is 1 Timothy 6:11-16]. The Gospel “At that time, a large crowd followed Jesus” [Matthew 12:15-21]. At “Especially,” “Magnify, O my soul . . . It would be easier for us.” Communion Hymn “The Lord has sent deliverance,” the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ,” and Dismissal.⁵ Sunday After Christmas, and the Holy Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen.
units.english_cohort_translation: 11.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Antiphons of the Feast as yesterday. Introit (Entrance Hymn): **"From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee"** (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε*, Ps. 109:3 LXX). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto Him Who is transcendent in essence"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). Instead of the Trisagion: **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*, Gal. 3:27). The Epistle of the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ: **"O my son Timothy, follow after righteousness"** (*Τέκνον Τιμόθεε, δίωκε δικαιοσύνην*, 1 Tim. 6:11–16; note: the Greek text has "Titus", which is a typographical error for 1 Timothy 6:11–16); and the Holy Gospel likewise: **"At that time, great multitudes followed Jesus"** (*Τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ὄχλοι πολλοί*, Matt. 12:15–21). At the Megalynarion: **"Magnify, O my soul... Easier for us would it be"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*). Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people. Alleluia"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε Κύριος τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 110:9 LXX); the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 12.    In Vespers on Saturday evening following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at “Lord, I have cried” we sing 4 Stichira of the Resurrection, 3 of the Fathers “Come, let us extol David the king,” and 3 of Saint Stephen; Glory, “Let us commemorate,” Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode. Entrance, “O Gladsome Light” and the Prokimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory of the Saint “You were the first in martyrdom,” Now and ever, “Today all the angels.” The Apolytikia: of the Resurrection, of Saint Stephen, of the Fathers “Proclaim, O Joseph,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: *Note.* On other days (that is, outside the occurrence of this Feast on a Saturday or Sunday), the Epistle read is: **"Brethren, both He that sanctifies and they who are sanctified are all of one"** (*Ἀδελφοί, ὁ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι*, Heb. 2:11–18); and the Holy Gospel: **"When the wise men had departed"** (*Ἀναχωρησάντων τῶν Μάγων*, Matt. 2:13–23).

On that same Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX] and the First Kathisma of the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Holy Forefathers [David, Joseph, and James]: **"Come, let us all praise the Ancestor of God"** (*Τὸν θεοπάτορα πάντες*), and 3 of Saint Stephen; **"Glory"**: **"Let us celebrate the memory"** (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance with the censer: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; **"Glory"** of the Saint: **"Thou wast shown to be the first among martyrs"** (*Πρῶτος ἐν Μάρτυσιν ἐδείχθης*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The Angels dance in chorus"** (*Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion, that of Saint Stephen, that of the Holy Forefathers: **"Proclaim the wonders, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), and Dismissal.[^204]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 13.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ γέννησίς σου Χριστὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος. Τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ ἀνὰ ἓν τῆς ἑορτῆς ἀντὶ τῶν Θεοτοκίων, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μνήστορος Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε μετὰ Στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, καὶ τὸ Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν, ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν, αἱ Καταβασίαι Ἔσωσε λαὸν καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τοῦ ἁγίου Στεφάνου, τὸ τοῦ Μνήστορος Σὺν Ἰακώβῳ μέλψωμεν καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου δ΄, Δόξα Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ, Καὶ νῦν Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μνήστορος Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε μετὰ Στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, καὶ τὸ Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν, ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν, αἱ Καταβασίαι Ἔσωσε λαὸν καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 13.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon, and the Triadic “It is meet”; then the Trisagion, the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ our God,” and the Exapsalmos. At “God is the Lord”: the Apolytikia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Resurrection Kathismata and one of the Feast for each of the Theotokia; the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon. The Canons of the Resurrection and of the Betrothed [Saint Joseph] “Blessed servant of Christ” with the Verse “Holy one of God.” After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma “As a true Father,” that of the Saint, and “The chorus of Prophets”; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion “Of joy today,” and Ikos, and the Minologion of the Saint and the Postscript of the Sunday after the Nativity.
units.english_cohort_translation: 13.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Triadic hymns: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Resurrectional Kathismata, and one of the Feast in place of each Theotokion; the Resurrectional Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: of the Resurrection, and of the Betrothed [Saint Joseph]: **"Blessed servant of Christ"** (*Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε*) with the Verse: **"Holy righteous one of God, pray to God for us"** (*Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ*). After the Third Ode: the Kathisma: **"As a true Father"** (*Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*), that of the Saint, and **"The chorus of Prophets"** (*Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion: **"Of joy today"** (*Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the Saint, and the Synaxarion notice of the Sunday after the Nativity. The Katavasiai: **"He saved the people"** (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*), and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we chant: **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of Saint Stephen, of the Betrothed: **"With James let us sing"** (*Σὺν Ἰακώβῳ μέλψωμεν*), and that of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrectional Stichira and 4 of the Saint; **"Glory"**: **"Blood and fire, and vapor of smoke"** (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art thou"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation is come unto the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.english_cohort_translation: 14.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone, and 4 hymns from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Betrothed. After the Entrance: **"Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ. O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead..."** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Fathers: **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), that of the Saint, that of the Temple Patron, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle of the Saint [Acts 6:8–7:5, 47–60] and the Gospel: **"When the Magi had departed"** (*Ἀναχωρησάντων τῶν Μάγων*, Matthew 2:13–23). At **"Especially"**: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 18.    Τῷ αὐτῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τῆς ἑορτῆς Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα γ΄ καὶ τῶν Θεοπατόρων γ΄. Δόξα Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν, Καὶ νῦν Δόξα ἐν Ὑψίστοις θεῷ. Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Μ. Προκείμενον Τίς θεὸς μέγας μετὰ τῶν στίχων αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά. Δόξα Ἱερέων μνήμη, Καὶ νῦν Ἐν Βηθλεὲμ συνέδραμον ποιμένες, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, Δόξα Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ, Καὶ νῦν Ἡ γέννησίς σου Χριστὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
units.english_cohort_translation: 18.    Τῷ αὐτῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τῆς ἑορτῆς *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα* γ΄ καὶ τῶν Θεοπατόρων γ΄. *Δόξα* *Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Δόξα ἐν Ὑψίστοις θεῷ*. Εἴσοδος, *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* καὶ τὸ Μ. Προκείμενον *Τίς θεὸς μέγας* μετὰ τῶν στίχων αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά. *Δόξα* *Ἱερέων μνήμη*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ἐν Βηθλεὲμ συνέδραμον ποιμένες*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, *Δόξα* *Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Ἡ γέννησίς σου Χριστὲ ὁ θεὸς* καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 19.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ γέννησίς σου καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινόν· εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος· τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ ἀνὰ ἓν τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον, Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος, καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μνήστορος Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε μετὰ Στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ θεοῦ. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον μετὰ τοῦ Οἴκου, εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς, Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν. Ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν· αἱ Καταβασίαι Ἔσωσε λαὸν καὶ

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 18.    That Saturday evening after the Introductory Psalm, at “Lord, I have cried” we sing the 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 Idiomela of the Feast “Come, let us rejoice in the Lord” and 3 of the Fathers. Glory, “Let us commemorate,” Now and ever, “Glory to God in the highest.” Entrance, “O Gladsome Light” and the Great Prokimenon “Who is so great a God” with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira. Glory, “The commemoration of priests,” Now and ever, “The shepherds hastened to Bethlehem.” The Apolytikia of the Resurrection, Glory “Proclaim, O Joseph,” Now and ever, “Your birth, O Christ,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: **The Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos and the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ** 18.    That Saturday evening, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrectional Stichira, 3 Idiomela of the Feast: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ*), and 3 of the Ancestors of God. **"Glory"**: **"Let us celebrate the memory"** (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Glory to God in the highest"** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*). Entrance, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Great Prokeimenon: **"Who is so great a god as our God?"** (*Τίς Θεὸς μέγας ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν;*, Ps. 76:14 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"The memory of the priests"** (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The shepherds hastened together to Bethlehem"** (*Ἐν Βηθλεὲμ συνέδραμον ποιμένες*). The Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion; **"Glory"**: **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ τῶν δύο κανόνων τῆς ἑορτῆς μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ ἡ Καταβασία Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 20.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς, εἰς τὸ β΄ Ἀντίφωνον ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου τεχθείς. Εἰς τὴν Εἴσοδον Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ γέννησίς σου Χριστέ, Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσήφ, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, ἀντὶ τοῦ Τρισαγίου, τὸ Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε. Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Μεγαλυνον ψυχή μου . . . Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς, Κοινωνικὸν Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε, τὸ Ἡ γέννησίς σου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.english_cohort_translation: saved the people" (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*), and the entire order of the Morning Gospel; then we sing the Ninth Ode of both Canons with their Megalynaria and the Katavasia: **"It would be easier for us"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*). Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Ancestors of God: **"With James let us sing"** (*Σὺν Ἰακώβῳ μέλψωμεν*), and of the Afterfeast: **"Be cleansed and approach"** (*Καθάρθητε, προσέλθετε*). [*Note.* This Exapostilarion is not found in the Menaion, which repeatedly indicates in this place the Exapostilarion of the Feast: **"Our Savior, the Dayspring from on high, hath visited us"** (*Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς*).] At the Praises: 4 Resurrectional Stichira and 4 of the Feast: **"Be glad, O ye righteous"** (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); **"Glory"**: **"Blood and fire, and vapor of smoke"** (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today the invisible nature"** (*Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation is come unto the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 20.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast, at the 2nd Antiphon “...born of a Virgin.” Entrance Hymn “Come let us worship . . . who is risen from the dead.” Apolytikia: The Resurrection Apolytikion, “Your birth, O Christ,” “Proclaim, O Joseph,” that of the Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion “The Virgin today.” Instead of the Trisagios Hymn, “As many as have been baptized.” The Apostolos and Gospel of the Sunday after The Birth of Christ [Christmas]. At “Especially,” “Magnify, O my soul, . . .
units.english_cohort_translation: 20.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Festal Antiphons; at the Second Antiphon: **"...Who wast born of a Virgin"** (*...ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου τεχθείς*). Entrance Hymn: **"Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ. O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead..."** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστέ*), **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), that of the Temple Patron, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). Instead of the Trisagion Hymn: **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*). The Epistle [Galatians 1:11–19] and Gospel [Matthew 2:13–23] of the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. At **"Especially"**: **"Magnify, O my soul... It would be easier for us"** (*Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου . . . Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*); Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε*, Ps. 110:9 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 22.    If the Feast of the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Sunday, on Friday morning, after the prescribed Matins Service (see Situation One, Paragraphs 1-5), the Great Hours alone are sung; after the Prayer of the 9th Hour, the usual Dismissal takes place.
units.english_cohort_translation: *Note.* In this Third Situation, at the Hours we use the Troparion: **"Prepare, Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου, Βηθλεέμ*), since **"Mary was registered once in a census"...[^207]**

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 24.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ πρωΐ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, οἱ Κανόνες χῦμα, εἶτα ψάλλεται ὁ Εἱρμὸς τῆς Η΄ Ὠδῆς καὶ στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Προεόρτιον Ὁ φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον, τὸ τῆς Ἁγίας καὶ τὸ ἕτερον Προεόρτιον, οἱ Αἶνοι Ὦ τῶν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Ὑπόδεξαι Βηθλεέμ, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον. Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, Ἀντίφωνα τὸ Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ, εἰς τὴν Εἴσοδον Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἐν ἁγίοις θαυμαστὸς, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, καὶ Κοντάκιον Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Σαββάτου πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 25.    Τῷ αὐτῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας ψάλλεται ὁ τῆς ἑορτῆς Μ. Ἑσπερινὸς ὡς ἑξῆς· Μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ Ἰδιόμελα Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ς΄, Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος, Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν, καὶ εὐθὺς τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα μετὰ τῶν Τροπαρίων ἀπαραλλάκτως ὡς διετάχθησαν ἐν περιπτώσει Α΄ § 6. Μετὰ τὸ τελευταῖον Ἀνάγνωσμα εὐθὺς (ἄνευ τῆς Συναπτῆς) ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον. Εἶτα ἡ Μ. Συναπτὴ Εἴπωμεν πάντες, τὸ Καταξίωσον, Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν, καὶ ψάλλονται τὰ γ΄ Ἀπόστιχα Ἰδιόμελα Μέγα καὶ παράδοξον θαῦμα, Δόξα Εὐφράνθητι Ἱερουσαλὴμ, Καὶ νῦν Σπηλαίῳ παρῴκησας, Νῦν ἀπολύεις, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ γέννησίς σου ἐκ γ΄ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις ἡ ἐν § 6 τῆς Α΄ περιπτώσεως.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 24.    On Saturday morning at Matins, the Canons are read, the Irmos of the 8th Ode is sung, and then “More honorable” with its verses. Exapostilaria: of the Pre-feast “He who dwells in the light,” of the Saint, and the other one of the Pre-feast, The Praises: “What mysteries beyond the mind,” Glory, Now and ever, “O Bethlehem, receive,” Great Doxology and the Apolytikion. In the Liturgy, Antiphons “It is good to confess to the Lord.” At the Entrance “Come let us worship . . . who are wonderful in your saints.” The Apolytikion “Mary was registered once in a census,” of the Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion “Today the Virgin.” Apostolos and Gospel of the Saturday before Christmas. At “Especially,” “It is meet,” Communion Hymn “Blessed are those whom you have chosen,” “We have seen the [true] light,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 24.    On Saturday morning at Matins: the Canons are read plain, the Heirmos of the Eighth Ode is sung, and then **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*) with its verses. Exapostilaria: of the Forefeast: **"He Who dwells in unapproachable light"** (*Ὁ φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον*), of the Saint, and the second Exapostilarion of the Forefeast. At the Praises: **"What mysteries beyond understanding"** (*Ὦ τῶν ὑπὲρ νοῦν*); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"Receive, O Bethlehem"** (*Ὑπόδεξαι, Βηθλεέμ*); the Great Doxology, and the Dismissal Troparion. In the Divine Liturgy: Antiphons: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ*, Ps. 91:2 LXX). At the Entrance: **"Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ. O Son of God, Who art wonderful in the saints..."** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἐν ἁγίοις θαυμαστός*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Mary was registered once in a census"**, that of the Temple Patron, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle [Galatians 3:8–12] and Gospel [Luke 13:18–29] of the Saturday before the Nativity. At **"Especially"**: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken unto Thyself, O Lord"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω*, Ps. 64:5 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 25.    On that Saturday evening, the Great Vespers of the Feast is sung as follows: After the Introductory Psalm at “Lord, I have cried” we sing the 4 Idiomela “Come, let us greatly rejoice in the Lord” in 6 (i.e., repeat the first two). Glory, Now and ever “When Augustus reigned alone on earth.” Entrance with the Gospel, “O Gladsome Light,” and immediately the Readings with the hymns as ordered in Situation One, Paragraph 6. After the last Reading immediately (without the Petition), the Apostolos and Gospel are read. Then the Petitions “Let us all say,” “Vouchsafe,” “Let us complete our evening” and the 3 Idiomela Aposticha: “A great and marvelous wonder,” Glory, “Make glad, O Jerusalem,” Now and ever, “You have come to dwell in a cave.” Then “Lord, now let,” the Trisagion, the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ” (3 times), and Dismissal as in Situation One, Paragraph 6.
units.english_cohort_translation: 25.    On that Saturday evening: Great Vespers of the Feast is sung as follows: After the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing the 4 Idiomela: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα τῷ Κυρίῳ*) in 6 (repeating the first two). **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"When Augustus reigned alone upon the earth"** (*Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς*). Entrance with the Holy Gospel, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and immediately the Old Testament Readings with the Troparia without variation as ordered in Situation One, Paragraph 6. Immediately after the last Reading (without the Litany), the Epistle [Hebrews 1:1–12] and the Holy Gospel [Luke 2:1–20] are proclaimed. Then the Litanies: **"Let us all say"** (*Εἴπωμεν πάντες*), **"Vouchsafe, O Lord"** (*Καταξίωσον*), **"Let us complete our evening prayer"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινήν*), and the 3 Idiomela of the Aposticha are sung: **"A great and marvelous wonder"** (*Μέγα καὶ παράδοξον θαῦμα*); **"Glory"**: **"Rejoice, O Jerusalem"** (*Εὐφράνθητι, Ἱερουσαλήμ*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Thou hast come to dwell in a cave"** (*Σπηλαίῳ παρῴκησας*). Then **"Lord, now lettest Thou"** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*) thrice, and the Dismissal as in Situation One, Paragraph 6.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 27.    Τῇ αὐτῇ Κυριακῇ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα, ψάλλομεν Ἰδιόμελα τῆς ἑορτῆς Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα γ΄ καὶ τῶν Θεοπατόρων γ΄. Δόξα Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν, Καὶ νῦν Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις θεῷ (ζήτει τῇ ΚΣΤ΄). Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Μ. Προκείμενον Τίς θεὸς μέγας μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ Ἰδιόμελα τῆς ἑορτῆς Παράδοξον μυστήριον καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ δύο (ζήτει τῇ ΚΣΤ΄). Δόξα Ἱερέων μνήμη (Κυρ. μετὰ τὴν Χ. Γέννησιν), Καὶ νῦν Ἐν Βηθλεὲμ συνέδραμον ποιμένες (ἐν τῇ ΚΣΤ΄), Ἀπολυτίκια Ἡ Γέννησίς σου, τῶν Θεοπατόρων Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσήφ, αὖθις Ἡ Γέννησίς σου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 28.    Τῇ Δευτέρᾳ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ Γέννησίς σου καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, τὸ Ψαλτήριον (ἄνευ τοῦ Πολυελέου), τὰ δύο Καθίσματα τῆς ἑορτῆς Δεῦτε ἴδωμεν πιστοὶ καὶ τὸ Τί θαυμάζεις Μαριάμ; καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, ὁ Κανὼν τῆς ἑορτῆς Χριστὸς γεννᾶται μετὰ Στίχου Δόξα σοι ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μνήστορος Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε μετὰ Στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὰ Καθίσματα Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς, Δόξα Καὶ νῦν Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν, ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῶν Θεοπατόρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι Ἔσωσε λαὸν, εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἐκ τοῦ α΄ Κανόνος μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ ἡ τοῦ Μνήστορος μετὰ στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἡ καταβασία Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς μετὰ τοῦ Μεγαλυναρίου. Ἐξαποστειλάρια Σὺν Ἰακώβῳ μέλψωμεν καὶ ὁ τῆς ἑορτῆς Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ δ΄ Ἰδιόμελα τῆς ἑορτῆς Εὐφραίνεσθε δίκαιοι. Δόξα Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ. Καὶ νῦν Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις, Δοξολογία μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Ἡ Γέννησίς σου.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 27.    That Sunday evening after the Introductory Psalm at “Lord, I have cried” we sing 3 Idiomela of the Feast “Come, let us greatly rejoice in the Lord,” and 3 of the Fathers {“Come, let us extol David the king,”} Glory, “Let us commemorate,” Now and ever, “Glory to God in the highest,” (see the 26th of this month). Entrance: “O Gladsome Light” and the Great Prokimenon “Who is so great a God” with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Idiomela of the Feast “A marvelous wonder” and the other two (see the 26th of December). Glory, “Your Nativity has become the Priests' memorial” (Sunday after Christmas), Now and ever, “The shepherds hastened to Bethlehem,” (see the 26th of December). The Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ,” that of the Fathers “Proclaim, O Joseph,” again “Your birth, O Christ,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 27.    That Sunday evening: after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 3 Idiomela of the Feast: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*), and 3 of the Ancestors of God [**"Come, let us all together praise in song David the renowned king"** / *Δεῦτε συμφώνως ἅπαντες Δαυῒδ τὸν ἀοίδιμον*]. **"Glory"**: **"Let us celebrate the memory"** (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Glory to God in the highest"** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*, see the 26th of this month). Entrance: **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*) and the Great Prokeimenon: **"Who is so great a god as our God?"** (*Τίς Θεὸς μέγας ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν;*, Ps. 76:14 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Idiomela of the Feast: **"A marvelous wonder"** (*Παράδοξον μυστήριον*) and the other two (see the 26th of December). **"Glory"**: **"Thy Nativity hath become the Priests' memorial"** (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*, Sunday after the Nativity); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The shepherds hastened together to Bethlehem"** (*Ἐν Βηθλεὲμ συνέδραμον ποιμένες*, see the 26th of December). The Dismissal Troparia: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, that of the Ancestors of God: **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), again **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 28.    On Monday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Trisagion, the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ,” and the Exapsalmos. At “God is the Lord”: the Apolytikion as in Vespers, then the Psalter (without the Polyeleos). The two Kathismata of the Feast “Come, O you faithful” and “Why are you filled with wonder, O Mary?” and Psalm 50 (read). The Canon of the Feast “Christ is born” with the Verse “Glory to You, our God” and the Canon of the Betrothed “Blessed servant of Christ” with the Verse “Holy one of God.” After the 3rd Ode, the Kathismata “As a true Father,” Glory, Now and ever, “The chorus of Prophets”; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday after Christmas and the Minologion of the day and the Postscript of the Fathers. The Katavasie “He saved the people,” then the 9th Ode of the Feast from the first Canon with its Megalynaria and that of the Betrothed with the Verse “Holy One of God,” and the Katavasia “It would be easier for us,” with its Megalynarion. Exapostilaria: “With James let us sing” and of the Feast “Our Saviour visited us from on high.” At the Praises: the 4 Idiomela of the Feast “Make glad, O you righteous”; Glory, “The blood and fire,” Now and ever, “Today the invisible nature,” Great Doxology and the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ.”
units.english_cohort_translation: 28.    On Monday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter (without the Polyeleos). The two Kathismata of the Feast: **"Come, ye faithful, let us behold"** (*Δεῦτε ἴδωμεν, πιστοί*) and **"Why art thou amazed, O Mary?"** (*Τί θαυμάζεις, Μαριάμ;*), and Psalm 50 [LXX] read plain. The Canon of the Feast: **"Christ is born"** (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*) with the Verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Canon of the Betrothed: **"Blessed servant of Christ"** (*Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε*) with the Verse: **"Holy righteous one of God, pray to God for us"** (*Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ*). After the Third Ode: the Kathismata: **"As a true Father"** (*Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"The chorus of Prophets"** (*Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday after the Nativity, the Menologion of the day, and the Synaxarion notice of the Ancestors of God. The Katavasiai: **"He saved the people"** (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*); then the Ninth Ode of the Feast from the First Canon is sung with its Megalynaria, and that of the Betrothed with the Verse: **"Holy righteous one of God"**, and the Katavasia: **"It would be easier for us"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*) with its Megalynarion. Exapostilaria: **"With James let us sing"** (*Σὺν Ἰακώβῳ μέλψωμεν*) and of the Feast: **"Our Savior, the Dayspring from on high, hath visited us"** (*Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς*). At the Praises: the 4 Idiomela of the Feast: **"Be glad, O ye righteous"** (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); **"Glory"**: **"Blood and fire, and vapor of smoke"** (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today the invisible nature"** (*Σήμερον ἡ ἀόρατος φύσις*); the Great Doxology, and the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**.

units.english_cohort_translation: 29.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Antiphons of the Feast as yesterday. Entrance Verse: **"From the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee"** (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου*, Ps. 109:3 LXX). The Dismissal Troparia: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, **"Proclaim, O Joseph"**, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto the Transcendent One"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν ὑπερούσιον τίκτει*). Instead of the Trisagion Hymn: we sing **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστόν*). The Epistle [Galatians 1:11–19] and Gospel [Matthew 2:13–23] of the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. At **"Especially"**: **"Magnify, O my soul... It would be easier for us"** (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*); Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε*, Ps. 110:9 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Dismissal.[^209]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 30.    Τῆς ἑορτῆς ἡ Ἀπόδοσις κατὰ τὴν Γ΄ ταύτην περίπτωσιν γίνεται τὸ προσεχὲς Σάββατον (ἤτοι τῇ Λ΄ τοῦ μηνός, [ὀρθότερον εἶναι τῇ ΛΑ΄ τοῦ μηνός]), ἐν ᾧ ὡς προείρηται ἐν περιπτώσει Α΄ § 15 ψάλλονται ἅπαντα τὰ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον λέγονται τοῦ Σαββάτου πρὸ τῶν Φώτων.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 31.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ ἑορτὴ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Δευτέρᾳ, τῇ Παρασκευῇ πρωῒ μετὰ τὴν ἐνδιάτακτον Ἀκολουθίαν τοῦ Ὄρθρου, ψάλλονται αἱ Μ. Ὧραι μόναι ὡς προδιετάχθησαν ἐν περιπτώσει Α΄ § 1-5 καὶ μετὰ τὴν εὐχὴν τῆς Θ΄ Ὥρας ἡ Ἀπόλυσις. Καὶ ἐν τῇ περιπτώσει ταύτῃ Ἀπολυτίκιον εἰς τὰς Ὥρας λέγεται τὸ Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεὲμ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἄμεσον εἶναι (ὡς εἴρηται ἐν περιπτώσει Γ΄ § 22) τὴν Παραμονὴν τῇ ἑορτῇ.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 32.    Τῇ αὐτῇ Παρασκευῇ ἑσπέρας καὶ τῷ Σαββάτῳ πρωῒ ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῶν Δέκα Μαρτύρων καὶ τῶν Προεορτίων ψάλλονται κατὰ τὴν ἐν τῷ Μηναίῳ διάταξιν· τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεὲμ καὶ Κοντάκιον Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν προαιώνιον Λόγον. Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Σαββάτου πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως. Κοινωνικὸν Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

The Leave-taking of the Feast in this Third Situation occurs the following Saturday (that is the 30th of the month) [it should be the 31st] in which (as indicated in Situation One, Paragraph 15) are sung all those hymns of the Feast. Apostolos and Gospel are those of the Saturday before Epiphany.
units.english_cohort_translation: **The Apodosis** 30. The Epistle and Gospel are those of the Saturday before Theophany.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 31.    If the Feast of Christ’s Nativity occurs on a Monday, on Friday morning, after the prescribed Matins Service, the Great Hours alone are sung, as prescribed in Situation One, Paragraphs 1 - 5; after the Prayer of the 9th Hour, follows the usual Dismissal. In this Situation in the Hours, we use as Apolytikion the hymn “Prepare, Bethlehem,” since (as mentioned above in Situation Three, Paragraph 22) it is not the immediate Eve of the Feast.
units.english_cohort_translation: **Situation Four** 31.    If the Feast of the Nativity of Christ occurs on a Monday: on Friday morning, after the prescribed Matins Service, the Royal Hours alone are sung, as prescribed in Situation One, Paragraphs 1–5; after the Prayer of the Ninth Hour, follows the usual Dismissal. In this Situation, at the Hours we use as Dismissal Troparion the hymn: **"Prepare, Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου, Βηθλεέμ*), since (as mentioned above in Situation Three, Paragraph 22) the Paramony is not immediately adjacent to the Feast.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 32.    That Friday evening and Saturday morning, the Service of the 10 Martyrs and of the Pre-feast are sung according to the order in the Mineon. The Apolytikion “Prepare, Bethlehem” and the Kontakion “Today the Virgin the pre-eternal Word.” Apostolos and Gospel of the Saturday before Christ’s Birth, Communion Hymn “Blessed are they who you have chosen,” “We have seen the [true] light,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 32.    That Friday evening and Saturday morning, the Service of the Ten Holy Martyrs of Crete and that of the Forefeast are sung according to the order in the Menaion. The Dismissal Troparion: **"Prepare, Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου, Βηθλεέμ*), and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin comes to give birth ineffably unto the Pre-eternal Word"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν προαιώνιον Λόγον*). The Epistle and Gospel of the Saturday before the Nativity of Christ. Communion Verse: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken unto Thyself, O Lord"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω καὶ προσελάβου, Κύριε*, Ps. 64:5 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 37.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα γ΄, τῆς ἑορτῆς Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα δ΄ καὶ τῶν Θεοπατόρων γ΄, Δόξα Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν, Καὶ νῦν Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, Δόξα Ἱερέων μνήμη. Καὶ νῦν Σπηλαίῳ παρῴκησας, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Θεοπατόρων Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, *Δόξα* *Ἱερέων μνήμη*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Σπηλαίῳ παρῴκησας*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Θεοπατόρων *Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ*, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 38.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ Γέννησίς σου καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ τὰ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἀντὶ Θεοτοκίων, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τῆς ἑορτῆς μετὰ Στίχου Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μνήστορος Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε μετὰ Στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον μετὰ τοῦ Οἴκου χῦμα, εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς, Καὶ νῦν Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν, αἱ Καταβασίαι διπλαῖ καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ τῶν δύο Κανόνων τῆς ἑορτῆς μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ ἀμφότεραι αἱ Καταβασίαι τῆς Θ΄. Ἐξαποστειλάρια, τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Θεοπατόρων καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς δ΄. Δόξα Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ. Καὶ νῦν Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 37.    On Saturday evening, after the Introductory Psalm at “Lord, I have cried” we sing 3 Resurrection Stichira, 4 Idiomela of the Feast “Come, let us greatly rejoice in the Lord,” and 3 of the Fathers, Glory, “Let us commemorate,” Now and ever, “When Augustus reigned alone.” Entrance, “O Gladsome Light” and the Prokimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory, “Your Nativity has become the priests’ memorial,” Now and ever, “You have come to dwell in a cave.” Apolytikia: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers “Proclaim, O Joseph,” and of the Feast, and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: **Sunday After the Nativity of Christ and the Apodosis of the Feast** 37.    On Saturday evening, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 3 Resurrectional Stichira, 4 Idiomela of the Feast: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*), and 3 of the Ancestors of God; **"Glory"**: **"Let us celebrate the memory"** (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"When Augustus reigned alone upon earth"** (*Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος*). Entrance, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"Thy Nativity hath become the priests' memorial"** (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Thou hast made Thy dwelling in a cave"** (*Σπηλαίῳ παρῴκησας*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion; of the Ancestors: **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*); of the Feast: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 38.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon and the Triadic “It is meet,”; then the Trisagion, the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ,” and the Exapsalmos. At “God is the Lord”: the Apolytikia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos. The Resurrection Kathismata and those of the Feast instead of the Theotokia, the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon. The Canons of the Resurrection and of the Feast with the Verse “Glory to you, O God” and of the Betrothed “Blessed servant of Christ” with the Verse “Holy one of God.” After the 3rd Ode, the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos (read), then the Kathisma “As a true Father,” Glory, Now and ever, “The chorus of Prophets.” After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, the Minologion of the Saints of the day and the Postscript of the Sunday after Christmas. The double Katavasie and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then the 9th Ode of both Canons of the Feast with their Megalynaria and both Katavasie of the 9th Ode. Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers, and of the Feast. units.english_cohort_translation: 38.    On Sunday at Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and the Triadic hymns: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Hexapsalmos. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos [Kathisma 17 / Psalm 118 LXX]. The Resurrectional Kathismata and those of the Feast instead of the Theotokia; the Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. The Canons: of the Resurrection, of the Feast with the Verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and of the Betrothed: **"Blessed servant of Christ"** (*Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε*) with the Verse: **"Holy righteous one of God, pray to God for us"** (*Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ*). After the Third Ode: the Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos plain; then the Kathisma: **"As a true Father"** (*Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The chorus of Prophets"** (*Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*). After the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ, the Menologion of the Saints of the day, and the Synaxarion notice of the Sunday after the Nativity. The double Katavasiai: **"He saved the people"** (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*) and **"The Lord, working wonders"** (*Στείβει θαλάσσης*), and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then the Ninth Ode of both Canons of the Feast is sung with their Megalynaria, and both Katavasiai of the Ninth Ode. Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Ancestors, and of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrectional Stichira and 4 of the Feast; **"Glory"**: **"Blood and fire, and vapor of smoke"** (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and...[^211]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 39.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς, εἰς τὸ β΄ Ἀντίφωνον Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου τεχθείς, τὸ Εἰσοδικὸν τῆς ἑορτῆς μετὰ τοῦ Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, Ἡ Γέννησίς σου, τὸ Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Κοντάκιον Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, τὸ Τρισάγιον, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς πρὸ τῶν Φώτων. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 40.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ ἑορτὴ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Τρίτῃ, Τετάρτῃ ἢ Πέμπτῃ, τῇ Παραμονῇ ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῶν Μ. Ὡρῶν, ὁ Μ. Ἑσπερινὸς καὶ ἡ Λειτουργία τοῦ Μ. Βασιλείου, καὶ τὸ πρωῒ ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῆς ἑορτῆς, ὡς καὶ ἡ τῆς ἑπομένης ἡμέρας, ψάλλονται ὡς διετάχθησαν ἐν περιπτώσει Α΄ § 1-11. Καὶ ἐν ταῖς τρισὶ ταύταις περιστάσεσιν ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν ψάλλεται ὡς ἐφεξῆς.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 41.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄, τῆς ἑορτῆς Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα γ΄, καὶ τῶν Θεοπατόρων γ΄, Δόξα Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, Δόξα Ἱερέων μνήμη. Καὶ νῦν Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Θεοπατόρων Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ, Ἡ Γέννησίς σου Χριστέ, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
units.english_cohort_translation: 41.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄, τῆς ἑορτῆς *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα* γ΄, καὶ τῶν Θεοπατόρων γ΄, *Δόξα* *Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*, *Καὶ νῦν* τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ, *Δόξα* *Ἱερέων μνήμη*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι*, Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Θεοπατόρων *Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ*, *Ἡ Γέννησίς σου Χριστέ*, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 42.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ψάλλεται ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἡ Γέννησίς σου καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα μετὰ τῶν μεθεόρτων, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μνήστορος μετὰ Στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον μετὰ τοῦ Οἴκου...

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 39.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast, at the 2nd Antiphon “born of a Virgin.” The Entrance Hymn of the Feast with “who is risen from the dead.” The Resurrection Apolytikion, then “Your birth, O Christ,” then “Proclaim, O Joseph,” the Apolytikion of the Saint of the Church and the Kontakion “The Virgin today.” The Trisagios Hymn, the Apostolos and Gospel of the Sunday before Epiphany. At “Especially,” “Magnify, O my soul, . . . It would be easier for us.” Communion Hymn “The Lord has sent deliverance,” the Apolytikion “Your birth, O Christ,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 39.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Antiphons of the Feast; at the Second Antiphon, the refrain: **"Who wast born of a Virgin, save us who chant unto Thee: Alleluia"** (*Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου τεχθείς*). The Entrance Verse of the Feast with **"Who art risen from the dead"** (*Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, then **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), then **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), the Dismissal Troparion of the Temple Patron, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto the Transcendent One"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Trisagion Hymn. The Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday before Theophany. At **"Especially"**: **"Magnify, O my soul... It would be easier for us"** (*Μεγάλυνον ἡ ψυχή μου . . . Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*); Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε*, Ps. 110:9 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Dismissal.

The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, then **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), then **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), the Dismissal Troparion of the Temple Patron, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto the Transcendent One"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Trisagion Hymn. The Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday before Theophany. At **"Especially"**: **"Magnify, O my soul... It would be easier for us"** (*Μεγάλυνον ἡ ψυχή μου . . . Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*); Communion Verse: **"The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people"** (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε*, Ps. 110:9 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"**, and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 41.    On Saturday evening after the Introductory Psalm at “Lord, I have cried” we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 Idiomela of the Feast “Come, let us greatly rejoice in the Lord,” and 3 of the Fathers, Glory, “Let us commemorate,” Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode. Entrance, “O Gladsome Light” and the Prokimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory, “Your Nativity has become the priest’s memorial,” Now and ever, “Today all the angels dance.” Apolytikia: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers “Proclaim, O Joseph,” “Your birth, O Christ,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: **Sunday After the Nativity of Christ** 41.    On Saturday evening: after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrectional Stichira, 3 Idiomela of the Feast: **"Come, let us rejoice in the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*), and 3 of the Ancestors of God; **"Glory"**: **"Let us celebrate the memory"** (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone. Entrance, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Stichira; **"Glory"**: **"Thy Nativity hath become the priests' memorial"** (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Today all the angels dance"** (*Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion; of the Ancestors: **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*); **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς,
units.slavonic_diplomatic: εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς, Καὶ νῦν Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν· ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος Ἀπορρήτῳ βουλῇ, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς· αἱ Καταβασίαι Ἔσωσε λαὸν καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῶν Θεοπατόρων καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς Εὐφραίνεσθε δίκαιοι δ΄, Δόξα Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ, Καὶ νῦν Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.
units.english_cohort_translation: εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα *Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*, *Καὶ νῦν* *Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*· ἀφ’ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον *Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον* καὶ ὁ Οἶκος *Ἀπορρήτῳ βουλῇ*, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς· αἱ Καταβασίαι *Ἔσωσε λαὸν* καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 43.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τοῦ Μνήστορος δ΄. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ Ἡ Γέννησίς σου, τὸ Εὐαγγελίζου Ἰωσὴφ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Κοντάκιον Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς μετὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ Γέννησιν. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: a true Father,” Glory, Now and ever, “The chorus of Prophets”; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion “Of joy today” and the Ikos “Of ineffable will,” the Minologion of the Saints of the day and the Postscript of the Sunday after Christmas. The Katavasie “He saved the people,” and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then “More honorable.” Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers and of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Feast, “Make glad, O you righteous,” Glory, “The fire and blood,” Now and ever, “Most blessed are You,” Great Doxology and “Today salvation.”
units.english_cohort_translation: a true Father"** (*Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: **"The chorus of Prophets"** (*Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*); after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion: **"Of joy today"** (*Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον*) and the Ikos: **"By ineffable counsel"** (*Ἀπορρήτῳ βουλῇ*), the Menologion of the Saints of the day, and the Synaxarion notice of the Sunday after the Nativity. The Katavasiai: **"He saved the people"** (*Ἔσωσε λαόν*), and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then we sing: **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Ancestors, and of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrectional Stichira and 4 of the Feast: **"Be glad, O ye righteous"** (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); **"Glory"**: **"Blood and fire, and vapor of smoke"** (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); the Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation is come unto the world"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 43.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Mode and 4 hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Betrothed. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Apolytikion, the “Your birth, O Christ,” the “Proclaim, O Joseph,” that of the Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion “The Virgin today.” The Apostolos and the Gospel of the Sunday after Christ’s Nativity. At “Especially,” “It is meet,” Communion Hymn “Praise,” “We have seen the [true] light,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 43.    In the Divine Liturgy: the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone, and 4 hymns from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Betrothed. After the Entrance: the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, **"Thy Nativity, O Christ our God"** (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), **"Proclaim, O Joseph"** (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), that of the Temple Patron, and the Kontakion: **"Today the Virgin gives birth unto the Transcendent One"** (*Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*). The Epistle [Galatians 1:11–19] and the Gospel [Matthew 2:13–23] of the Sunday after the Nativity of Christ. At **"Especially"**: **"It is truly meet"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Verse: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 1.    In Vespers following the Introductory Psalm and the first Stasis of the Psalter, at “Lord, I have cried,” we sing the 2 Idiomela of the Feast repeating the first, and 3 Prosomia of the Saint. Glory of the Saint “O lover of Wisdom,” Now and ever, “The Savior coming down.” Entrance, “O Gladsome Light,” the Prokimenon of the day and the Readings. At the Aposticha: the 3 Idiomela of the Saint, Glory, “Having received the grace of miracles,” Now and ever, “The all-good God was not ashamed.” The Apolytikia: of the Saint, then Glory, Now and ever of the Feast once, and Dismissal “May He who on the eighth day deigned to be circumcised in the flesh for our salvation, Christ our true God ....”
units.english_cohort_translation: **The 1st: The Circumcision of our Lord Jesus Christ and Commemoration of our Father among the Saints Basil the Great** 1.    In Vespers: following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the First Stasis of the First Kathisma of the Psalter [Ps. 1–3 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing the 2 Idiomela of the Feast, repeating the first [making 3], and 3 Prosomoia of the Saint [making 6 Stichira in all]. **"Glory"** of the Saint: **"O lover of wisdom"** (*Σοφίας ἐραστής*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The Savior, coming down in condescension"** (*Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ*). Entrance, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon of the day, and the 3 Old Testament Readings [Genesis 17:1–14; Proverbs 8:22–30; Proverbs 10:31–11:12]. At the Aposticha: the 3 Idiomela of the Saint; **"Glory"**: **"Having received the grace of miracles"** (*Ὁ τὴν χάριν τῶν θαυμάτων*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The all-good God was not ashamed"** (*Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη ὁ πανάγαθος Θεός*). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Saint: **"Thy sound hath gone forth"** (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν*); then **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: of the Feast once: **"Without change Thou didst take human form"** (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*), and the Dismissal: **"May He Who on the eighth day deigned to be circumcised in the flesh for our salvation, Christ our true God..."** (*Ὁ ἐν τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἡμέρᾳ σαρκὶ περιτμηθῆναι καταδεξάμενος διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*).

units.slavonic_incipit: τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως
units.slavonic_diplomatic: τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ Ἁγίου, δὶς καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειράν, οἱ ἀναβαθμοί, τὸ α΄ Ἀντίφωνον τοῦ δ΄ ἤχου, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτοῦ [τὸ Μηναῖον καὶ ἄλλαι πηγαὶ ὑποδεικνύουν ὡς τὸ ὀρθὸν Προκείμενον τὸ Τὸ στόμα μου λαλήσει σοφίαν]· τὸ Πᾶσα πνοή, καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Ὄρθρου (ζήτει, Νοεμβρίου ΙΓ΄)· εἶτα ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, Δόξα, Ταῖς τοῦ Ἱεράρχου, Καὶ νῦν, Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου, Στίχος Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός, καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις ἐν χείλεσί σου· ὁ Κανὼν τῆς ἑορτῆς Δεῦτε λαοὶ μετὰ Στίχου Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεός, καὶ ὁ τοῦ Ἁγίου Σοῦ τὴν φωνὴν μετὰ Στίχου Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Κάθισμα τοῦ Ἁγίου, καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς, ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον· αἱ καταβασίαι διπλαῖ, εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ τῆς ἑορτῆς μετὰ τῆς τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὰ Μεγαλυνάρια αὐτῶν.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: At “God is the Lord”: the Apolytikion of the Saint (2 times) and of the Feast (once), then the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata in order, the Anavathmi, the first Antiphon of Mode Four and the Prokimenon “His word went out to all the earth” {it appears, however, from the Mineon and other sources that the correct Prokimenon is “My mouth shall speak wisdom”}. Then “Let everything that has breath” and the Gospel of Matins (see November 13); then Psalm 50 read, Glory, “By the intercessions of the Hierarch,” Now and ever, “By the intercessions of the Theotokos,” the Verse “Have mercy upon me, O God,” and the Idiomelon “Grace poured forth from your lips”; the Canon of the Feast “Come, all you people” with the Verse “Glory to You, O God” and of the Saint “It would be fitting for the sound of your voice” with the Verse “Holy One of God.” After the 3rd Ode, the Kathismata of the Saint and of the Feast; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint and the Minologion. Both (double) Katavasie, then the 9th Ode of the Feast with that of the Saint and their Megalynaria.
units.english_cohort_translation: At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion of the Saint twice, and of the Feast once; then the Psalter of the day and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata in order, the Anavathmoi: the First Antiphon of Tone 4 [**"From my youth"** / *Ἐκ νεότητός μου*], and the Prokeimenon: **"Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world"** (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν*, Ps. 18:5 LXX) [the Menaion and other sources indicate as the correct Prokeimenon: **"My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding"** (*Τὸ στόμα μου λαλήσει σοφίαν*, Ps. 48:4 LXX)]. Then **"Let every breath praise the Lord"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*) and the Morning Gospel (seek on November 13: John 10:1–9); then Psalm 50 [LXX] read plain. **"Glory"**: **"At the intercessions of the Hierarch"** (*Ταῖς τοῦ Ἱεράρχου*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"At the intercessions of the Theotokos"** (*Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*); the Verse: **"Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy great mercy"** (*Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός*, Ps. 50:3 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"Grace was poured out upon your lips, venerable Father Basil"** (*Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις ἐν χείλεσί σου*). The Canon of the Feast: **"Come, ye peoples"** (*Δεῦτε λαοί*) with the Verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Canon of the Saint: **"Thy voice"** (*Σοῦ τὴν φωνήν*) with the Verse: **"Holy Hierarch of God, pray to God for us"** (*Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ*). After the Third Ode: Kathisma of the Saint, and of the Feast; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and the Menologion. The Katavasiai are double [from both Iambic and Non-iambic Canons of Theophany: **"The Lord, mighty in battle, uncovered the foundations of the deep"** / *Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα* and **"Israel traversed the stormy swell of the sea"** / *Στείβει θαλάσσης*]; then the Ninth Ode of the Feast is sung together with that of the Saint and their Megalynaria.

units.slavonic_incipit: Savior coming down,” Great Doxology, the
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Savior coming down,” Great Doxology, the Apolytikion “The human form without change,” and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: Exapostilaria of the Saint and of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Prosomoia of the Saint; **"Glory"**: **"Grace was poured out upon Thy lips, venerable Father Basil"** (*Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις ἐν χείλεσί σου*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The Savior, coming down unto the human race"** (*Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ*); Great Doxology, the Dismissal Troparion: **"In unalterable form"** (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*), and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 4.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ ἑορτὴ ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τῆς ἑορτῆς τὰ δύο Ἰδιόμελα εἰς γ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου γ΄, Δόξα τοῦ Ἁγίου, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου. Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, τὸ Προκείμενον καὶ τὰ ᾿Αναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα τοῦ Ἁγίου, Καὶ νῦν, Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη, ᾿Απολυτίκια, τὸ ᾿Αναστάσιμον, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

The Trisagios Hymn, Apostolos “Brethren, beware lest anyone cheat you” and Gospel “The shepherds returned glorifying,” and then the Liturgy of Basil the Great; at the Diptychs we sing the Megalynarion of the Saint:
units.english_cohort_translation:
**"Let us all extol the great Basil, revealer of heavenly things, initiate of the Master, the star shining brightly from Caesarea and the land of Cappadocia, honoring and magnifying him."** (*Τὸν οὐρανοφάντορα τοῦ Χριστοῦ μύστην τοῦ Δεσπότου...*)

units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    If the Feast occurs on a Sunday: in Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter Kathisma, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we sing 4 Resurrectional Stichira, the 2 Idiomela of the Feast repeating the first to make 3, and 3 Prosomoia of the Saint; **"Glory"** of the Saint: **"O lover of wisdom"** (*Σοφίας ἐραστής*); **"Both now and ever"**: the First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone. Entrance, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings. At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Stichira; **"Glory"** of the Saint: **"Having received the grace of miracles"** (*Ὁ τὴν χάριν τῶν θαυμάτων*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The all-good God was not ashamed"** (*Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη ὁ πανάγαθος Θεός*). Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saint, that of the Feast, and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_incipit: Εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ τῆς
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ἡ τοῦ ἁγίου μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ αἱ β΄ Καταβασίαι τῆς Θ΄. Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ ᾿Αναστάσιμον, τὸ τοῦ ἁγίου καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς δ΄, Δόξα τοῦ ἁγίου, Καὶ νῦν, Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.
units.english_cohort_translation: Ἁγίου ἀνὰ δ΄· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον μετὰ τοῦ Οἴκου, εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς· ἀφ’ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας, αἱ Καταβασίαι διπλαῖ καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου. Εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ Ὠδὴ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ἡ τοῦ ἁγίου μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ αἱ β΄ Καταβασίαι τῆς Θ΄. Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τὸ τοῦ ἁγίου καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς δ΄, *Δόξα* τοῦ ἁγίου, *Καὶ νῦν*, *Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ*, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ *Σήμερον σωτηρία*.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 6.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν τὰ ᾿Αντίφωνα· εἰς τὸ β΄ ᾿Αντίφωνον Ὁ σαρκὶ περιτμηθείς· μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, [τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ] Κοντάκιον Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Κύριος (ζήτει ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς), ᾿Απόστολος τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον Ὑπέστρεψαν οἱ ποιμένες καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ Λειτουργία τοῦ Μεγάλου Βασιλείου. Εἰς τὰ Δίπτυχα ψάλλεται τὸ Μεγαλυνάριον τοῦ Ἁγίου (ὅρα ὄπισθεν § 3). Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ Κυριακὴ πρὸ τῶν Φώτων τῇ Β΄, Γ΄, ἢ Δ΄ τοῦ μηνός, ἡ ᾿Ακολουθία ψάλλεται ὡς ἐφεξῆς· Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ᾿Αναστάσιμα ς΄ καὶ Προεόρτια δ΄ Προεόρτια ᾄσματα (ζήτει τῇ Β΄ τοῦ μηνός)· Δόξα, Ἔρχετε πρὸς Ἰορδάνην, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἰωάννη Βαπτιστὰ (ζήτει τῇ Β΄ τοῦ μηνός). ᾿Απολυτίκια τὸ ᾿Αναστάσιμον, τὸ Προεόρτιον Ἑτοιμάζου Ζαβουλὼν καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection, then the Kathisma of the Saint and that of the Feast; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and the Minologion of the day. The two (double) Katavasie, and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then the 9th Ode of the Feast with that of the Saint with their Megalynaria and the 2 (double) Katavasie of the 9th Ode.
units.english_cohort_translation: Saint with 4 troparia each. After the Third Ode: the Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, then the Kathisma of the Saint and that of the Feast; after the Sixth Ode: the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, and the Menologion of the day. The double Katavasiai: **"He uncovered the bottom of the deep"** (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα*) and **"The Lord, working wonders"** (*Στείβει θαλάσσης*), and the entire order of the Morning Gospel. Then the Ninth Ode of the Feast with that of the Saint is sung with their Megalynaria, and both Katavasiai of the Ninth Ode. Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, that of the Saint, and that of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrectional Stichira and 4 of the Feast; **"Glory"** of the Saint: **"Grace was poured out upon Thy lips"** (*Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις ἐν χείλεσί σου*); **"Both now and ever"**: **"The Savior, coming down"** (*Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).
