units.slavonic_diplomatic: Apolytikion “Buried with You [through Baptism, Christ our God]” and the Exapsalmos. At “God is the Lord”: the Apolytikia as in Vespers [“The common resurrection” and the other one “Buried with You [through Baptism, Christ our God]”] then [the Second Kathisma of] the Psalter and the Polyeleos [Psalms 134-135], the Kathismata in order {of the Triodion: “In spirit carrying branches, with our souls cleansed let us come to praise Christ the Master in faith like children,” and another Kathisma “You did raise Lazarus from the tomb after four days, O Lord,”; {Kathisma Three of} the Psalter followed by the {Triodion} Kathismata: “O Christ Savior, You did shed tears in secret over Your friend Lazarus lying dead” and “You people and nations, rejoice harmoniously.” The Polyeleos [Kathisma 19 (Psalms 134 and 135 [only])] followed by the {Triodion} Kathismata in order: {“He Who sits upon the throne of the cherubim, for our sake sits upon a foal” (2 times).} The First Antiphon of the Anavathmi of Mode IV, the Prokimenon “Out of the mouths of infants {and sucklings You have perfected praise.}” The “Let all breath” {The Verse “O Lord, our Lord, how admirable is Your Name in all the earth!”} The Matins Gospel {Matthew 21:1-11, 15-17.} We do not say “{Having beheld} the Resurrection of Christ” but immediately Psalm 50 is read. Glory, “Today Christ enters {the Holy City,}” Now and ever, “Today, Christ enters {the Holy City.}” The Verse “Have mercy upon me, O God” and “Today the grace {of the Holy Spirit has brought us together,}” the Canon in six without verses, except Glory, Now and ever, at the last two hymns. After the Third Ode, the Ypakoi “With branches praising” (read). After the Sixth [Ode] the Kontakion, the Ikos, the Minologion of the Saints of the Day and the Postscript of the Triodion. The Katavasie “Verily, the springs of the deep appeared dry” and [instead of “More honorable,”] the Ninth Ode [of the Canon is chanted in its entirety]. Then the “Holy is the Lord our God” (3 times) sung as the Exapostilarion and, after this, the prayer of the Palms is read by the Proestos. Immediately, the First Choir sings the “Let all breath” and the verses of the Praises³⁶, and the 4 Idiomela: {“O Lord, great multitudes spread their 36.
units.english_cohort_translation: ... Dismissal Troparion: **"Buried with Thee through Baptism, O Christ our God..."** (*Συνταφέντες σοι*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers [**"In confirming the common Resurrection..."** twice, "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Buried with Thee through Baptism..."** once]. Then the Psalter [Kathisma 2, Pss. 9–16 LXX, and Kathisma 3, Pss. 17–23 LXX] and the Polyeleos [Kathisma 19, Pss. 134–135 LXX]. The Sessional Hymns [Kathismata] in order from the Triodion: after the first Kathisma: **"In spirit carrying branches, with cleansed souls let us praise Christ in faith like children..."** (*Μετὰ κλάδων νοητῶς*) and another Sessional Hymn: **"Thou didst raise Lazarus from the tomb after four days, O Lord..."** (*Τετραήμερον ἤγειρας*); after the second Kathisma: **"O Christ our Savior, Thou didst shed tears in secret over Thy friend Lazarus lying dead..."** (*Δάκρυα προέχεας, Σωτήρ*) and **"O ye peoples and nations, rejoice together!..."** (*Λαοὶ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη συνευφράνθητε*). After the Polyeleos: the festal Sessional Hymn: **"He Who sits upon the throne of the Cherubim, for our sake sits upon a foal..."** (*Ὁ ἐπὶ θρόνου Χερουβίμ*) twice. After the Third Ode, the Hypakoe: **"Praising with branches, first the peoples cried aloud with hymns of praise..."** (*Μετὰ κλάδων ὑμνήσαντες*) read plain. After the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion: **"Upborne upon the throne in heaven and upon a foal on earth, O Christ God..."** (*Τῷ θρόνῳ ἐν οὐρανῷ*), the Oikos: **"Since Thou didst bind Hades, O Immortal One..."** (*Ἐπειδὴ ᾍδην ἔδησας*), the Menologion of the Saints of the day from the Menaion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion. The Katavasiai: **"The springs of the deep appeared dry..."** (*Ὤφθησαν αἱ πηγαὶ τῆς ἀβύσσου*). units.slavonic_diplomatic: 65.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικὸν Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν· Σῶσον ἡμᾶς... ὁ ἐπὶ πώλου ὄνου κτλ. τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν, καὶ Συνταφέντες σοι, εἶτα τὸ Κοντάκιον Τῷ θρόνῳ ἐν οὐρανῷ, τὸ Τρισάγιον, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, ὁ Εἱρμὸς τῆς θ' Θεὸς Κύριος, Κοινωνικὸν Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Ἀλληλούϊα. Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, ὁ Εἱρμὸς τῆς θ' *Θεὸς Κύριος*, Κοινωνικὸν *Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Ἀλληλούϊα*. *Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν*, *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 66.    Τὸ ἑσπέρας [μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακόν], εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ γ' Ἀπόστιχα τῆς χθὲς Ἰδιόμελα Χαῖρε καὶ εὐφραίνου, δευτεροῦντες αὐτά, Δόξα, τὸ αὐτό, Καὶ νῦν Ὁ τοῖς Χερουβὶμ ἐποχούμενος, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας, τὰ γ' τῆς σειρᾶς Ἀπόστιχα, Δόξα, Ἐκ βαΐων καὶ κλάδων, Καὶ νῦν, Φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν. Μετὰ τὸ Νῦν ἀπολύεις, εὐθὺς ψάλλεται ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Ἀποδείπνου Ἰωσὴφ τὴν σωφροσύνην μετὰ Στίχου Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν δόξα σοι· ἀπ' θ' ὁ Εἱρμὸς Ἀλλότριον τῶν μητέρων, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Θεοτόκε Παρθένε κτλ. ὡς ἐν ταῖς λοιπαῖς Κυριακαῖς

units.english_cohort_translation: 65.    At the Divine Liturgy, the Festal Antiphons of Palm Sunday [First Antiphon: Ps. 114 LXX with refrain "Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us"; Second Antiphon: Ps. 115 LXX with refrain "Save us, O Son of God, Who didst sit upon the foal of an ass, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"; Third Antiphon: Ps. 117 LXX with the Dismissal Troparion: "In confirming the common Resurrection..."]. The Entrance Hymn [Isodikon]: **"Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord! God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us: Save us, O Son of God, Who didst sit upon the foal of an ass, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου...*, Ps. 117:26–27 [LXX]). After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: **"In confirming the common Resurrection before Thy Passion..."** (*Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν*) and **"Buried with Thee through Baptism, O Christ our God..."** (*Συνταφέντες σοι*). Then the Kontakion: **"Upborne upon the throne in heaven and upon a foal on earth, O Christ God..."** (*Τῷ θρόνῳ ἐν οὐρανῷ*). The Trisagion Hymn: **"Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us"** (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός*). The Epistle [Apostolos]: Philippians 4:4–9 ("Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice!..."), and the Gospel: John 12:1–18 (The Anointing at Bethany and the Triumphal Entry). At "Especially [among the all-holy]...", the Heirmos of the Ninth Ode: **"God the Lord hath appeared unto us; let us appoint a festival, and rejoicing come, let us magnify Christ with palms and branches, crying aloud with voices of praise: Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord!..."** (*Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν*). The Communion Hymn [Koinōnikon]: **"Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord. Alleluia!"** (*Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου. Ἀλληλούϊα*, Ps. 117:26 [LXX]). In place of **"We have seen the true Light"**, we chant the Dismissal Troparion: **"In confirming the common Resurrection..."** (*Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν*); then: **"Blessed be the name of the Lord"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and the Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 66.    On Sunday evening, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 [LXX]), we chant the three Aposticha Idiomela of yesterday: **"Rejoice and be glad, O city of Zion!..."** (*Χαῖρε καὶ εὐφραίνου*) twice, **"Today the Savior comes unto Jerusalem..."** (*Σήμερον ὁ Σωτὴρ εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἔρχεται*) twice, and **"O Thou Who sittest upon the Cherubim and art praised by the Seraphim!..."** (*Ὁ τοῖς Χερουβὶμ ἐποχούμενος*) twice. "Glory...": **"Rejoice and be glad, O city of Zion!..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"O Thou Who sittest upon the Cherubim..."**. Little Entrance with the censer, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Great Prokimenon of the day: **"Turn not away Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble; hear me speedily: attend unto my soul, and deliver it!"** (*Μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἀπὸ τοῦ παιδός σου*, Ps. 68:18–19 [LXX]). Then the three appointed Aposticha: **"Passing from one divine feast to another divine feast, let us hasten, O believers..."** (*Ἐκ βαΐων εἰς βάϊα πιστοί*); verse: **"Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven..."** (Ps. 122:1 [LXX]); **"It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God..."** (*Φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖρας Θεοῦ ζῶντος*, Heb. 10:31); verse: **"Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us..."** (Ps. 122:3 [LXX]); **"O evil and adulterous generation, that hath not kept faith with its husband!..."** (*Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλίς*); "Glory...": **"Passing from one divine feast to another divine feast..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God..."**. After **"Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace"** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*, Luke 2:29), we immediately chant the Canon of Compline: **"Emulating the chaste wisdom of Joseph..."** (*Ἰωσὴφ τὴν σωφροσύνην ζηλώσαντες*) with the verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!"**. After the Ninth Ode, the Heirmos: **"Childbirth without corruption is alien to mothers, and virginity is strange to childbearing women..."** (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν μητέρων ἡ παρθενία*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos, Mary full of grace, the Lord is with thee..."** (*Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*), and the rest of Small Compline as on other Sundays of Great Lent.[^439]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ΜΕΓΑΛΗ ΔΕΥΤΕΡΑ ΕΙΣ ΤΟΝ ΟΡΘΡΟΝ 67.    Ὁ Ἱερεὺς Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός, ὁ Προεστὼς Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι, τὸ Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἱερεὺς Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης Κύριε ἐλέησον ιβ', Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν γ' καὶ τοὺς ψαλμοὺς Ἐπακούσαι σου Κύριος, κτλ. (ἀναγινωσκομένων τούτων βραδέως, ὁ Ἱερεὺς θυμιᾷ τὸν λαὸν διὰ κατζίου)· μετὰ τὸ Τρισάγιον, Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν, Σῶσον Κύριε κτλ. καὶ ὁ Προϊστάμενος λέγει τὸν Ἑξάψαλμον. Μετὰ τὴν Συναπτήν, ψάλλεται μετὰ τῶν ὡρισμένων αὐτοῦ Στίχων Ἐκ νυκτὸς ὀρθρίζει, τὸ Μέγα Ἀλληλουϊάριον δίς, καὶ δὶς τὸ μικρὸν καὶ τὸ Τροπάριον Ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος ἔρχεται ἐκ τρίτου δίς, μὲν ἀργῶς, ἅπαξ δὲ συντόμως· εἰς τὸ τέλος τοῦ πρώτου μὲν λέγομεν Προστασίαις τῶν Ἀσωμάτων σῶσον ἡμᾶς ³⁸, τοῦ δευτέρου δὲ συνάπτομεν τὸ χαρακτηριστικὸν τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, λέγοντες Πρεσβείαις τοῦ Ἁγίου ἢ τῶν Ἁγίων σῶσον ἡμᾶς, καὶ εἰς τὸ τρίτον Διὰ τῆς Θεοτόκου ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς· εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον³⁹ καὶ ἀκολούθως ψάλλονται τὰ γ' κατὰ σειρὰν Καθίσματα ἀργῶς, τὰ δύο ἀνὰ μίαν καὶ τὸ γ' δίς, καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Ἱερεὺς Καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ καταξιωθῆναι ἡμᾶς, καὶ 37. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 39. Συνήθως παραλείπεται τὸ Ψαλτήριον τῆς ἡμέρας ἐν ταῖς πλείσταις τῶν ἱερῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν κατὰ τοὺς ὄρθρους τούτους, εἴτε χάριν τῆς συντομίας εἴτε καὶ διότι εἰσὶ πέντε Καθίσματα ὡρισμένα καθ' ἑκάστην τῶν τριῶν πρώτων ἡμερῶν τῆς Μ. Ἑβδομάδος, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ἰδιαιτέρως τὸ πρωΐ ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἱερέως· ἀλλ' εὐχῆς ἔργον ἐστὶν ἵνα ἀναγινώσκηται μέρος τοὐλάχιστον τῶν πέντε Καθισμάτων εἰς ἀκρόασιν καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ, καθ' ὅσον μάλιστα τὸ Ψαλτήριον ἐθεωρήθη ἀνέκαθεν ἡ βάσις τῶν ἐκκλησιαστικῶν ἡμῶν προσευχῶν καὶ ἡ ἐπιούσιος πνευματικὴ τροφὴ ἑκάστου χριστιανοῦ, ὡς ἐσημειώθη ἐν τῇ Προθεωρίᾳ §3 ὑποσημ. 3.

Priest: “Blessed is our God {always}.” The Proestos: “Glory to You, our God, glory to You. O Heavenly King, {Comforter, the Spirit of Truth.}” Reader: Trisagion. Priest: “For Yours is {the Kingdom, and the Power....}” Reader: “{Amen.} Lord, have mercy” (12 times). {Glory, Now and ever,} “O come let us worship and bow down...” (3 times) and Psalm 19 “The Lord answer you in the day of trouble” {and Psalm 20 “In Your strength the king rejoices, O Lord.”} (While these Psalms are being read slowly, the Priest censes the people with the small hand censer (Katzion). After the Trisagion, “For Yours is,” then “Lord, save Your people.” {Glory, “Christ our God, Who were of Your own will lifted up on the Cross,” Now and ever, “O awesome and ever-present protection.”} The Exapsalmos is read by the Proistamenos (Dean of the Church). After the Litany, the Great “Alliluarion” [several Alleluia's] is sung with its assigned verses. “{My spirit seeks You early in the night watches.” Then the Troparion “Behold, the Bridegroom comes {in the middle of the night”} (three times — twice slowly and once rapidly). At the end of the first time, we chant “...through the protection of the Heavenly hosts save us.”³⁸ At the second time, we add the characteristic phrase of the Saint of the Church “...through the intercessions of Your Saint (or your Saints) save us.” At the third time we chant the “through the Theotokos have mercy on us.” {The Small Litany,} the {Kathismata of} the Psalter³⁹ and the 3 Kathismata {of the 37.
units.english_cohort_translation: 67.    The Priest: **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός*); the Superior [Proestos]: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι. Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."** (*Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*); the Reader: **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..."** (3 times) and the Royal Psalms: Psalm 19 [LXX]: **"The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble..."** (*Ἐπακούσαι σου Κύριος*), and Psalm 20 [LXX]: **"The king shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord..."** (While these Psalms are being read slowly, the Priest censes the people with the hand-censer [*katzion*]). After the Trisagion Prayers, the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; then the Troparia: **"Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance..."** (*Σῶσον Κύριε*); **"Glory..."**: **"Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God..."**; **"Both now and ever..."**: **"O awesome and unashamed protection, despise not our petitions, O Good One..."** (*Προστασία φοβερὰ καὶ ἀκαταίσχυντε*). The Dean or presiding Reader [Proistamenos] recites the Six Psalms. After the Great Litany, the Great Alleluia is chanted with its appointed verses: **"From night until morning my spirit seeks Thee early, O God, for Thy commandments are a light upon the earth"** (*Ἐκ νυκτὸς ὀρθρίζει*, Isa. 26:9 [LXX]), twice in slow melody and twice in brief melody. Then the Dismissal Troparion: **"Behold, the Bridegroom comes in the middle of the night, and blessed is the servant whom He finds watching..."** (*Ἰδοὺ ὁ Νυμφίος ἔρχεται*) three times (twice slowly and once rapidly). At the end of the first time we say: **"...through the protection of the Bodiless Hosts, save us!"** (*Προστασίαις τῶν Ἀσωμάτων σῶσον ἡμᾶς*);³⁸ at the second time we join the commemoration of the Patron Saint of the Church, saying: **"...through the intercessions of Saint [N.] (or: the Saints), save us!"** (*Πρεσβείαις τοῦ Ἁγίου ἢ τῶν Ἁγίων σῶσον ἡμᾶς*); and at the third time: **"...through the Theotokos, have mercy on us!"** (*Διὰ τῆς Θεοτόκου ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*). Then the Kathismata of the Psalter,³⁹ and next the three appointed Sessional Hymns [Kathismata] of the Triodion are chanted slowly in sequence: the first two once each, and the third twice. Immediately the Priest exclaims: **"And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel..."**, and...[^440]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 39. The Psalter of the day is customarily omitted in most of the Churches at these Matins services, either for the sake of brevity or because there are Five Kathismata designated for every day of the first three days of the Great and Holy Week, and it is read separately in the morning by the Priest; but the function of prayer is that at least part of the Five Kathismata be read for the hearing of the laity, in as much as we viewed the Psalter from the beginning as the basis of our ecclesiastical prayers and the necessary daily spiritual food of each and every Christian, as was noted in the Provisions [Protheoria] Paragraph 3, note 3.
units.english_cohort_translation: 39. The Psalter of the day is customarily omitted in most holy churches during these Matins services, either for the sake of brevity or because five Kathismata are appointed for each of the first three days of Holy Week, and it is read privately in the morning by the Priest; nevertheless it is devoutly to be wished that at least a portion of the five Kathismata be read in the hearing of the people also, inasmuch as the Psalter has ever been regarded as the foundation of our ecclesiastical prayers and the daily spiritual sustenance of every Christian, as was noted in the Introductory Chapter [Protheoria] § 3, footnote 3.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, μεθ' ὃ ὁ Ν' ψαλμὸς καὶ τὰ Τριῴδια ἀνὰ ς' ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ, καὶ αὖθις ὁ Εἱρμὸς ἀργῶς. ἡ Αἴτησις, τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τοῦ Τριῳδίου· εἶτα ἡ η' Ὠδὴ μετὰ τοῦ Εἱρμοῦ, καὶ ἀντὶ μὲν τοῦ Δόξα, λέγομεν Εὐλογοῦμεν Πατέρα, Υἱὸν καὶ Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα τὸν Κύριον, εἰς δὲ τὸν Εἱρμὸν Αἰνοῦμεν, εὐλογοῦμεν καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν τὸν Κύριον· εἶτα Τὴν θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτὸς καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ' Ὠδὴ μετὰ τοῦ Εἱρμοῦ αὖθις· εἰς τὸ τέλος ἡ Αἴτησις καὶ τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον ἐκ γ', καὶ ψάλλομεν τὰ β' τῶν Αἴνων Ἰδιόμελα εἰς δ', Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Κύριε ἐρχόμενος. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους⁴⁰, ἱστῶμεν Στίχους δ', καὶ ψάλλομεν τὰ β' τῶν Αἴνων Ἰδιόμελα εἰς δ'. Δόξα καὶ νῦν, Κύριε ἐρχόμενος, τὸ Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει χῦμα καὶ μετὰ τὸ Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν, ἄρχεται τῶν Ἀποστίχων ὁ α' Χορός, εἶτα Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι, τὸ Τρισάγιον, Κοντάκιον Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὠδύρετο, Κύριε ἐλέησον ιβ' ⁴¹, Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός, Ἐπουράνιε βασιλεῦ, τὰς τρεῖς Μ. μετανοίας, ἡ Ἀπόλυσις Ἐρχόμενος ὁ Κύριος ἐπὶ τὸ ἑκούσιον πάθος καὶ τὸ Δι' εὐχῶν⁴².

units.slavonic_incipit: Triodion} are chanted according to the
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Triodion} are chanted according to the following order: Kathisma Four of the Psalter and “Your Passion, as a perfect light raises and shines upon the world this present day.... from” Kathisma Five and “O invisible Judge, how have You been seen and gone to be killed by iniquitous men....” Kathisma Six and “The present day brings the light of the first fruits of the Passion of the Lord....” Glory, Now and ever. Repeat “The present day...” and immediately the Priest: “Let us supplicate the Lord our God,” and he reads the Gospel {Matthew 21:18-43.} {Reader:} Psalm 50; then the First Ode of the Triodion Canon (each verse repeated) and immediately slowly the Irmos “{Let us sing a song to the Lord” is repeated as a Katavasia.} The [Small] Litany, Kontakion, Ikos, Minologion and the Postscript of the Triodion. Then the Eighth Ode with its Irmos and, instead of Glory, we say “We bless Father, Son and Holy Spirit, the Lord.” Before the Irmos of the Eighth Ode is repeated as a Katavasia, the following verse is added: “We praise, we bless and worship the Lord.” Deacon: “{We magnify} the Theotokos and Mother of Light, {and honor her in hymns.}” Chanters: immediately the Ninth Ode with its Irmos. The Small Litany; Exapostilarion {“I see Your bridal chamber”} (3 times). At the Praises:⁴⁰ we sing the two Idiomela of the Praises (twice each). Glory, Now and ever, “O Lord, going to Your Passion”; the Small Doxology “To You belongs all glory” (read). After the Petitions: “Let us complete our morning supplication {to the Lord}.” The First Choir begins the Aposticha. At the conclusion of the Aposticha, the Priest: “It is a good thing to confess unto the Lord.” The Reader: the Trisagion, then the Kontakion “Jacob lamented {the loss of Joseph,}” “Lord have mercy” (12 times).⁴¹ Priest: “Wisdom. You Who are blessed, Christ our God, now and ever and to the ages of ages.” “O Heavenly King, {strengthen our faithful kings,}” the three Great Prostrations, and the Dismissal “{Glory to You, our God and our Hope, glory to You.} May Christ, our True God, the Lord, Who willingly came to His Passion for our salvation... Through the prayers {of our Holy Fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy upon us and save us}.”⁴² 40.
units.english_cohort_translation: ... reads the Gospel [Matthew 21:18–43: The Cursing of the Barren Fig Tree and the Parable of the Wicked Vinedressers]. After the Gospel, Psalm 50 is read; then the Three-Ode Canon [Triodion] in six Troparia in each Ode, and again the Heirmos slowly as Katavasia. The Small Litany, the Kontakion: **"Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph..."** (*Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὠδύρετο*), the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion. Then the Eighth Ode with its Heirmos; and instead of **"Glory..."**, we say: **"We bless the Lord: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit"** (*Εὐλογοῦμεν Πατέρα, Υἱὸν καὶ Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα τὸν Κύριον*). Before the Heirmos is repeated as Katavasia, we sing: **"We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord"** (*Αἰνοῦμεν, εὐλογοῦμεν καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν τὸν Κύριον*). Then the Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode is chanted with its Heirmos again. At the conclusion, the Small Litany and the Exaposteilarion: **"I see Thy bridal chamber adorned, O my Savior, and I have no wedding garment that I may enter therein; enlighten the robe of my soul, O Giver of Light, and save me!"** (*Τὸν νυμφῶνά σου βλέπω, Σωτήρ μου, κεκοσμημένον*) three times. At the Praises:⁴⁰ we set 4 verses, and we chant the two Idiomela of the Praises (twice each): [**"O Lord, coming unto Thy voluntary Passion..."** (*Κύριε, ἐρχόμενος πρὸς τὸ πάθος*) and **"O Lord, coming unto Thy Passion, Thou didst establish the hearts of Thy Disciples..."**]. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"O Lord, coming unto Thy Passion, Thou didst say unto Thy Disciples: Watch and pray..."** (*Κύριε, ἐρχόμενος πρὸς τὸ πάθος, τοὺς ἰδίους ἐστήριξας Μαθητάς*). The Small Doxology: **"To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God..."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) read plain. After the litany: **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν*), the First Choir begins the Aposticha. Then: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to sing unto Thy name, O Most High"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: **"Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph..."**, **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times);⁴¹ the Priest: **"Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"** (*Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*); the Reader: **"Confirm, O God, the holy Orthodox faith..."**; then the Prayer: **"O Heavenly King, strengthen our faithful civil authorities..."** (*Ἐπουράνιε βασιλεῦ*); the three Great Prostrations with the Prayer of Saint Ephrem the Syrian, and the Dismissal: **"May the Lord, coming unto His voluntary Passion for our salvation, Christ our true God..."** (*Ἐρχόμενος ὁ Κύριος ἐπὶ τὸ ἑκούσιον πάθος*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).⁴²[^441]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 42. This order of the Service is observed on the following two days, that is, on Holy Tuesday and Holy Wednesday, either in in the morning or in the evening, when the Matins of the Bridegroom takes place. If in the evening, then the Psalter is usually omitted and, instead, is read the following morning.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 68.    Τὸ πρωῒ ἀναγινώσκονται πέντε Καθίσματα τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου, εἶτα αἱ Ὧραι λιταὶ μετὰ τοῦ Ἀπολυτικίου Ἰδοὺ ὁ Νυμφίος ἔρχεται καὶ τοῦ Κοντακίου Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὠδύρετο· εἰς τὴν θ' Ὥραν ψάλλονται οἱ Μακαρισμοί, μετὰ δὲ τὴν Εὐχὴν Παναγία Τριάς, ἡ Ἀπόλυσις, καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ Ἑσπερινός.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 69.    Ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὰ Πρὸς Κύριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ ς' Ἰδιόμελα τῶν Αἴνων καὶ τῶν Ἀποστίχων, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δευτέραν Εὔαν, Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τῆς ἡμέρας, τὸ Κατευθυνθήτω καὶ εὐθὺς μετ' αὐτὸ Σοφία, ὀρθοί, ἀκούσωμεν... καὶ λέγεται τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ Λειτουργία τῶν Προηγιασμένων.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 70.    Τὸ ἑσπέρας ἀναγινώσκεται τὸ Μέγα Ἀπόδειπνον, ὡς εἴθισται, μετὰ δὲ τὸ Δόξα ἐν Ὑψίστοις Θεῷ, ἄρχεται τοῦ Τριῳδίου ὁ β' Χορός, ἀπ' θ' ὁ Εἱρμὸς Τὸν προδηλωθέντα ἐν ὄρει, τὸ Τρισάγιον καὶ ἀκολούθως τὸ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων κτλ. τοῦ Μ. Ἀποδείπνου· εἰς τὴν Συγχώρησιν ψάλλεται τὸ Σφαγήν σου τὴν ἄδικον Χριστέ.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 73.    Ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὰ Πρὸς Κύριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ ς' Ἰδιόμελα τῶν Αἴνων καὶ τῶν Ἀποστίχων, ἅπερ ἐψάλησαν ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἰδού σοι τὸ τάλαντον, Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τῆς ἡμέρας, τὸ Κατευθυνθήτω, τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας, καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ λοιπὴ Ἀκολουθία τῶν Προηγιασμένων.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 68.    In the morning, the five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathisma Four, Five, Six, Seven, and Eight] then the Hours with the Apolytikion “Behold, the Bridegroom comes....” and the Kontakion “Jacob lamented.” At the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes are chanted; after the prayer “All-holy Trinity,” the Dismissal, and Vespers begin.
units.english_cohort_translation: 68.    In the morning, the five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8]; then the plain Hours with the Dismissal Troparion: **"Behold, the Bridegroom comes..."** (*Ἰδοὺ ὁ Νυμφίος ἔρχεται*) and the Kontakion: **"Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph..."** (*Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὠδύρετο*). At the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes [Makarismoi] are chanted; and after the Prayer: **"All-Holy Trinity, Consubstantial Might..."** (*Παναγία Τριάς*), the Dismissal is given, and Vespers begins.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 69.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm {103} and Kathisma 18 [of the Psalter], at “Lord, I have cried,” we sing the six Idiomela of the Praises and the Aposticha. Glory, Now and ever, “Finding the Egyptian woman another Eve.” The Entrance with the Gospel, “O Gladsome Light,” and the Readings of the day: {Exodus 1:1-20 and Job 1:1-12.} Then the “Let my prayer arise” and immediately after it “Wisdom! Arise, let us hear [the Holy Gospel...]” and the Gospel {Matthew 24:3-35} and the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.
units.english_cohort_translation: 69.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]) and the Eighteenth Kathisma: **"Unto the Lord"** (*Πρὸς Κύριον*, Pss. 119–133 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 [LXX]), we chant the six Idiomela of the Praises and the Aposticha. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Finding the Egyptian woman another Eve, the serpent hastened through speech to trip up Joseph..."** (*Δευτέραν Εὔαν τὴν Αἰγυπτίαν εὑρὼν ὁ δράκων*). Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Old Testament Readings of the day: Exodus 1:1–20 [LXX] and Job 1:1–12 [LXX]. Then **"Let my prayer arise"** (*Κατευθυνθήτω*), and immediately after it: **"Wisdom! Stand upright! Let us hear the Holy Gospel"**, and the Gospel is read [Matthew 24:3–35: The Discourse on the Mount of Olives], and in sequence the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 70.    In the evening, as is customary, we read the Great Compline. After the Doxology “Glory to God in the Highest,” the Second Choir begins the Triodion Canon; after the Irmos of the Ninth Ode “The Establisher of the law,” the Trisagion, then “O Lord of Hosts” and the rest of the Great Compline. At the Forgiveness Rite, we chant “When the Virgin beheld Your unjust slaughter, O Christ, [she wailed].” GREAT TUESDAY 71.    The Matins of Great Tuesday is chanted unalterably according to the rubrics of Great Monday, Paragraph 67.
units.english_cohort_translation: 70.    In the evening, Great Compline is read, as is customary. After the Doxology: **"Glory to God in the highest..."** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*), the Second Choir begins the Three-Ode Canon [Triodion]; after the Heirmos of the Ninth Ode: **"Him that was prefigured upon the mountain..."** (*Τὸν προδηλωθέντα ἐν ὄρει*), the Trisagion Prayers, and following this: **"O Lord of hosts, be with us..."** (*Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*), and the rest of Great Compline. At the rite of Mutual Forgiveness, we chant: **"When the Virgin beheld Thy unjust slaughter, O Christ, she lamented: Woe is me, my Child!..."** (*Σφαγήν σου τὴν ἄδικον, Χριστέ*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 72.    In the morning, before the “You are blessed,” the five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata Nine, Ten, Eleven, Twelve and Thirteen], then the Hours with the Apolytikion “Behold the Bridegroom” and the Kontakion “Knowing the hour of the end.” {At the Ninth Hour the Beatitudes are chanted;} after the prayer “All-Holy Trinity,” the Dismissal, and Vespers begin.
units.english_cohort_translation: 72.    In the morning, before the exclamation: **"Blessed is our God..."**, the next five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13], and the plain Hours as yesterday with the Dismissal Troparion: **"Behold, the Bridegroom comes..."** and the Kontakion: **"Having in mind the hour of the end, O my soul..."** (*Τὴν ὥραν, ψυχή, τοῦ τέλους ἐννοήσασα*). At the Ninth Hour the Beatitudes are chanted; after the Prayer: **"All-Holy Trinity..."**, the Dismissal is given, and Vespers begins.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 73.    In Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (103) and Kathisma 18 [of the Psalter], at “Lord, I have cried,” we sing the six Idiomela of the Praises and Aposticha which were chanted in Matins. Glory, Now and ever, “The Master has entrusted you with a talent.” The Entrance with the Gospel, “O Gladsome Light,” the Readings of the day {Exodus 2:5-10 and Job 1:13-22.} Then “Let my prayer arise,” the Gospel of the day {Matthew 24:36-26:2} and the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.
units.english_cohort_translation: 73. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Behold, the Master entrusts thee with the talent, O my soul..."** (*Ἰδού σοι τὸ τάλαντον ὁ Δεσπότης ἐγχειρίζει, ψυχή μου*). Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Old Testament Readings of the day: Exodus 2:5–10 [LXX] and Job 1:13–22 [LXX]. Then **"Let my prayer arise"** (*Κατευθυνθήτω*), the Gospel of the day [Matthew 24:36–26:2: The Parables of the Ten Virgins and the Talents], and in sequence the remaining service of the Presanctified Gifts.

units.english_cohort_translation: Τὸ δὲ πρωῒ ἀναγινώσκονται ἕτερα ε' Καθίσματα τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου, καὶ οὕτω πληροῦται ὅλον τὸ Ψαλτήριον, καταλιμπανομένων τῶν β' Καθισμάτων, ΙΖ' καὶ ΙΗ', τοῦ μὲν ὡς ἐν τῷ Μ. Σαββάτῳ ἀναγνωσθησομένου, τοῦ δὲ ὡς συχνάκις ἐν ἑκάστῃ Προηγιασμένῃ, καὶ δὴ καὶ ἐν ταῖς τρισὶ τῆς ἑβδομάδος ταύτης ἀναγινωσκομένου, ἐπίσης ἀναγινώσκονται καὶ αἱ Ὧραι λιταί, ὡς κατὰ τὰς δύο προηγουμένας ἡμέρας, καὶ μετὰ τὴν Εὐχὴν *Παναγία Τριὰς* ἡ Ἀπόλυσις, καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ Ἑσπερινός.

units.english_cohort_translation: 76.    Ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὰ Πρὸς Κύριον, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ἱστῶμεν Στίχους ι' καὶ ψάλλομεν πάντα τὰ Στιχηρά, ἅπερ ὡς Αἶνοι καὶ Ἀπόστιχα ἐψάλησαν ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, *Κύριε ἡ ἐν πολλαῖς ἁμαρτίαις*, Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα τῆς ἡμέρας, τὸ *Κατευθυνθήτω*, καὶ τὸ ὡρισμένον Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ τῶν Προηγιασμένων Λειτουργία, ἥτις ἐστὶ καὶ ἡ τελευταία τῆς Μεγάλης Τεσσαρακοστῆς.

units.english_cohort_translation: In the morning, another five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata 14, 15, 16, 19, and 20], and thus the entire Psalter is completed, omitting the two Kathismata (17 and 18): the former because it is to be read on Great Saturday, and the latter because it is frequently read at every Presanctified Liturgy, and indeed was read on the three preceding days of this week. Likewise the plain Hours are read, as on the two preceding days; and after the Prayer: **"All-Holy Trinity..."** (*Παναγία Τριάς*), the Dismissal is given, and Vespers begins.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: In the morning, another five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata Fourteen, Fifteen, Sixteen, Nineteen and Twenty] and in this way the entire Psalter is completed, omitting the two Kathismata (Seventeen and Eighteen), the former because it will be read on Great Saturday, and the latter because it is read frequently in every Presanctified Liturgy and because it was already read on three days of this week. Also the Liti Hours are read as on the two previous days, and after the Prayer “All-Holy Trinity” the Dismissal and then Vespers begin.
units.english_cohort_translation: 76.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]) and the Eighteenth Kathisma: **"Unto the Lord"** (*Πρὸς Κύριον*, Pss. 119–133 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we set 10 verses, and we chant all the Stichera which were chanted as Praises and Aposticha at Matins. "Glory... Both now and ever...": the Doxastikon: **"O Lord, the woman who had fallen into many sins, having recognized Thy divinity, O Lord, taking upon herself the office of a myrrh-bearer..."** (*Κύριε, ἡ ἐν πολλαῖς ἁμαρτίαις*). Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Old Testament Readings of the day: Exodus 2:11–23 [LXX] and Job 2:1–10 [LXX]. Then **"Let my prayer arise"** (*Κατευθυνθήτω*), and the appointed Gospel [Matthew 26:6–16: The Anointing at Bethany and the Betrayal of Judas], and in sequence the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts, which is also the final one of Great Lent.

Also the Liti Hours are read as on the two previous days, and after the Prayer “All-Holy Trinity” the Dismissal and then Vespers begin.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: In the morning, another five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata Fourteen, Fifteen, Sixteen, Nineteen and Twenty] and in this way the entire Psalter is completed, omitting the two Kathismata (Seventeen and Eighteen), the former because it will be read on Great Saturday, and the latter because it is read frequently in every Presanctified Liturgy and because it was already read on three days of this week. Also the Liti Hours are read as on the two previous days, and after the Prayer “All-Holy Trinity” the Dismissal and then Vespers begin.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ΜΕΓΑΛΗ ΠΕΜΠΤΗ ΕΙΣ ΤΟΝ ΟΡΘΡΟΝ 78.    Μετὰ τὸν Ἑξάψαλμον καὶ τὴν Μ. Συναπτήν, ψάλλομεν μετὰ Στίχων τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα εἰς ἦχον πλ. δ' τετράκις, καὶ τὸ Τροπάριον Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι Μαθηταὶ ἐκ γ' καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Ὄρθρου τῆς ἡμέρας, εἶτα ὁ Ν' ψαλμός, καὶ ὁ Κανὼν ἄνευ Στίχων μετὰ τῆς Καταβασίας ἐν τέλει ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς. Ἀπὸ γ' Ὠδῆς τὰ Καθίσματα· ἀφ' ς' τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τοῦ Τριῳδίου. Μετὰ τὸν Εἱρμὸν τῆς η' Ὠδῆς, γίνεται ἡ Ἐκφώνησις Τὴν θεοτόκον καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ' Ὠδή, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον ἐκ γ', οἱ Αἶνοι εἰς δ', Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ὃν ἐκήρυξεν Ἀμνόν, τὸ Σοὶ Δόξα πρέπει χῦμα, Πληρώσωμεν τὴν Ἑωθινήν, καὶ τὰ δ' Ἀπόστιχα, Δόξα, Ὁ τρόπος σου δολιότης, Καὶ νῦν, Μυσταγωγῶν σου Κύριε, Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Τροπάριον τῆς Προφητείας, καὶ ἡ Προφητεία. Ἐκτενής, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

Μετὰ τὸν Εἱρμὸν τῆς η' Ὠδῆς, γίνεται ἡ Ἐκφώνησις *Τὴν θεοτόκον* καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ' Ὠδή, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον ἐκ γ', οἱ Αἶνοι εἰς δ', Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, *Ὃν ἐκήρυξεν Ἀμνόν*, τὸ *Σοὶ Δόξα πρέπει* χῦμα, *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν Ἑωθινήν*, καὶ τὰ δ' Ἀπόστιχα, Δόξα, *Ὁ τρόπος σου δολιότης*, Καὶ νῦν, *Μυσταγωγῶν σου Κύριε*, *Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Τροπάριον τῆς Προφητείας, καὶ ἡ Προφητεία. Ἐκτενής, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Trisagion; the Kontakion “Having transgressed more than the harlot”; “Lord, have mercy” (40 times), “You Who at all times,” the “O Virgin pure, spotless” etc., and the Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: ... Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: **"Having transgressed more than the harlot, O Good One, I have in no wise brought forth a flood of tears for Thee; but falling down in silence before Thee, I kiss Thy most pure feet with love..."** (*Ὑπὲρ τὴν πόρνην, Ἀγαθέ*); **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times), the Prayer of the Hours: **"Thou Who at all times and at every hour..."** (*Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ*), the nocturnal prayer: **"O spotless, undefiled, incorrupt, unblemished, pure Virgin, Lady Bride of God..."** (*Ἄσπιλε, ἀμόλυντε*), etc., and the Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 78.    {At Matins} after the Exapsalmos and the Great Litany, we sing “Alleluia” with its verses in Mode IV Plagal four times and the Troparion “When the glorious disciples {were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet” (3 times)} and then the Gospel of Matins of the day {Luke 22:1-39.} Then, Psalm 50, the Canon without verses and the Katavasia at the end of each Ode. After the Third Ode, the Kathismata {“He Who alone loves mankind,” Glory, “Having humbled Yourself through compassion,” Now and ever, “Eating, O Master, with Your disciples.”} After the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion, the Ikos, the Minologion and the Postscript of the Triodion. After the Irmos of the Eighth Ode is chanted {as a Katavasia}, the Deacon: “The Theotokos {and Mother...}” and the Ninth Ode is chanted. The Exapostilarion “[I see Your bridal chamber...]” (3 times.) At the Praises, we sing the four Stichira {“The rest of the assembly of the Jews ran forward,” “Judas, the transgressor, when at the supper he had dipped,” “Judas being a treacherous servant deceitfully” and “Judas, servant and traitor, disciple and plotter”}. Glory, Now and ever, “The Lamb whom Isaiah proclaimed goes of His own will.” The Small Doxology “To You glory belongs” (read). “Let us complete our morning prayer.” The four Aposticha: {“Today, the evil Sanhedrin has assembled against Christ.” The Verse “Who ate of my bread, has lifted his heel against me.” (Psalm 41:9); “Today Judas covers his face to love of the poor.” The Verse “When he goes out, he tells it abroad” (Psalm 41:6); “Your most deceitful way of life come to fulfillment.” The Verse “They denounced a wicked word against me” (Psalm 41:8); “O you faithful, let no man attend the Lord’s Supper.”} Glory, “Your most deceitful way of life,” Now and ever, “Initiating Your disciples, {You, O Christ.}” Then “It is a good thing to confess the Lord.” The Trisagion, the Troparion of the Prophecy, the Prophecy {Jeremiah 11:18-12:5}, Ektenis and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 78.    After the Six Psalms and the Great Litany, we chant the Alleluia with its verses in Tone 8 four times, and the Troparion: **"When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice; and to lawless judges he delivered Thee, the righteous Judge. Behold his goods, O lover of money, who for the sake thereof hanged himself! Flee from the insatiable soul that dared such things against the Master! O Lord, Who art good towards all, glory to Thee!"** (*Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι Μαθηταὶ*) three times. Immediately the Matins Gospel of the day is read: Luke 22:1–39 [LXX: The Institution of the Holy Eucharist and the Discourse at the Last Supper]. Then Psalm 50 is read, and the Canon is chanted without verses, with its Katavasia at the end of each Ode. After the Third Ode, the Sessional Hymns [Kathismata]: **"He Who created the lakes, the springs and the seas, desiring to teach us the highest humility, girded Himself with a towel and washed the feet of the Disciples..."**; "Glory...": **"Having humbled Thyself through compassion, Thou didst wash the feet of Thy Disciples..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"Eating, O Master, with Thy Disciples, Thou didst mystically reveal Thy holy slaughter..."**. After the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion: **"Having taken the Bread into his hands, the traitor extends them secretly to receive the price of Him Who fashioned man with His own hands; and Judas remained incorrigible, having dipped his hand into the dish with Christ..."**, the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion on the Mystical Supper, the Washing of the Disciples' Feet, the Agony in the Garden, and the Betrayal of Judas. After the Heirmos of the Eighth Ode is chanted as Katavasia, the Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode is chanted. Then the Exaposteilarion: **"I see Thy bridal chamber adorned, O my Savior..."** (*Τὸν νυμφῶνά σου βλέπω*) three times. At the Praises [Lauds], we chant the four Stichera: [**"The assembly of the Jews hastens together to deliver the Creator and Fashioner of all unto Pilate..."**, **"Judas the transgressor, having dipped his hand into the dish with Thee at supper..."**, **"Judas, being a treacherous servant, deceitfully devised betrayal..."**, and **"Judas, servant and deceiver, disciple and plotter, friend and devil, was made manifest from his deeds..."**]. "Glory... Both now and ever...": the Doxastikon: **"The Lamb whom Isaiah proclaimed comes of His own will to the slaughter..."** (*Ὃν ἐκήρυξεν Ἀμνόν*). The Small Doxology: **"To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God..."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) read plain. The litany: **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν Ἑωθινήν*), and the four Aposticha with verses from Psalm 40 LXX: [**"Today the evil Sanhedrin has assembled together against Christ..."**; verse: **"He that eats of my bread has lifted up his heel against me"** (Ps. 40:9 [LXX]); **"Today Judas hides his treachery under the pretense of love for the poor..."**; verse: **"When he went abroad, he spoke of the same"** (Ps. 40:6 [LXX]); **"Thy deceitful manner is revealed unto the end..."**; verse: **"An evil word have they poured out against me"** (Ps. 40:8 [LXX]); and **"O believers, let none of us who are uninitiated draw near to the Master's table..."**]. "Glory...": **"Thy deceitful manner..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"Initiating Thy Disciples, O Lord, Thou didst teach them, saying: O my friends, see that no fear separate you from Me..."** (*Μυσταγωγῶν σου, Κύριε*). Then: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord..."** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Troparion of the Prophecy: **"Thou Who didst endure slaps for the human race, O Christ God, deliver us from corruption and save our souls"**, and the Old Testament Prophecy: Jeremiah 11:18–12:5, 9–11, 14–15 [LXX: The Prophecy of the Innocent Lamb Led to the Slaughter]. The Augmented Litany [Ektenis], and the Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 79.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the five Idiomela of the Praises, repeating the first one for six. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Judas is truly the offspring of vipers, who ate the manna in the wilderness and murmured against the Nourisher..."** (*Γέννημα ἐχιδνῶν*). Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Old Testament Readings: Exodus 19:10–19 [LXX], Job...[^444]

units.english_cohort_translation: ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα· εἶτα ἡ μικρὰ Συναπτή, τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ Λειτουργία τοῦ Μεγάλου Βασιλείου, Χερουβικὸν καὶ Κοινωνικὸν *Τοῦ δείπνου σου τοῦ μυστικοῦ*, τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ ἀντὶ τοῦ *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, ἔπειτα *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, ἡ Ἀπόλυσις *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς . . . ὁ δι' ὑπερβάλλουσαν ἀγαθότητα ὁδὸν ἀρίστην τὴν ταπείνωσιν ὑποδείξας ἐν τῷ νίψαι τοὺς πόδας τῶν Μαθητῶν καὶ μέχρι Σταυροῦ καὶ ταφῆς συγκαταβὰς ἡμῖν, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς* κτλ. καὶ τὸ *Δι' εὐχῶν*.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα· εἶτα ἡ μικρὰ Συναπτή, τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ καθεξῆς ἡ Λειτουργία τοῦ Μεγάλου Βασιλείου, Χερουβικὸν καὶ Κοινωνικὸν Τοῦ δείπνου σου τοῦ μυστικοῦ, τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ ἀντὶ τοῦ Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς, ἔπειτα Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου, ἡ Ἀπόλυσις Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς . . . ὁ δι' ὑπερβάλλουσαν ἀγαθότητα ὁδὸν ἀρίστην τὴν ταπείνωσιν ὑποδείξας ἐν τῷ νίψαι τοὺς πόδας τῶν Μαθητῶν καὶ μέχρι Σταυροῦ καὶ ταφῆς συγκαταβὰς ἡμῖν, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς κτλ. καὶ τὸ Δι' εὐχῶν.
units.english_cohort_translation: 80.    Τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Μ. Πέμπτῃ ἑσπέρας, περὶ ὥραν α΄ τῆς νυκτός, εὐλογήσαντος τοῦ Ἱερέως, ὁ Προεστὼς λέγει *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν δόξα σοι*, τὸ *Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἱερεὺς *Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης *Κύριε ἐλέησον* ιβ΄, *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν* γ΄ καὶ τοὺς ψαλμοὺς *Ἐπακούσαι σου Κύριος* (βραδέως ἕως οὗ θυμιάσῃ ὁ Ἱερεύς), εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὰ Τροπάρια *Σῶσον Κύριε* κτλ. καὶ ὁ Προεστὼς τὸν Ἑξάψαλμον, ἡ Μ. Συναπτή, καὶ ψάλλεται τὸ σύντομον Ἀλληλουϊάριον ἐκ δ΄ καὶ τὸ Τροπάριον *Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι μαθηταὶ* δὶς ἀργῶς καὶ ἅπαξ συντόμως, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως τὸ [α΄.] Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Διαθήκης· εἰς τὸ τέλος εὐλογήσας τὸν λαὸν διὰ τρικηρίου, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*, ἀνέρχεται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον καὶ οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλουσι τὰ Ἀντίφωνα *Ἄρχοντες λαῶν* μέχρι τοῦ

Συναπτή, καὶ ψάλλεται τὸ σύντομον Ἀλληλουϊάριον ἐκ δ΄ καὶ τὸ Τροπάριον Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι μαθηταὶ δὶς ἀργῶς καὶ ἅπαξ συντόμως, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως τὸ [α΄.] Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Διαθήκης· εἰς τὸ τέλος εὐλογήσας τὸν λαὸν διὰ τρικηρίου, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, ἀνέρχεται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον καὶ οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλουσι τὰ Ἀντίφωνα Ἄρχοντες λαῶν μέχρι τοῦ 44. Ὅρα ἰδιαιτέραν κατ' ἔκτασιν Ἀκολουθίαν τῶν Ἁγίων Παθῶν, ὡς γίνεται ἐν τοῖς Πατριαρχείοις εἰς τὸ Παράρτημα.
units.english_cohort_translation: 44. Ὅρα ἰδιαιτέραν κατ' ἔκτασιν Ἀκολουθίαν τῶν Ἁγίων Παθῶν, ὡς γίνεται ἐν τοῖς Πατριαρχείοις εἰς τὸ Παράρτημα.

In place of the Cherubic Hymn, the Communion Hymn, and **"We have seen the true light"**, is chanted: **"Of Thy Mystical Supper, O Son of God, receive me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of the Mystery to Thine enemies, neither will I give Thee a kiss as did Judas, but like the thief do I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!"** (*Τοῦ δείπνου σου τοῦ μυστικοῦ*). Then: **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and the Dismissal: **"Glory to Thee, our God, our hope, glory to Thee. May He Who out of exceeding goodness showed humility to be the most excellent way when He washed the feet of the Disciples, and condescended unto the Cross and burial for our sake, Christ our true God..."** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς . . . ὁ δι' ὑπερβάλλουσαν ἀγαθότητα*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 38:1-21, 42:1-5; and Isaiah 50:4-11.} Then the Small Litany, the Trisagios Hymn, the Apostolos {1 Corinthians 11:23-32} and the Gospel {Matthew 26:2-20; John 13:3-17; Matthew 26:21-39; Luke 22:43-45; Matthew 26:40-27:2} and the rest of the order of the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great. The “Receive me today, {O Son of God}” is sung in place of the Cherubic Hymn, the Communion Hymn [Kinonikon] and “We have seen the [True] Light.” Then, “Blessed be the name [of the Lord],” and Dismissal: “Glory to You, our God {and our Hope, glory to You . . .} You Who because of Your exceeding goodness, did reveal humility as a virtuous way when You did wash the feet of Your Disciples; and did condescend to endure Crucifixion and Burial for our sakes, O Christ, our True God,” etc. Then Through the prayers {of our holy Fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ, our God, have mercy upon us and save us}.” SERVICE OF THE HOLY PASSION⁴⁴ 80.    On Holy and Great Thursday evening, around the First Hour of the night [7 p.m.] the Priest having given the opening blessing, the Proestos says “Glory to You, our God, glory to You. O Heavenly King, {Comforter.}” The Reader: the Trisagion. The Priest: “For Yours is [the Kingdom and the Power].” The Reader: “[Amen.] Lord, have mercy” (12 times), [Glory, Now and ever,] “O come let us worship [and bow down]” (3 times) and the Psalms “May the Lord answer you [in the day of trouble]” (Psalm 20) {and “The King shall have joy in Your strength” (Psalm 21)} (these are done slowly until the Priest has completed censing with the small hand censer), then the Trisagion, the Troparia “Lord, save Your people,” etc. {Glory, “O Christ our God, who was of Your own will.” Now and ever, “O awesome and ever-present protection.”} The Proestos reads the Exapsalmos, the Great Litany and then is sung the quick “Alleluia” (in 4) [with its verses], and the Troparion “When the glorious disciples” (twice slowly and once quickly). The reading of the First Gospel of the Testament {John 13:31-18:1} is done by the Archbishop {or Priest}, at the conclusion of which the Archbishop blesses the people with the Trikiri [three-stemmed candelabra of the Bishop], the choir singing “For many years, [Master].” Then the Archbishop ascends the Throne and the Choirs sing the Antiphons beginning with “The princes of the people [assembled against the Lord and his annointed]” until the Kathisma “Sustaining the disciples at the supper.” 44.
units.english_cohort_translation: 80.    On Holy and Great Thursday evening, around the First Hour of the night [7:00 p.m.], the Priest having given the blessing, the Superior [Proestos] says: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι. Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; the Reader: **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times), **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..."** (3 times) and the Royal Psalms: Psalm 19 [LXX]: **"The Lord hear Thee in the day of trouble..."** (*Ἐπακούσαι σου Κύριος*), and Psalm 20 [LXX]: **"The king shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord..."** (these are read slowly until the Priest finishes censing with the hand-censer [*katzion*]); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Troparia: **"Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance..."** (*Σῶσον Κύριε*); **"Glory..."**: **"Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God..."**; **"Both now and ever..."**: **"O awesome and unashamed protection, despise not our petitions, O Good One..."**; and the Superior [Proestos] reads the Six Psalms. The Great Litany; then the brief Alleluia is chanted four times with its verses, and the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: **"When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice; and to lawless judges he delivered Thee, the righteous Judge. Behold his goods, O lover of money, who for the sake thereof hanged himself! Flee from the insatiable soul that dared such things against the Master! O Lord, Who art good towards all, glory to Thee!"** (*Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι μαθηταὶ*) twice slowly and once rapidly. Then the First Gospel of the Testament [John 13:31–18:1: The Farewell Discourse of Christ to the Disciples] is read by the Archbishop [or the Priest]; at the conclusion, having blessed the people with the three-stemmed candlestick [*trikirion*], while the choirs chant: **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), he ascends the throne, and the choirs chant the Antiphons, beginning with: **"The rulers of the peoples took counsel together against the Lord and against His Anointed"** (*Ἄρχοντες λαῶν*) until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"Sustaining the disciples at the supper, Thou didst say: One of you will betray Me..."** (*Ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ τοὺς μαθητάς*).[^445]

O Heavenly King, {Comforter.}” The Reader: the Trisagion. The Priest: “For Yours is [the Kingdom and the Power].” The Reader: “[Amen.] Lord, have mercy” (12 times), [Glory, Now and ever,] “O come let us worship [and bow down]” (3 times) and the Psalms “May the Lord answer you [in the day of trouble]” (Psalm 20) {and “The King shall have joy in Your strength” (Psalm 21)} (these are done slowly until the Priest has completed censing with the small hand censer), then the Trisagion, the Troparia “Lord, save Your people,” etc. {Glory, “O Christ our God, who was of Your own will.” Now and ever, “O awesome and ever-present protection.”} The Proestos reads the Exapsalmos, the Great Litany and then is sung the quick “Alleluia” (in 4) [with its verses], and the Troparion “When the glorious disciples” (twice slowly and once quickly). The reading of the First Gospel of the Testament {John 13:31-18:1} is done by the Archbishop {or Priest}, at the conclusion of which the Archbishop blesses the people with the Trikiri [three-stemmed candelabra of the Bishop], the choir singing “For many years, [Master].” Then the Archbishop ascends the Throne and the Choirs sing the Antiphons beginning with “The princes of the people [assembled against the Lord and his annointed]” until the Kathisma “Sustaining the disciples at the supper.” 44.

Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..."** (3 times) and the Royal Psalms: Psalm 19 [LXX]: **"The Lord hear Thee in the day of trouble..."** (*Ἐπακούσαι σου Κύριος*), and Psalm 20 [LXX]: **"The king shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord..."** (these are read slowly until the Priest finishes censing with the hand-censer [*katzion*]); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Troparia: **"Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance..."** (*Σῶσον Κύριε*); **"Glory..."**: **"Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God..."**; **"Both now and ever..."**: **"O awesome and unashamed protection, despise not our petitions, O Good One..."**; and the Superior [Proestos] reads the Six Psalms. The Great Litany; then the brief Alleluia is chanted four times with its verses, and the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: **"When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice; and to lawless judges he delivered Thee, the righteous Judge. units.slavonic_incipit: Καθίσματος Ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ τοὺς μαθητάς,
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Καθίσματος Ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ τοὺς μαθητάς, μεθ' ὃ ἀναγινώσκεται τὸ β΄ Εὐαγγέλιον· εἰς τὸ τέλος ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ψάλλει Δόξα τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σου Κύριε δόξα σοι (ὅπερ καὶ εἰς πάντα τὰ λοιπὰ Εὐαγγέλια ἐπαναλαμβάνεται), καὶ ἄρχεται τοῦ δ΄ Ἀντιφώνου μέχρι τοῦ Καθίσματος Ποῖός σε τρόπος Ἰούδα καὶ τὸ γ΄ Εὐαγγέλιον· εἶτα ὁ Χορὸς τὸ ζ΄ Ἀντίφωνον μέχρι τοῦ Καθίσματος Ὢ πῶς Ἰούδας ὁ ποτέ σου μαθητής, καὶ τὸ δ΄ Εὐαγγέλιον· εἶτα ὁ β΄ Χορὸς τὸ ι΄ Ἀντίφωνον μέχρι τοῦ Καθίσματος Ὅτε παρέστης τῷ Καϊάφᾳ ὁ Θεός, καὶ τὸ ε΄ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ τοῦτο ὁ α΄ Χορὸς τὸ ιγ΄ Ἀντίφωνον μέχρι τοῦ ιε΄, ὅτε καὶ γίνεται ἡ ἔξοδος τοῦ Σταυροῦ, ὡς συνειθίσθη ἤδη σχεδὸν πανταχοῦ, εἶτα ἐξακολουθοῦσι τὰ Ἀντίφωνα μέχρι τοῦ Καθίσματος Ἐξηγόρασας ἡμᾶς, καὶ τότε λέγεται τὸ ϛ΄ Εὐαγγέλιον· εἶτα ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς τοὺς Μακαρισμούς· τούτων συμπληρωθέντων, ψάλλεται τὸ Προκείμενον Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς ἐκ γ΄ καὶ τὸ ζ΄ Εὐαγγέλιον, ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς καὶ τὸ η΄ Εὐαγγέλιον· εἶτα ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ἄρχεται τοῦ Κανόνος Πρὸς σὲ ὀρθρίζω, ἀνὰ δ΄ Τροπάρια ἀφ' ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς ἄνευ Στίχων καὶ εἰς τὸ τέλος ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς ὁ Εἱρμὸς ἀργῶς, ἡ Αἴτησις, τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τοῦ Τριῳδίου, ἡ Ἐκφώνησις Τὴν θεοτόκον, καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον ἐκ γ΄ καὶ τὸ θ΄ Εὐαγγέλιον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα δευτεροῦντες τὸ α΄ μετὰ τὸ

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Then, the Second Gospel {John: 18:1-28} is read, at the end of which the Second Choir sings “Glory to Your forbearance, O Lord, glory to You.” (This is also repeated at the end of each of the remaining Gospels.) And then begins the Fourth Antiphon until the Kathisma “What reason has made you, O Judas.” Then follows the Third Gospel {Matthew 26:57-75}, then the Choir sings the Seventh Antiphon until the Kathisma “O how did Judas who was once Your disciple.” Then the Fourth Gospel {John 18:28-19:16} is read; then the Second Choir begins the Tenth Antiphon until the Kathisma “When You, O God, had stood before Caiaphas.” Then the Fifth Gospel {Matthew 27:3-32} is read; after this, the First Choir begins Antiphon Thirteen {“The assembly of the Jews.”} After Now and ever, of the Fourteenth Antiphon {“Hail, You Who have received through”} [the faithful kneel]. At this point takes place the Procession of the Cross, as it has become customary almost everywhere. The Priest {carrying the Crucifix and preceded by the Altar Boys}, exits from the Sanctuary {and proceeds all around the Church, reciting in a recitative style the following hymn: “Today is hung upon the Tree, He who suspended the land in the midst of the waters” (3 times) which is repeated by the Choir.} The Antiphons continue until the Kathisma “You ransomed us {from the curse of the Law by Your precious blood}”; then the Sixth Gospel {Mark 15:16-32} is read. Then the First Choir begins the Beatitudes at the conclusion of which is chanted the Prokimenon “They divided my garments among themselves” (3 times) and the Seventh Gospel {Matthew 27:33-54} is read. Then, Psalm 50, and the Eighth Gospel {Luke 23:32-49} is read; then the First Choir begins the Canon [of the Triodion]: “Before You, rise in the morning” (with four Troparia at each Ode, without verses, and at the end of each Ode the Irmos is repeated slowly [as a Katavasia]). [After the Ode is sung,] the [Small] Litany, the Kontakion, the Ikos, the Minologion and the Postscript of the Triodion. Then, [Ode Eight of the Canon at the end of which the Deacon exclaims:] “The Theotokos [and the Mother of Light],” and the Ninth [Ode] is sung [at which time the Deacon censes. The Small Litany], the Exapostilarion [“O Lord, the thief on the same day”] (3 times). The Ninth Gospel {John 19:25-37} is then read. At the Praises: the 3 Idiomela with their verses are sung, repeating the first: [Verse 1 “Praise Him for His mighty acts, praise Him according to His excellent greatness” (Psalm 150:2); “Two most evil things has my first-born Israel done.” Verse 2 “Praise Him with trumpet sound, praise Him with lute and harp” (Psalm 150:3); “Two most evil things has my first-born Israel done.” Verse 3 “Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him
units.english_cohort_translation: ... Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"Sustaining the disciples at the supper, Thou didst say: One of you will betray Me; but Judas the transgressor did not wish to understand"** (*Ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ τοὺς μαθητάς*). After this, the Second Gospel [John 18:1–28: The Betrayal and Arrest in Gethsemane, and Jesus before Annas] is proclaimed; at the conclusion, the Second Choir chants: **"Glory to Thy forbearance, O Lord, glory to Thee!"** (*Δόξα τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σου Κύριε δόξα σοι*) (which is repeated at the end of each of the remaining Gospels). Then begins the Fourth Antiphon until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"What reason has made thee, O Judas, a traitor of the Savior? Did He cast thee off from the choir of the Apostles? Did He deprive thee of the gift of healings?..."** (*Ποῖός σε τρόπος Ἰούδα*). Then follows the Third Gospel [Matthew 26:57–75: Jesus before Caiaphas and the Denial of Peter]. Then the choir chants the Seventh Antiphon until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"O how did Judas, who was once Thy disciple, devise betrayal against Thee?..."** (*Ὢ πῶς Ἰούδας ὁ ποτέ σου μαθητής*). Then the Fourth Gospel [John 18:28–19:16: Jesus before Pilate and the Condemnation to Death] is read; then the Second Choir begins the Tenth Antiphon until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"When Thou, O God, didst stand before Caiaphas, and wast delivered unto Pilate, the Judge of all: the powers of heaven shook with fear..."** (*Ὅτε παρέστης τῷ Καϊάφᾳ ὁ Θεός*). Then the Fifth Gospel [Matthew 27:3–32: The Despair of Judas, Pilate Washes His Hands, and Simon of Cyrene Bears the Cross] is proclaimed; after this, the First Choir begins Antiphon Thirteen: **"The assembly of the Jews requested Pilate to crucify Thee, O Lord..."** (*Ὁ δῆμος τῶν Ἰουδαίων*), continuing through Antiphon Fourteen. At this point takes place the Procession of the Holy Cross, as has now become customary almost everywhere: the Priest, carrying the Holy Crucifix and preceded by candle-bearers and the hand-censer [*katzion*], exits from the Sanctuary and proceeds in solemn procession around the temple, chanting in a recitative melody: **"Today is hung upon the Tree, He Who suspended the earth upon the waters"** (*Σήμερον κρεμᾶται ἐπὶ ξύλου, ὁ ἐν ὕδασι τὴν γῆν κρεμάσας*) three times, which is repeated by the choir. The Antiphons continue until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"Thou hast ransomed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood; having been nailed to the Cross and pierced with the spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality upon mankind. O our Savior, glory to Thee!"** (*Ἐξηγόρασας ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου*); then the Sixth Gospel [Mark 15:16–32: The Mocking by the Soldiers and the Crucifixion at Golgotha] is read. Then the First Choir begins the Beatitudes [Makarismoi], at the conclusion of which is chanted the Prokimenon in Tone 4 three times: **"They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots"** (*Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς*, Ps. 21:18 [LXX]), and the Seventh Gospel [Matthew 27:33–54: The Crucifixion, the Darkness, and the Death of Jesus] is read. Then Psalm 50 [LXX], and the Eighth Gospel [Luke 23:32–49: The Penitent Thief and the Death of Christ] is read; then the First Choir begins the Canon of the Triodion: **"Early in the morning my soul rises unto Thee, O Word of God..."** (*Πρὸς σὲ ὀρθρίζω*) by Saint Cosmas the Melodist, with four Troparia at each Ode, without biblical verses, and at the end of each Ode the Heirmos is chanted slowly as Katavasia. After Ode 5 is sung, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us; for Mary beheld Him upon the Tree and said: Even though Thou dost endure the Cross, Thou art my Son and my God!"** (*Τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς σταυρωθέντα*), the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion. Then Ode 8 of the Canon, at the end of which the Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode is sung. The Small Litany, the Exaposteilarion in Tone 3: **"The wise thief in a single hour Thou didst account worthy of Paradise, O Lord; enlighten me also by the wood of the Cross, and save me!"** (*Τὸν λῃστὴν αὐθημερὸν*) three times. The Ninth Gospel [John 19:25–37: Jesus Commends His Mother to John, "It Is Finished", and the Piercing of His Side] is then read. At the Praises: the three Idiomela with their verses are sung, repeating the first: Verse 1: **"Praise Him for His mighty acts, praise Him according to the multitude of His greatness!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐπὶ ταῖς δυναστείαις αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 150:2 [LXX]); Idiomelon 1: **"Two evil deeds has My first-born son Israel committed: he has forsaken Me, the fountain of living water, and has dug for himself a broken cistern..."** (*Δύο καὶ πονηρὰ ἐποίησεν*). Verse 2: **"Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet, praise Him with lute and harp!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν ἤχῳ σάλπιγγος*, Ps. 150:3 [LXX]); Idiomelon 1 repeated. Verse 3: **"Praise Him with timbrel and dance, praise Him with strings and pipes!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν τυμπάνῳ καὶ χορῷ*, Ps. 150:4 [LXX]); Idiomelon 2: **"Every member of Thy holy flesh endured dishonor for our sake: the head with thorns, the face with spittings, the cheeks with buffetings, the mouth with vinegar mingled with gall, the ears with impious blasphemies, the back with scourgings, the hand with the reed, the whole body with extension upon the Cross, the limbs with nails, and the side with the spear. O Thou Who didst suffer for us and didst free us from passions, Who didst condescend to us in Thy love for mankind and didst raise us up: O Almighty Savior, have mercy on us!"** (*Ἕκαστον μέλος τῆς ἁγίας σου σαρκός*)...[^446]

May Christ, our true God, Who endured spittings, and scourgings, buffetings, and the Cross and Death for the salvation of mankind . . .” etc. Then, Through the prayers [of our holy Fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy upon us and save us.]”
units.english_cohort_translation: ... Verse 4: **"Praise Him with sounding cymbals, praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that has breath praise the Lord!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν κυμβάλοις εὐήχοις*, Ps. 150:5–6 [LXX]); Idiomelon 3: **"Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, all creation trembled; the foundations of the earth shook with fear of Thy might; for when Thou wast lifted up today, the Hebrew race perished..."** (*Σταυρωθέντα σε θεωροῦσα*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"They stripped Me of My garments and clothed Me in a scarlet robe; they placed upon My head a crown of thorns and gave a reed into My right hand, that I might smash them like a potter's vessels"** (*Ἐξέδυσάν με τὰ ἱμάτιά μου*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"I gave My back to scourgings, and My cheeks to blows, and I turned not My face from the shame of spittings; I stood before the tribunal of Pilate and endured the Cross for the salvation of the world"** (*Τὸν νῶτόν μου ἔδωκα εἰς μάστιγας*). Then the Tenth Gospel [Mark 15:43–47: Joseph of Arimathea Obtains the Body of Jesus and Lays It in a Tomb] is read, and immediately: **"To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God, and to Thee we send up glory: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) read plain. The Deacon: **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν*), and the Eleventh Gospel [John 19:38–42: The Burial of Jesus by Joseph and Nicodemus] is proclaimed. Then, immediately, the Aposticha: 1. **"All creation was altered with fear when it beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ; the sun was darkened, and the foundations of the earth were shaken..."** (*Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις ἠλλοιοῦτο φόβῳ*); the Verse: **"They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots"** (*Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου*, Ps. 21:18 [LXX]); 2. **"Why does the impious and lawless people imagine vain things? Why did they condemn to death the Life of all?..."** (*Λαὸς δυσσεβὴς καὶ παράνομος*); the Verse: **"They gave Me gall for My food, and for My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink"** (*Ἔδωκαν εἰς τὸ βρῶμά μου χολὴν*, Ps. 68:21 [LXX]); 3. **"Today, seeing Thee, O Word, hanging upon the Cross, the blameless Virgin wept with maternal sorrow..."** (*Σήμερον σὲ θεωροῦσα ἡ ἄμεμπτος Παρθένος*); the Verse: **"God is our King before the ages; He has worked salvation in the midst of the earth"** (*Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων*, Ps. 73:12 [LXX]); 4. **"Beholding Thee, the Creator and God of all, lifted up upon the Tree, all creation trembled..."** (*Ἐπὶ ξύλου βλέπουσα κρεμάμενον*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"O Lord, when Thou didst ascend the Cross, fear and trembling fell upon creation..."** (*Κύριε, ἀναβαίνοντός σου ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 8: **"The reed of denial has already been dipped by the unjust judges..."** (*Ἤδη βάπτεται κάλαμος ἀποφάσεως*). The Twelfth Gospel [Matthew 27:62–66: The Guard Set at the Tomb] is read by the Deacon from the ambo. At the conclusion of the reading, the Archbishop blesses him, and the choir chants: **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*). The Priest: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to sing unto Thy name, O Most High"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, Ps. 91:1 [LXX]). The Reader: the Trisagion Prayers. The Chanter: the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ransomed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood; having been nailed to the Cross and pierced with the spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality upon mankind. O our Savior, glory to Thee!"** (*Ἐξηγόρασας ἡμᾶς*) three times. The Deacon intones the Augmented Litany: **"Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee: hear and have mercy"**; **"Again we pray for all pious and Orthodox Christians"**; **"Again we pray for our Archbishop [N.]"**. The Priest gives the exclamation: **"For Thou art a merciful and loving God, and unto Thee we send up glory: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** The Deacon: **"Wisdom!"** The Priest: **"Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"** (*Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*). The Archbishop [or Superior / Proestos]: **"Confirm, O Lord God, the holy Orthodox faith of pious and Orthodox Christians unto ages of ages"** (*Στερεώσαι Κύριος ὁ Θεός*). The Priest: **"Glory to Thee, O God, our hope, glory to Thee. May Christ our true God, Who endured spittings, and scourgings, buffetings, and the Cross and Death for the salvation of the world, through the intercessions of His all-pure and blameless holy Mother, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν δόξα σοι· ὁ ἐμπτυσμοὺς καὶ μάστιγας...*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).[^447]

Why did they condemn to death the Life of all?..."** (*Λαὸς δυσσεβὴς καὶ παράνομος*); the Verse: **"They gave Me gall for My food, and for My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink"** (*Ἔδωκαν εἰς τὸ βρῶμά μου χολὴν*, Ps. 68:21 [LXX]); 3. **"Today, seeing Thee, O Word, hanging upon the Cross, the blameless Virgin wept with maternal sorrow..."** (*Σήμερον σὲ θεωροῦσα ἡ ἄμεμπτος Παρθένος*); the Verse: **"God is our King before the ages; He has worked salvation in the midst of the earth"** (*Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων*, Ps. 73:12 [LXX]); 4. **"Beholding Thee, the Creator and God of all, lifted up upon the Tree, all creation trembled..."** (*Ἐπὶ ξύλου βλέπουσα κρεμάμενον*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"O Lord, when Thou didst ascend the Cross, fear and trembling fell upon creation..."** (*Κύριε, ἀναβαίνοντός σου ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 8: **"The reed of denial has already been dipped by the unjust judges..."** (*Ἤδη βάπτεται κάλαμος ἀποφάσεως*). The Twelfth Gospel [Matthew 27:62–66: The Guard Set at the Tomb] is read by the Deacon from the ambo. At the conclusion of the reading, the Archbishop blesses him, and the choir chants: **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*). The Priest: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to sing unto Thy name, O Most High"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, Ps. 91:1 [LXX]). The Reader: the Trisagion Prayers. The Chanter: the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ransomed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood; having been nailed to the Cross and pierced with the spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality upon mankind. O our Savior, glory to Thee!"** (*Ἐξηγόρασας ἡμᾶς*) three times. The Deacon intones the Augmented Litany: **"Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee: hear and have mercy"**; **"Again we pray for all pious and Orthodox Christians"**; **"Again we pray for our Archbishop [N.]"**. The Priest gives the exclamation: **"For Thou art a merciful and loving God, and unto Thee we send up glory: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** The Deacon: **"Wisdom!"** The Priest: **"Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"** (*Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*). The Archbishop [or Superior / Proestos]: **"Confirm, O Lord God, the holy Orthodox faith of pious and Orthodox Christians unto ages of ages"** (*Στερεώσαι Κύριος ὁ Θεός*). The Priest: **"Glory to Thee, O God, our hope, glory to Thee. May Christ our true God, Who endured spittings, and scourgings, buffetings, and the Cross and Death for the salvation of the world, through the intercessions of His all-pure and blameless holy Mother, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν δόξα σοι· ὁ ἐμπτυσμοὺς καὶ μάστιγας...*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).[^447]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 81.    Περὶ τὴν α΄ πρωϊνὴν ὥραν τῆς ἡμέρας εὐλογήσαντος τοῦ Ἱερέως, ὁ Προεστὼς τὸ Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἱερεὺς Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης Κύριε ἐλέησον ιβ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν γ΄ καὶ ἀναγινώσκει τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς α΄ Ὥρας, εἶτα Δόξα, Σταυρωθέντος σου Χριστέ, Καὶ νῦν, Τί σε καλέσωμεν καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλων τὸ α΄ Ἰδιόμελον, ὁ β΄ μετὰ τοῦ Στίχου Ἵνα τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη, καὶ ψάλλει τὸ β΄, καὶ αὖθις ὁ α΄ Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τοῖς συλλαβοῦσί σε παρανόμοις· ἀκολούθως ἡ Προφητεία, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ εὐθὺς Τὰ διαβήματά μου, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Κοντάκιον Τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς σταυρωθέντα, Κύριε ἐλέησον μ΄, Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ καὶ ὁ Προεστὼς τὴν Εὐχήν· Χριστὲ τὸ φῶς, καὶ ἄρχεται ἡ γ΄ Ὥρα ⁴⁵.

units.english_cohort_translation: 81.    Around the First Hour of the morning [7:00 a.m.], the Priest having given the blessing, the Superior [Proestos] says: **"O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; the Reader: **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times), **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..."** (3 times), and he reads the Psalms of the First Hour: Psalm 5 [LXX]: **"Give ear to my words, O Lord..."**; Psalm 2 [LXX]: **"Why do the nations rage..."**; and Psalm 21 [LXX]: **"O God, my God, attend to me; why hast Thou forsaken me?..."**. Then "Glory...": **"When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, the tyranny was destroyed, and the power of the enemy was trampled underfoot; for neither an angel nor a man, but the Lord Himself saved us. Glory to Thee!"** (*Σταυρωθέντος σου Χριστέ*); "Both now and ever...": **"What shall we call thee, O full of grace?..."** (*Τί σε καλέσωμεν*). The First Choir begins chanting the first Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"Today the veil of the temple is rent in twain for the rebuke of the lawless, and the sun hides its rays beholding the Master crucified"** (*Σήμερον τοῦ ναοῦ τὸ καταπέτασμα*); the Second Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"As a sheep led to the slaughter wast Thou brought, O Christ King, and as an innocent lamb nailed to the Cross by lawless men on account of our sins, O Lover of mankind"** (*Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν*), preceded by the verse: **"Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain?"** (*Ἵνα τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη*, Ps. 2:1 [LXX]); and again the First Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Unto the transgressors who seized Thee, O Christ, Thou didst cry aloud: What harm did I do unto you, or wherein did I provoke you?..."** (*Τοῖς συλλαβοῦσί σε παρανόμοις*). Next, the Prophecy: Zechariah 11:10–13 [LXX] (The Thirty Pieces of Silver Cast into the Furnace in the House of the Lord); the Epistle: Galatians 6:14–18 (Glorying only in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ); and the Gospel: Matthew 27:1–56 (The Trial before Pilate, the Mocking, the Crucifixion, and the Death of Jesus). units.slavonic_diplomatic: 81.    Around the First Hour of the morning (7 a.m.), the Priest blesses and the Proestos says “O Heavenly King, {Comforter, the Spirit of Truth}.” The Reader: the Trisagion. The Priest: “For Yours is [the kingdom and the power].” The Reader: “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). Glory, Now and ever, “O come let us worship” (3 times) and he reads the Psalms of the First Hour [Psalms 5, 2, 21]. Glory, “O Christ, by Your being crucified {the tyrant has been destroyed},” Now and ever, “What shall we call you, {O full of grace?}” The First Choir sings the first Idiomelon {“Today the curtain of the Temple is rent”}. The Second Choir sings the second Idiomelon {“As a sheep to the slaughter You were brought, O Christ”} preceded by the Verse “Why have the nations raged?” [Psalm 2:1]. Then the First Choir sings Glory, Now and ever, “To the transgressors who took You, {O Christ, have You come and cried out aloud}.” The Reader: the Prophecy [Zacharias 11:10-13] and the Apostolos [Galatians 6:14-18]. The Gospel [Matthew 27:1-56] is then read. The Reader: “[Order] my steps [according to Your word].” The Trisagion, [Glory, Now and ever, “All-Holy Trinity, have mercy on us]; Kontakion “[O come let us all sing the praises of Him] Who was crucified for us,” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). “You Who at every season [and every hour].” And the Proestos says the prayer “O Christ, the [True] Light [do enlighten and sanctify every man who comes into the world],” and the Third Hour begins.⁴⁵ At the Third Hour, we begin as in the First Hour, {then Psalms 35, 109 and 51}. Glory, “O Lord, the Jews condemned You to death,” Now and ever, “O Theotokos, you are the [True] vine.” The Second Choir sings the first Idiomelon “Through fear of the Jews.” Then the First Choir sings the second Idiomelon {“Before Your precious Cross when the captains were mocking You, the captains of the heavenly host were,”} preceded by the Verse “Give ear to my words, O Lord; {give heed to my groaning}” {Psalm 5:1}. Then the Second Choir sings Glory, Now and ever, “Drawn upon the Cross {You have cried out aloud, O Lord}.” The Prophecy {Isaiah 50:4-11}. The Apostolos {Romans 5:6-10}; then the Gospel {Mark 15:16-41}. {Reader: “Blessed be the Lord God”} and the rest as above;
units.english_cohort_translation: At the Third Hour, the service begins as at the First Hour, then Psalms 34, 108, and 50 [LXX]. "Glory...": **"O Lord, the Jews condemned Thee to death, the Life of all..."** (*Κύριε, κατέκριναν σε Ἰουδαῖοι θανάτῳ*); "Both now and ever...": **"O Theotokos, thou art the true vine that blossomed for us the fruit of life..."** (*Θεοτόκε, σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος*). The Second Choir begins the first Idiomelon in Tone 6: **"Through fear of the Jews, Peter Thy friend and companion denied Thee, O Lord..."** (*Διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων*); then the First Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 6: **"Before Thy precious Cross, when the soldiers mocked Thee, O Lord, the angelic hosts were struck with dread..."** (*Πρὸ τοῦ τιμίου σου Σταυροῦ*), preceded by the verse: **"Give ear to my words, O Lord; understand my cry"** (*Τὰ ῥήματά μου ἐνώτισαι Κύριε*, Ps. 5:1 [LXX]). Then the Second Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Drawn upon the Cross, Thou didst cry aloud, O Lord: For which deed do the Jews wish to stone Me? Because I healed their paralytics?..."** (*Ἑλκόμενος ἐπὶ Σταυροῦ*). The Prophecy: Isaiah 50:4–11 [LXX] (The Obedient Servant Gives His Back to Scourges); the Epistle: Romans 5:6–10 (While We Were Still Sinners, Christ Died for Us); then the Gospel: Mark 15:16–41 (The Soldiers Mock Christ, the Crucifixion, and His Death on the Cross). The Reader: **"Blessed is the Lord God, blessed is the Lord day by day..."** (*Εὐλογητὸς Κύριος ὁ Θεός*), and the rest as above: the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us..."**, **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times), **"Thou Who at all times..."**, the Prayer of Saint Mardarios: **"O Master God, Father Almighty, Lord, Only-Begotten Son Jesus Christ, and Holy Spirit, one Divinity, one Power, have mercy on me a sinner..."** (*Δέσποτα Θεέ*), and the Sixth Hour begins.[^448]
