units.slavonic_diplomatic: 82.    Εἰς τὴν ϛ΄ Ὥραν, ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλει τὸ α΄ Ἰδιόμελον, ὁ β΄ μετὰ τοῦ Στίχου Ἔδωκαν εἰς τὸ βρῶμά μου χολὴν τὸ β΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δεῦτε χριστοφόροι λαοί, ἡ Προφητεία, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον κτλ. ὡς ἄνωθεν, ἡ Εὐχὴ Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων, καὶ ἄρχεται ἡ θ΄ Ὥρα.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 83.    Εἰς τὴν θ΄ Ὥραν, ὁ β΄ Χορὸς ἄρχεται τοῦ α΄ Ἰδιομέλου, τὸ β΄ λέγει ὁ α΄ μετὰ τοῦ Στίχου Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς, τὸ δὲ τέλος ἀπὸ τοῦ Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι λαμβάνει ὁ β΄ Χορός· ὁ δὲ α΄ ἄρχεται Δόξα Πατρί, ὁ β΄ Καὶ νῦν καὶ ἀεί, καὶ ὁ Κανονάρχης ἐρχόμενος εἰς τὸ μέσον τοῦ Ναοῦ ἀναγινώσκει κατὰ τὸ ὕφος τοῦ Ἀποστόλου τὸ Στιχηρὸν Σήμερον κρεμᾶται ἐπὶ ξύλου, ὁ ἐν ὕδασι τὴν γῆν κρεμάσας ἐκ γ΄, καὶ τὸ τέλος Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὰ πάθη Χριστὲ ὡσαύτως ἐκ γ΄, εἶτα ψάλλεται τὸ αὐτὸ Στιχηρὸν ὑπ' ἀμφοτέρων τῶν Χορῶν κατὰ Στίχον, ἡ Προφητεία, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Κοντάκιον κτλ. ἡ Εὐχὴ Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ, ἡ Ἀπόλυσις καὶ ἄρχεται

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 82.    The Sixth Hour begins as the previous two Hours [Psalms 54, 140, and 91]; {Glory, “You, O Christ God, worked out salvation.” Now and ever, “As there is no boldness in us because of the multitude of our sins.” The First Choir sings the first Idiomelon {“This is what the Lord said to the Jews.” The Second Choir sings the Second Idiomelon “You, the lawmakers of Israel,”} preceded by the Verse “They gave me poison for food, {and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink}.” {Psalm 69:21}. Then the First Choir sings Glory, Now and ever, “Come, you people, bearers of Christ {and see what Judas}.” The Prophecy {Isaiah 52:13-54:1}. The Apostolos {Hebrews 2:11-18} and the Gospel {Luke 23:32-49}. {The Reader: “Let Your tender mercies, O Lord, speedily go before us.”} Then the rest as before with the prayer “O God and Lord {of the angelic hosts},” and the Ninth Hour begins.
units.english_cohort_translation: 82.    The Sixth Hour begins as the previous two Hours, with Psalms 53, 139, and 90 [LXX]. "Glory...": **"Thou hast worked salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God; Thou didst stretch out Thy most pure hands upon the Cross; Thou didst gather all the nations that cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord, glory to Thee!"** (*Εἰργάσω σωτηρίαν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς*); "Both now and ever...": **"Seeing that we have no boldness because of our manifold sins, do thou entreat Him Who was born of thee, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν παρρησίαν*). The First Choir chants the first Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"Thus says the Lord unto the Jews: My people, what have I done unto you, or wherein have I grieved you? Your blind have I given sight, your lepers have I cleansed, the man lying on his pallet have I restored. My people, what have I done unto you, and wherewith have you repaid Me? Instead of manna, gall; instead of water, vinegar; instead of loving Me, you have nailed Me to the Cross!..."** (*Τάδε λέγει Κύριος πρὸς Ἰουδαίους*); the Second Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"O lawgivers of Israel, Jews and Pharisees, the choir of the Apostles cries aloud unto you: Behold the Temple which you destroyed; behold the Lamb Whom you crucified and delivered unto the tomb!..."** (*Οἱ νομοθέται Ἰσραήλ*), preceded by the verse: **"They gave Me gall for My food, and for My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink"** (*Ἔδωκαν εἰς τὸ βρῶμά μου χολὴν*, Ps. 68:21 [LXX]). Then the First Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Come, O Christ-bearing peoples, let us behold what counsel Judas the traitor took with the lawless priests against our Savior..."** (*Δεῦτε χριστοφόροι λαοί*). Next, the Prophecy: Isaiah 52:13–54:1 [LXX] (The Suffering Servant: He Was Wounded for Our Transgressions); the Epistle: Hebrews 2:11–18 (He Who Sanctifies and Those Who Are Sanctified Are All from One); and the Gospel: Luke 23:32–49 (The Crucifixion, the Penitent Thief, the Veil Rent, and the Death of Jesus). The Reader: **"Let Thy tender mercies speedily prevent us, O Lord, for we are brought very low..."** (*Ταχὺ προκαταλαβέτωσαν ἡμᾶς οἱ οἰκτιρμοί σου*, Ps. 78:8 [LXX]), the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us..."**, **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times), **"Thou Who at all times..."**, the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great: **"O God and Lord of powers, and Maker of all creation, Who through the compassion of Thine inscrutable mercy didst send down Thine Only-Begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, for the salvation of our race..."** (*Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*), and the Ninth Hour begins.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 83.    We begin the Ninth Hour as we did the previous three Hours {but with Psalms 69, 70, and 86; Glory, “The thief said, as he beheld the Author of life, hanging upon the Cross.” Now and ever, “O good Lord, for our sakes You were born of a Virgin and have endured crucifixion.”} The Second Choir sings the first Idiomelon {“A dazzling wonder it was to see the Maker of heaven and earth.”} Then the First Choir sings the second Idiomelon “When the transgressors nailed the Lord of glory upon the Cross,” preceded by the Verse “They divided my garments among them.” The Second Choir sings the conclusion to the above Idiomelon: “...with the Father and the Spirit.” The First Choir sings “Glory to the Father {and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit}.” The Second Choir, “Now and ever {and to the ages of ages. Amen.}” At this point the Canonarch, coming to the middle of the Church, {stands facing the Crucifix and} intones in the manner of the Apostolos the Stichiron:
units.english_cohort_translation: 83.    The Ninth Hour begins as the previous three Hours, with Psalms 68, 69, and 85 [LXX]. "Glory...": **"When the thief beheld the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, he said: If Thou wert not God incarnate Who art crucified with us, the sun would not have hidden its rays, nor would the earth have shaken with trembling. But O Thou Who endurest all things, remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!"** (*Ὁρῶν ὁ λῃστὴς τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς*); "Both now and ever...": **"O Good One, Who for our sake wast born of a Virgin and didst endure crucifixion, Who by death didst despoil death and didst manifest the Resurrection as God, despise not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thine own hand..."** (*Ὁ δι' ἡμᾶς γεννηθεὶς ἐκ Παρθένου*). The Second Choir begins the first Idiomelon in Tone 7: **"A marvelous and fearful wonder it was to behold today: the Creator of heaven and earth hangs upon the Tree; He Who suspended the earth upon the waters is transfixed with nails; the sun hides its rays at the sight of the Master dishonored..."** (*Θάμβος ἦν κατιδεῖν τὸν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς Ποιητήν*); then the First Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 2: **"When the transgressors nailed the Lord of glory upon the Cross, they mocked Him and said: If Thou art the Son of God, save Thyself and come down from the Cross!..."** (*Ὅτε σε σταυρῷ προσήλωσαν παράνομοι*), preceded by the verse: **"They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots"** (*Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς*, Ps. 21:18 [LXX]). The Second Choir takes up the conclusion to this Idiomelon: **"...Together with the Father and the Holy Spirit!"** (*Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι*). The First Choir chants: **"Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit"**; the Second Choir: **"Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** At this point the Canonarch, coming into the middle of the temple [before the Holy Cross], intones in the recitative manner of the Epistle the solemn Sticheron:

units.english_cohort_translation: Then this same Sticheron is chanted by both choirs verse by verse. The Prophecy: Jeremiah 11:18–12:5, 9–11, 14–15 [LXX] (The Innocent Lamb Led to the Slaughter); the Epistle: Hebrews 10:19–31 (A New and Living Way Opened through the Veil of His Flesh); the Gospel: John 19:23–37 (The Crucifixion, the Parting of the Garments, "It Is Finished", and the Piercing of His Side). The Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Kontakion: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us..."**; **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times); **"Thou Who at all times..."**; the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great: **"O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who hast patiently endured our transgressions, and hast brought us even unto this present hour, in which, hanging upon the life-creating Tree, Thou didst open the way into Paradise unto the penitent thief, and by death didst destroy death..."** (*Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ*); the Dismissal, and begins...[^449]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 84.    Ἐν τῷ Μ. Ἑσπερινῷ, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακόν, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ τῶν Ἀποστίχων ε΄ Ἰδιόμελα Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις [Δὶς] κτλ. εἰς ϛ΄. Δόξα, Ὢ πῶς ἡ παράνομος συναγωγή, Καὶ νῦν, Φοβερὸν καὶ παράδοξον μυστήριον, Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, τὸ Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ εὐθὺς τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα, ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ ἀπ' ἄμβωνος τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· τὸ Εἴπωμεν πάντες, τὸ Καταξίωσον, Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν, καὶ μετὰ τὸ Εἴη τὸ κράτος, οἱ Χοροὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὴν βορείαν Πύλην τοῦ ἁγίου Βήματος καὶ ἄρχονται ψάλλοντες τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, ἓξ δὲ Ἱερεῖς ἀσκεπεῖς ἐνδεδυμένοι φελώνια καὶ αἴροντες μετ' εὐλαβείας ἐπὶ κεφαλῆς τὸν ἐπιτάφιον, ἐξ ὧν ὁ Μέγας Ἀρχιμανδρίτης φέρει ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον, ἐξέρχονται τοῦ ἱεροῦ Βήματος προπορευομένων τῶν λαμπάδων, τῶν ἑξαπτερύγων, τῶν Ψαλτῶν, τοῦ Πριμικηρίου μετὰ τοῦ Διβαμβούλου καὶ τῶν Διακόνων θυμιώντων ἔρχονται εἰς τὸ μέσον τοῦ Ναοῦ ὅπου ἵσταται ηὐτρεπισμένον τὸ Κουβούκλιον, καὶ οἱ μὲν Χοροὶ τῶν Ψαλτῶν ἵστανται κατὰ σειρὰν ψάλλοντες τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν Ἀποστίχων, οἱ δὲ Ἱερεῖς φέροντες ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον, ποιοῦσι τρεῖς κύκλους περὶ τὸ Κουβούκλιον, εἶτα τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ἐντὸς τοῦ Κουβουκλίου, καὶ ὁ Μ. Ἐκκλησιάρχης ῥαίνει μὲ εὔοσμα ἄνθη αὐτό, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης κατερχόμενος τοῦ Θρόνου προσέρχεται, ἀσπάζεται τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον καὶ τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον καὶ εὐλογήσας τὸν λαόν, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, ἀνέρχεται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον, οἱ δὲ ἅγιοι Ἀρχιερεῖς προσερχόμενοι ἀνὰ δύο ἀσπάζονται ἐπίσης καὶ ἔπειτα λαμβάνουσι παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἄνθη, ὡσαύτως καὶ πάντες

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 84.    At Great Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm, at “Lord, I have cried,” we chant the following five Idiomela of the Aposticha: “1. All the Creation {was changed by fear}.” (2 times); “2. O impious and transgressing people”; 3. {“Today, as the blameless Virgin sees You, O Word, hung”; “4. Beholding You, O Christ, the Creator and God”; “5. Today, the Master of the Creation stands before Pilate}”; Glory, “O what a wicked assembly {to condemn to death the Maker of all}”; Now and ever, “A fearful and most strange and glorious mystery {is seen taking place here}.” The Entrance with the Gospel, “O Gladsome Light,” the Prophecies {Exodus 33:11-23; Job 42:12-17; Isaiah 52:13-54:1.} The Apostolos {1 Corinthians 1:18-31; 2:1-2} and the Gospel {Matthew 27:1-38; Luke 23:39-43, Matthew 27:39-54, John 19:31-37, Matthew 27:55-61} read from the Pulpit. [At this point as we read “Now, when the evening had come, there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph,” the body of the Lord is taken down from the Cross and is wrapped in a clean white sheet. When the Gospel reading is completed, the Priest receives the Body and carries it into the Sanctuary.] Then the Petitions: “Let us say with all our soul.... Vouchsafe, O Lord.... Let us complete our evening supplication....” After the Exclamation “Blessed and glorified be the might {of Your Kingdom...}” and the choirs assemble by the North Door of the Holy Vima [Sanctuary] and begin singing the Aposticha. Six Priests with heads uncovered (not wearing the Kamilafchion) vested with Phelonia [and Epitrachilia] bear the Epitaphios upon their heads with reverence. The Great Archimandrite, one of the six, carries also the Holy Gospel in his right hand. They exit from the [North Door of the] Holy Vima being preceded by Candles, Fans (Exapteryga), the Chanters, the Dean of the Church
units.english_cohort_translation: 84.    At Great Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the five Idiomela of the Aposticha for six verses: 1. **"All creation was altered with fear when it beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ..."** (*Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις ἠλλοιοῦτο φόβῳ*) (twice); 2. **"Why does the impious and lawless people imagine vain things?..."** (*Λαὸς δυσσεβὴς καὶ παράνομος*); 3. **"Today, seeing Thee, O Word, hanging upon the Cross, the blameless Virgin wept..."** (*Σήμερον σὲ θεωροῦσα ἡ ἄμεμπτος Παρθένος*); 4. **"Beholding Thee, the Creator and God of all, lifted up upon the Tree..."** (*Ἐπὶ ξύλου βλέπουσα κρεμάμενον*); 5. **"Today the Master of creation stands before Pilate..."** (*Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης τῆς κτίσεως*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"O how did the lawless assembly condemn the King of creation to death!..."** (*Ὢ πῶς ἡ παράνομος συναγωγή*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"A fearful and marvelous mystery is seen accomplished today: He Who is untouchable is held fast..."** (*Φοβερὸν καὶ παράδοξον μυστήριον*). The Entrance is made with the Gospel Book; **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*); and immediately the Readings: Exodus 33:11–23 [LXX] (The Lord Speaks with Moses Face to Face, and Moses Beholds the Glory of God from the Cleft of the Rock); Job 42:12–17 [LXX] (The Lord Blesses the Latter End of Job More than His Beginning); and Isaiah 52:13–54:1 [LXX] (The Fourth Servant Song: "Behold, My Servant Shall Prosper"). The Epistle: 1 Corinthians 1:18–31; 2:1–2 (The Word of the Cross is Foolishness to Those Who Perish, but to Us Who Are Saved It Is the Power of God); and the Gospel: Matthew 27:1–38; Luke 23:39–43; Matthew 27:39–54; John 19:31–37; Matthew 27:55–61 (The Composite Passion Gospel of the Crucifixion, the Death, and the Deposition of the Lord) read from the ambo. [At this point, while the words are read: "Now when evening was come, there came a rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph...", the body of the Lord is taken down from the Cross and wrapped in a clean linen sheet. When the Gospel reading is completed, the Priest receives the Sacred Body and carries It into the Sanctuary]. Then the litanies: **"Let us all say with our whole soul..."** (*Εἴπωμεν πάντες*); **"Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin..."** (*Καταξίωσον*); **"Let us complete our evening supplication unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν*). After the exclamation: **"Blessed and glorified be the might of Thy kingdom: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εἴη τὸ κράτος*), the choirs assemble by the northern door of the Sanctuary and begin chanting the Aposticha. Six Priests with heads uncovered (not wearing the kamilavkion), vested in phelonia [and epitrachilia], bearing the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] upon their heads with reverence, among whom the Great Archimandrite carries also the Holy Gospel Book in his right hand, exit from the Sanctuary preceded by candles, processional fans [hexapteryga], the chanters, the Dean of the church [Primikirios] with the two-branched candlestick [divamvoulon], and the deacons censing; they advance to the middle of the temple, where the Tomb [Sepulchre / Kuvuklion] stands prepared...[^450]

Then the litanies: **"Let us all say with our whole soul..."** (*Εἴπωμεν πάντες*); **"Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin..."** (*Καταξίωσον*); **"Let us complete our evening supplication unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν*). After the exclamation: **"Blessed and glorified be the might of Thy kingdom: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εἴη τὸ κράτος*), the choirs assemble by the northern door of the Sanctuary and begin chanting the Aposticha. Six Priests with heads uncovered (not wearing the kamilavkion), vested in phelonia [and epitrachilia], bearing the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] upon their heads with reverence, among whom the Great Archimandrite carries also the Holy Gospel Book in his right hand, exit from the Sanctuary preceded by candles, processional fans [hexapteryga], the chanters, the Dean of the church [Primikirios] with the two-branched candlestick [divamvoulon], and the deacons censing; they advance to the middle of the temple, where the Tomb [Sepulchre / Kuvuklion] stands prepared...[^450]

units.slavonic_incipit: carrying a Divamvulon, and the Deacons
units.slavonic_diplomatic: carrying a Divamvulon, and the Deacons censing; when they arrive in the center of the Church where the Sepulchre [Kuvuklion] stands ornamented, the choirs of chanters stand in their accustomed place and continue the rest of the Aposticha. The Priests, who are bearing the Epitaphios [a cloth depicting Christ's burial] upon their heads, circle the Sepulchre three times, then they place the Epitaphios inside the Sepulchre and the Great Ecclesiarch sprinkles it with sweet-smelling flowers.
units.english_cohort_translation: ... and the ecclesiastical officials. In the meantime, when they arrive in the center of the temple where the Tomb [Sepulchre / Kuvuklion] stands decorated, the choirs of chanters stand in their appointed order and continue chanting the rest of the Aposticha. The Priests, bearing the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] upon their heads, make three circuits around the Tomb, then place the Epitaphios within the Tomb, and the Great Ecclesiarch sprinkles it with fragrant flowers. The Patriarch descends from the throne and approaches, venerates the Holy Gospel Book and the Epitaphios, and blesses the people while the choirs chant: **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*); after this he ascends the throne. The rest of the Bishops approach two by two, venerate, and then receive flowers from the Patriarch, as do all the other ecclesiastical officials. Meanwhile, the Second Choir slowly and melodiously chants the Doxastikon in Tone 5: "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, when Joseph with Nicodemus took Thee down from the Tree..."** (*Σὲ τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον τὸ φῶς*). Then: **"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace, O Master, according to Thy word..."** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*); the Reader recites the Trisagion Prayers; then the Dismissal Troparia in Tone 2:

units.slavonic_diplomatic: The Patriarch descends from the Throne and venerates the Gospel and the Epitaphios. He blesses the people while the choirs sing “For many years, [Master]” after which he returns to the Throne. The rest of the Bishops approach two by two, venerate and then receive flowers from the Patriarch, as do all the other Ecclesiastical officials.
units.english_cohort_translation:
1. **"The noble Joseph, taking down Thine undefiled Body from the Tree, wrapped It in a clean linen shroud and with sweet spices, and laid It for burial in a new tomb"** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ, ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου καθελὼν τὸ ἄχραντόν σου Σῶμα, σινδόνι καθαρᾷ εἱλήσας καὶ ἀρώμασιν, ἐν μνήματι καινῷ κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*), chanted until **"and laid It for burial"** (*κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*);
2. **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women the angel stood by the tomb and cried aloud: Myrrh is fitting for the dead, but Christ has shown Himself foreign to corruption"** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί, παρὰ τὸ μνῆμα ἐπιστάς, ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα· Τὰ μύρα τοῖς θνητοῖς ὑπάρχει ἁρμόδια, Χριστὸς δὲ διαφθορᾶς ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*), chanted until **"foreign to corruption"** (*διαφθορᾶς ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*).

Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτὴρ ἅπαξ καὶ τοῦτο ἀργῶς·⁴⁹ ἀφ' ϛ΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἡμέρας, καὶ ἀκολούθως ἡ ζ΄ καὶ ἡ η΄ Ὠδὴ τοῦ Κανόνος· εἶτα Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός, καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Κανόνος Ὠδή, εἰς τὸ τέλος τῆς θ΄ ἐξέρχεται ὁ Πατριάρχης ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἱεροῦ Βήματος ἐνδεδυμένος ἅπασαν τὴν ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν, προπορευομένων τῶν Ἁγίων Ἀρχιερέων, καὶ ψάλλων τὸ Ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τάφῳ, προχωρεῖ πρὸς τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον καὶ θυμιᾷ αὐτὸν σταυροειδῶς, ἀκολούθως δὲ πάντα τὸν λαόν· οἱ δὲ Ἀρχιερεῖς ἱστάμενοι ἐν χοροστασίᾳ ψάλλουσι τὰ ἐγκώμια τῆς α΄ Στάσεως, ἕως οὗ ἐπιστρέψῃ ὁ Πατρι

units.english_cohort_translation: 85.    Around the Seventh Hour of the night [1:00 a.m.]⁴⁶ the Amomos [Psalm 118 LXX: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way..."] and the Old Testament readings omitted from the Vespers of Great Saturday are customarily read here.⁴⁷ Then the Priest says: **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"**; the Superior [Proestos]: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; the Reader: the Troparia: **"Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance..."** (*Σῶσον Κύριε*); **"Glory..."**: **"Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God..."**; **"Both now and ever..."**: **"O awesome and unashamed protection, all-lauded Theotokos..."**; and the Six Psalms [Ps. 3, 37, 62, 87, 102, and 142 LXX]. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*), the Dismissal Troparia in Tone 2: **"The noble Joseph..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ*) until **"and laid It for burial"** (*κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*); **"Glory..."**: Tone 2: **"When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brilliance of Thy Divinity..."** (*Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*) in its entirety; **"Both now and ever..."**: Tone 2: **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women..."** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί*) until **"foreign to corruption"** (*ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*). Then the Small Litany, and the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 1 is chanted: **"In a clean shroud and with spices, the noble Joseph, taking down Thine all-pure Body from the Tree, wrapped It and laid It in a new tomb; and so early in the morning the myrrh-bearing women cried aloud: Show us, O Christ, Thy Resurrection!"** (*Σινδόνι καθαρᾷ*) once, slowly; **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: Tone 1: **"The angelic choirs were astounded at the sight of Him Who rests in the bosom of the Father being laid in a tomb as a mortal..."** (*Ἐξέστησαν χοροί*) likewise slowly.⁴⁸ Then Psalm 50 [LXX], and the Canon in Tone 6: **"Of old the surge of the sea covered the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves; but the children of those who were saved bury beneath the earth Him Who was hidden..."** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*) for six Troparia, the Heirmos being repeated slowly at the end of each Ode as Katavasia. After Ode 3, the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 1: **"Thy tomb, O Savior, the soldiers guarding became as dead men; and the angel sat upon the stone proclaiming the Resurrection unto the women..."** (*Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτήρ*) once, and this also slowly.⁴⁹ After Ode 6, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 2: **"He Who closed the abyss is beheld dead, and wrapped in fine linen and myrrh, the Immortal One is laid in a tomb as a mortal; and the women came to anoint Him with myrrh, weeping bitterly and crying aloud: This Sabbath is most blessed, in which Christ, having fallen asleep, shall rise again on the third day!"** (*Τὴν ἄβυσσον ὁ κλείσας*); the Ikos; the Menologion; and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the day from the Triodion; then follow Odes 7 and 8 of the Canon. The Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode of the Canon is chanted. At the conclusion of Ode 9, the Patriarch, fully vested in all his hierarchical vestments, exits from the Sanctuary preceded by the holy Hierarchs; chanting the opening verse of the Lamentations [Enkomia]: **"Life in the tomb art Thou laid, O Christ, and the angelic hosts were astounded, glorifying Thy condescension"** (*Ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τάφῳ κατετέθης Χριστέ*), he advances toward the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] and censes it cross-wise, and afterward censes all the people. The Hierarchs, standing in choir formation, chant the Lamentations of the First Stasis until the Patriarch returns to the throne; then the first Troparion is chanted again.

Both now and ever..."**: Tone 1: **"The angelic choirs were astounded at the sight of Him Who rests in the bosom of the Father being laid in a tomb as a mortal..."** (*Ἐξέστησαν χοροί*) likewise slowly.⁴⁸ Then Psalm 50 [LXX], and the Canon in Tone 6: **"Of old the surge of the sea covered the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves; but the children of those who were saved bury beneath the earth Him Who was hidden..."** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*) for six Troparia, the Heirmos being repeated slowly at the end of each Ode as Katavasia. After Ode 3, the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 1: **"Thy tomb, O Savior, the soldiers guarding became as dead men; and the angel sat upon the stone proclaiming the Resurrection unto the women..."** (*Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτήρ*) once, and this also slowly.⁴⁹ After Ode 6, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 2: **"He Who closed the abyss is beheld dead, and wrapped in fine linen and myrrh, the Immortal One is laid in a tomb as a mortal; and the women came to anoint Him with myrrh, weeping bitterly and crying aloud: This Sabbath is most blessed, in which Christ, having fallen asleep, shall rise again on the third day!"** (*Τὴν ἄβυσσον ὁ κλείσας*); the Ikos; the Menologion; and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the day from the Triodion; then follow Odes 7 and 8 of the Canon. The Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode of the Canon is chanted. At the conclusion of Ode 9, the Patriarch, fully vested in all his hierarchical vestments, exits from the Sanctuary preceded by the holy Hierarchs; chanting the opening verse of the Lamentations [Enkomia]: **"Life in the tomb art Thou laid, O Christ, and the angelic hosts were astounded, glorifying Thy condescension"** (*Ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τάφῳ κατετέθης Χριστέ*), he advances toward the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] and censes it cross-wise, and afterward censes all the people. The Hierarchs, standing in choir formation, chant the Lamentations of the First Stasis until the Patriarch returns to the throne; then the first Troparion is chanted again.

Πληρωθείσης δὲ καὶ τῆς γ΄ Στάσεως, αὖθις Συναπτὴ μικρά, ἡ ἐκφώνησις παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου Σὺ γὰρ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεύς, καὶ εὐθὺς ἄρχεται ψάλλων μετὰ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων τὰ Εὐλογητάρια· καὶ τούτων πληρωθέντων, ἡ Συναπτή, ἡ ἐκφώνησις παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου Ὅτι σὲ αἰνοῦσι, καὶ εὐθὺς ψάλλεται τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς 50. [Ὁ Βιολάκης ἐπαναλαμβάνει λανθασμένως τὸν ἀριθμὸν 49.] Εἰς τὸ Αἰνεῖτε ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται τοῦ Θρόνου προσκυνεῖ τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον, εὐλογεῖ τὸν λαὸν καὶ ἀνέρχεται αὖθις εἰς τὸν Θρόνον· ὡσαύτως καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς, ψαλλομένων τῶν Αἴνων, προσέρχονται ἀνὰ δύο, προσκυνοῦσι καὶ ἵστανται αὖθις εἰς τὰς θέσεις αὑτῶν.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: For holy are You, O our God, {Who sits upon the Throne of glory of the Cherubim and unto You we ascribe glory together with Your Father Who is without beginning and Your most holy, good and life-giving Spirit, now and ever and unto the ages of ages. Amen.} They then begin the Third Stasis “All generations {offer a hymn at Your burial, O my Christ}.” At the Verse “{“The myrrh-bearing women”} poured sweet ointment upon Your tomb {to which they came very early in the morning},” the Patriarch descends from the Throne, receives a sprinkler [Kanion] from the Ecclesiarch and, singing the same verse above (which is sung three times,) sprinkles the Epitaphios with rose water.
units.english_cohort_translation: They then begin the Third Stasis: **"All generations offer a hymn unto Thy burial, O my Christ"** (*Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι ὕμνον τῇ ταφῇ σου προσφέρουσι Χριστέ μου*). At the verse: **"The myrrh-bearing women came early in the morning and sprinkled myrrh upon Thy tomb"** (*Ἔρραναν τὸν τάφον αἱ Μυροφόροι μύρα, λίαν πρωῒ ἐλθοῦσαι*), the Patriarch descends from the throne, receives a sprinkler [*kanion*] from the Ecclesiarch, and singing this same verse (which is repeated three times), sprinkles the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] with rose-water. The Third Stasis having been completed, its first verse is repeated again. Then the Small Litany, with the exclamation by the Patriarch:

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ἡμῶν ἐκ γ΄ (τοῦτο καὶ μόνον), εἶτα τὸ Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ οἱ Αἶνοι⁵⁰ εἰς δ΄· Δόξα, Τὴν σήμερον μυστικῶς, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μ. εἰς τὸ τέλος ψάλλεται τὸ Ἀσματικὸν Ἅγιος ὁ Θεὸς ὑπὸ τῶν χορῶν προπορευομένων τοῦ Ἐπιταφίου κατὰ τὴν ἑξῆς τάξιν· πρῶτοι ἡγοῦνται οἱ ἱερεῖς, εἶτα ἕπονται οἱ ψάλται. μετ' αὐτοὺς ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς αἴροντες τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον· οὕτω γίνεται ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ ναοῦ ἔξοδος καὶ ἡ ἐπάνοδος ἐπίσης. Ἐπανελθὼν ἐν τῷ Ναῷ ὁ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῆς λοιπῆς παρατάξεως εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ Ἱερὸν καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκφωνεῖ Πρόσχωμεν, Εἰρήνη πᾶσι· Σοφία· ψάλλει τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον καὶ θυμιᾷ κύκλῳ τὴν Ἁγίαν Τράπεζαν προπορευόμενος ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἐπιταφίου, εἶτα⁵¹ τὸ Ταῖς Μυροφόροις γυναιξὶ μέχρι τοῦ ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος, ἑπομένως τὸ Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ μέχρι τοῦ κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο, καὶ τιθέασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον ἐπὶ τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης, ὁ δὲ Ἀναγνώστης ἔξωθεν ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Τροπάριον τῆς Προφητείας Ὁ συνέχων τὰ πέρατα, τὸ Προκείμενον, τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ ἀκολούθως τὸν Ἀπόστολον, καὶ ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, ἔμπροσθεν τῆς ὡραίας Πύλης. Μετὰ τὸ Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη ἐκδύεται τὴν Ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν,⁵² ἐνδύεται τὸν Μανδύαν καὶ κρατῶν τὴν ποιμαντορικὴν ῥάβδον ἐξέρχεται τοῦ Βήματος καὶ ἵσταται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον. Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ τούτῳ ὁ Ἀρχιδιάκονος λέγει τὴν Ἐκτενῆ Εἴπωμεν πάντες, Πληρώσωμεν τὴν Ἑωθινήν, ὁ Ἱερεὺς Σὸν γάρ ἐστι καὶ ἡ Ἀπόλυσις παρὰ τοῦ Ἱερέως (ἡ χθὲς σημειωθεῖσα ἤτοι Ὁ δι' ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν τὰ φρικτὰ Πάθη) καὶ ἄρχεται 51* Τὰ ἀρχαῖα Τυπικὰ σημειοῦσιν ὅτι λέγεται μόνον τὸ Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ μέχρι τοῦ ἀπέθετο, ὡς δὲ καὶ τὰ δύο ἄλλα τροπάρια, τὰ ὁποῖα ἡ συνήθεια παρεισήγαγε κατὰ τοὺς τελευταίους χρόνους ἵνα προτάττωνται τοῦ Ὁ εὐσχήμων.

Ἐπανελθὼν ἐν τῷ Ναῷ ὁ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῆς λοιπῆς παρατάξεως εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ Ἱερὸν καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκφωνεῖ *Πρόσχωμεν, Εἰρήνη πᾶσι· Σοφία*· ψάλλει τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια *Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον* καὶ θυμιᾷ κύκλῳ τὴν Ἁγίαν Τράπεζαν προπορευόμενος ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἐπιταφίου, εἶτα⁵¹ τὸ *Ταῖς Μυροφόροις γυναιξὶ* μέχρι τοῦ *ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*, ἑπομένως τὸ *Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ* μέχρι τοῦ *κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*, καὶ τιθέασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον ἐπὶ τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης, ὁ δὲ Ἀναγνώστης ἔξωθεν ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Τροπάριον τῆς Προφητείας *Ὁ συνέχων τὰ πέρατα*, τὸ Προκείμενον, τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ ἀκολούθως τὸν Ἀπόστολον, καὶ ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, ἔμπροσθεν τῆς ὡραίας Πύλης. Μετὰ τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη* ἐκδύεται τὴν Ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν,⁵² ἐνδύεται τὸν Μανδύαν καὶ κρατῶν τὴν ποιμαντορικὴν ῥά

units.slavonic_diplomatic: {“Today the tomb holds Him Who holds,” “What is this sight we behold? What is the present rest? “Come you and behold our Life lying in the tomb,” “Joseph asked for the Body of Christ and he laid it in a new tomb,”} Glory, “{Moses the Great} secretly forefigured this present day {saying}.” Now and ever, “Most blessed.” The Great Doxology and at the end the Melismatic [Asmatikon] “Holy God” is sung by the choirs which precede the Epitaphios in a procession, exiting from and returning to the church. The order of procession is as follows: first the Priests, then the chanters, and after them the Patriarch with the Hierarchs carrying the Epitaphios. Returning to the Church with the rest of the procession, the Patriarch enters the Holy Sanctuary [Vima] and immediately exclaims “Let us attend. Peace be with you. Wisdom.” Then he chants “When You had gone down to death,” while he proceeds to cense the Epitaphios which is being carried around the Holy Altar Table by the Hierarchs, then the hymn⁵¹* “The angel stood by the tomb” is chanted until “Christ has shown Himself foreign {to corruption}” and then the hymn “Noble Joseph taking down Your undefiled body” until “laid it in a tomb.” Then the Priests place the Epitaphios upon the Altar Table. Then the Reader reads the Troparion of the Prophecy “O Christ, Who holds fast the ends of the earth”; the Prophecy {Ezekiel 37:1-14}. The Apostolos {1 Corinthians 5:6-8 and Galatians 3:13-14}. The Gospel {Matthew 27:62-66} is read by the Patriarch in front of the Beautiful Gate. After “For many years, [Master],” he unvests from his Hierarchical vestments,⁵²* puts on the Mantle [Mandya], and holding the pastoral staff exits from the Sanctuary and stands at the Throne. In the meantime the Archdeacon says the Litany “Let us say with all our soul,” “Let us complete our morning supplication.” The Priest: “For to You belong {mercy and salvation}” and the Dismissal by the Priest (as yesterday): “May Christ, our True God, Who for us men and for our salvation voluntarily endured His terrible Passion, the Cross, and the entombment in the flesh, have mercy upon us.” And then begins:
units.english_cohort_translation: ... **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (*Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*) three times (this text only); then **"Let every breath"** and the Praises for four verses: 1. **"Today the tomb holds Him Who holds creation in the palm of His hand..."** (*Σήμερον συνέχει τάφος*); 2. **"What is this sight that we behold? What is this present rest?..."** (*Τί τὸ ὁρώμενον θέαμα;*); 3. **"Come, let us behold our Life lying in the tomb..."** (*Δεῦτε ἴδωμεν τὴν ζωὴν ἡμῶν*); 4. **"Joseph asked for the Body of Jesus, and laid It in his own new tomb..."** (*ᾐτήσατο Ἰωσὴφ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 2: **"This present day Moses mystically prefigured, saying: And God blessed the seventh day..."** (*Τὴν σήμερον μυστικῶς ὁ μέγας Μωϋσῆς προδιετυποῦτο λέγων*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 2: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις, Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*). The Great Doxology is chanted; at its conclusion, the Asmatikon: **"Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us"** (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός*) is chanted slowly by the choirs, who precede the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] in solemn procession, exiting from and circling back into the church. The order of the procession is as follows: first the priests lead the way, then follow the chanters, and after them the Patriarch with the Hierarchs bearing the Epitaphios upon their heads; thus is conducted the exit from the temple and likewise the return. Having returned into the church, the Patriarch with the rest of the procession enters the Sanctuary, and immediately exclaims: **"Let us attend! Peace be unto all! Wisdom!"** (*Πρόσχωμεν. Εἰρήνη πᾶσι. Σοφία*). Then he chants the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 2: **"When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal..."** (*Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*), and censes around the Holy Altar Table, processing in front of the Epitaphios; then the Troparion:⁵¹* **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women..."** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί*) until **"foreign to corruption"** (*ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*); next the Troparion: **"The noble Joseph..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ*) until **"and laid It for burial"** (*κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*); and the priests place the Epitaphios upon the Holy Altar Table. The Reader outside the iconostasis reads the Troparion of the Prophecy in Tone 2: **"O Christ, Who holdest fast the ends of the earth, Thou didst deign to be held fast in a narrow tomb..."** (*Ὁ συνέχων τὰ πέρατα*); the Prokimenon in Tone 4: **"Arise, O Lord, help us, and redeem us for Thy Name's sake!"** (*Ἀνάστα, Κύριε, βοήθησον ἡμῖν*, Ps. 43:26 [LXX]); the Prophecy: Ezekiel 37:1–14 [LXX] (The Vision of the Dry Bones in the Valley Brought to Life: "Behold, I Will Open Your Graves, and Cause You to Come Up out of Your Graves, O My People"); the Epistle: 1 Corinthians 5:6–8 and Galatians 3:13–14 (Christ Our Passover is Sacrificed for Us, and Has Redeemed Us from the Curse of the Law); and the Gospel: Matthew 27:62–66 (The Chief Priests and the Pharisees Seal the Tomb and Post the Roman Guard) read by the Patriarch before the Royal Doors [Beautiful Gate]. After **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), he unvests from his hierarchical vestments,⁵²* puts on his monastic mandya, and holding his pastoral staff exits from the Sanctuary and takes his place upon the throne. In the meantime, the Archdeacon recites the Augmented Litany: **"Let us all say with our whole soul..."** (*Εἴπωμεν πάντες*), and **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν*). The Priest gives the exclamation: **"For Thine it is to show mercy and to save us, O Christ our God..."** (*Σὸν γάρ ἐστι τὸ ἐλεεῖν καὶ σῴζειν ἡμᾶς*), and the Dismissal is given by the Priest (as noted yesterday): **"May Christ, our true God, Who for us men and for our salvation voluntarily endured His terrible Passions, the Cross, and voluntary entombment in the flesh, have mercy on us and save us..."**; and then begins...[^454]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 52.* If the Matins of the Epitaphios is sung at the First Hour of the night (7 p.m.), in which instance the Vesper and Liturgy do not follow Matins, then the Patriarch (or Hierarch) does not remove his vestments, but remains in the Altar until the end, and he himself does the Dismissal of Matins.
units.english_cohort_translation: 52.* If the Matins of the Epitaphios is chanted at the First Hour of the night (7:00 p.m.), in which case Vespers and the Divine Liturgy do not immediately follow Matins, the Patriarch [or presiding Hierarch] does not unvest from his hierarchical vestments, but remains in the Sanctuary until the end, where he himself pronounces the Dismissal of the section.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: *Δόξα, Τὴν σήμερον μυστικῶς, Καὶ νῦν, Τὴν παγκόσμιον δόξαν,* Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* καὶ εὐθὺς τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα α΄ *Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός*, β΄ *Ἐγένετο λόγος Κυρίου πρὸς Ἰωνᾶν* καὶ γ΄ *Ἔτους ὀκτωκαιδεκάτου* μέχρι τοῦ στίχου τῆς ζ΄ Ὠδῆς *Εὐλογημένος εἶ ὁ ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ Οὐρανοῦ, ὁ ὑπερύμνητος καὶ ὑπερυψούμενος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας.*

units.slavonic_incipit: Καὶ ἐνταῦθα ἀνιστάμενοι ψάλλομεν εἰς ἦχον
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Καὶ ἐνταῦθα ἀνιστάμενοι ψάλλομεν εἰς ἦχον α΄ *Τὸν Κύριον ὑμνεῖτε καὶ ὑπερυψοῦτε εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας*, ὅπερ ἐπαναλαμβάνεται ὑπὸ τῶν χορῶν ἕως οὗ ὁ Κανονάρχης πληρώσῃ πάντας τοὺς Στίχους τῆς η΄ Ὠδῆς, εἶτα Συναπτὴ μικρὰ καὶ ἀντὶ τοῦ Τρισαγίου ψάλλομεν τὸ *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*, ὁ Ἀπόστολος τῆς ἡμέρας, εἰς τὸ τέλος *Ἀλληλούϊα* οὐ λέγεται, ἀλλ’ εὐθὺς ὁ Ἱερεὺς ἔνδοθεν τοῦ Βήματος ψάλλει εἰς ἦχον βαρὺν τὸν Στίχον *Ἀνάστα ὁ Θεὸς κρῖνον τὴν γῆν, ὅτι σὺ κατακληρονομήσεις ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἔθνεσι*, διασκορπίζων δάφνας ἀπὸ τοῦ Βήματος καθ’ ἅπαντα τὸν ναόν· οἱ δὲ Χοροὶ

units.slavonic_incipit: ἐπαναλαμβάνουσι ψάλλοντες τὸν Στίχον, ἕως οὗ

units.slavonic_incipit: Ἀντὶ δὲ τοῦ Χερουβικοῦ ψάλλομεν τὸ
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Ἀντὶ δὲ τοῦ Χερουβικοῦ ψάλλομεν τὸ παρὸν Τροπάριον εἰς ἦχον πλ. α΄ *Σιγησάτω πᾶσα σὰρξ βροτεία, καὶ στήτω μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου, καὶ μηδὲν γήϊνον ἐν ἑαυτῇ λογιζέσθω· ὁ γὰρ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Βασιλευόντων, καὶ Κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων προσέρχεται σφαγιασθῆναι καὶ δοθῆναι εἰς βρῶσιν τοῖς πιστοῖς· προηγοῦνται δὲ τούτου οἱ Χοροὶ τῶν Ἀγγέλων μετὰ πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας*, [Μεγάλη Εἴσοδος] *τὰ πολυόμματα Χερουβὶμ καὶ τὰ ἑξαπτέρυγα Σεραφείμ, τὰς*

units.english_cohort_translation: The Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great continues. The Deacon: **"Let us pray to the Lord"**; the Priest: **"For Holy art Thou, our God, and unto Thee we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**

units.slavonic_incipit: Instead of the usual Cherubic Hymn
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Instead of the usual Cherubic Hymn the following [hymn] in Mode I Plagal is sung: "Let all mortal flesh be silent, and let it stand in fear and trembling. And let it take no thought for any earthly thing. For the King who reigns and the Lord who rules comes to the slaughter to give Himself as food to the faithful. Before Him go the choirs of angels with all the Principalities and Powers, [Great Entrance] the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim covering their faces and singing the hymn: Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia."
units.english_cohort_translation: **"Let all mortal flesh keep silence, and stand with fear and trembling, and ponder nothing earthly within itself; for the King of kings and Lord of lords comes forth to be slain, and to be given as food to the faithful. Before Him go the choirs of angels with every principality and power,"** [The Great Entrance is made] **"the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim, covering their faces and singing the hymn: Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!"** (*Σιγησάτω πᾶσα σὰρξ βροτεία...*)...[^456]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Τὸ Κοινωνικόν· *Ἐξηγέρθη ὡς ὁ ὑπνῶν Κύριος, καὶ ἀνέστη σῴζων ἡμᾶς, Ἀλληλούϊα*. Ἀντὶ τοῦ *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* ψάλλεται τὸ παρὸν εἰς ἦχον β΄ εἱρμολογικῶς· *Μνήσθητι εὔσπλαγχνε καὶ ἡμῶν, καθὼς ἐμνημόνευσας τοῦ Λῃστοῦ ἐν τῇ Βασιλείᾳ τῶν Οὐρανῶν*, τὸ *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, καὶ ἡ Ἀπόλυσις μετὰ τοῦ *Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*, διότι προηγήθη ὁ Ἑσπερινὸς τῆς Μ. Κυριακῆς. (῎Ιδε Προθεωρίας § 16 καὶ ἔκθεσιν τῆς ἐπιτροπῆς).

units.slavonic_incipit: ΤΥΠΙΚΗ ΔΙΑΤΑΞΙΣ ΤΩΝ ΑΚΟΛΟΥΘΙΩΝ ΤΟΥ ΠΕΝΤΗΚΟΣΤΑΡΙΟΥ
units.slavonic_diplomatic: ΤΥΠΙΚΗ ΔΙΑΤΑΞΙΣ ΤΩΝ ΑΚΟΛΟΥΘΙΩΝ ΤΟΥ ΠΕΝΤΗΚΟΣΤΑΡΙΟΥ ΤΗ ΚΥΡΙΑΚΗ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΣΧΑ Περὶ ὥραν ε΄ τῆς νυκτὸς (11 μ.μ.) εἰσερχόμεθα ἐν τῷ Ναῷ· ὁ Ἱερεὺς *Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός*, ὁ Πατριάρχης *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι, Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, *Κύριε ἐλέησον ιβ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν γ΄* καὶ ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, εἶτα ψάλλεται μετὰ Στίχου *Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι*, ὁ Κανὼν *Κύματι θαλάσσης* εἰς ϛ΄ καὶ μεθ’ ἑκάστην Ὠδὴν ὁ Εἱρμός, τὸ Κάθισμα οὐ ψάλλεται. Εἰς τὴν δ΄ Ὠδὴν ἐξέρχονται τοῦ Ἱεροῦ οἱ Διάκονοι ἐνδεδυμένοι, μετὰ δικηροτρικήρων, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης προσκυνήσας τὰς ἁγίας Εἰκόνας καὶ ἑτοιμασθείς, ὡς συνήθως, διὰ τὴν Λειτουργίαν, εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ Ἱερὸν Βῆμα καὶ ἐνδύεται ἅπασαν τὴν Ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν, ὡς καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς. Μετὰ τὴν θ΄ Ὠδὴν τοῦ Κανόνος, λέγεται ἔνδον τοῦ Βήματος τὸ *Τρισάγιον*, τὸ Τροπάριον *Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*, ἡ Ἐκτενὴς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις. Τότε ὁ Πατριάρχης,¹ προπορευομένων τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, ἐξέρχεται τοῦ Ἱεροῦ Βήματος, ψάλλων ἀργῶς μετ’ αὐτῶν τὸ *Τὴν Ἀνάστασίν σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*, ὅπερ ἐπαναλαμβάνεται καὶ ὑπὸ 1. Εἴθισται ἔν τισι μέρεσιν ἵνα κατὰ τὴν ὥραν ταύτην ὁ προεξάρχων Ἀρχιερεὺς ἱστάμενος πρὸ τῆς Ὡραίας Πύλης μετὰ δικηροτρικήρου ἀνημμένου ἐκ τῆς ἀκοιμήτου κανδήλας τῆς πρὸ τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης, προσκαλεῖ τὸν λαὸν ἵνα ἀνάψωσι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν, ψάλλων τὸ Δεῦτε λάβετε φῶς ἐκ τοῦ ἀνεσπέρου φωτός.

Εἰς τὴν δ΄ Ὠδὴν ἐξέρχονται τοῦ Ἱεροῦ οἱ Διάκονοι ἐνδεδυμένοι, μετὰ δικηροτρικήρων, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης προσκυνήσας τὰς ἁγίας Εἰκόνας καὶ ἑτοιμασθείς, ὡς συνήθως, διὰ τὴν Λειτουργίαν, εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ Ἱερὸν Βῆμα καὶ ἐνδύεται ἅπασαν τὴν Ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν, ὡς καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς. units.slavonic_diplomatic: RITUAL ORDER OF THE SERVICES OF THE PENTIKOSTARION THE SUNDAY OF PASCHA About the 5th hour of the night {11 PM} we enter the Church; the Priest: "Blessed is our God"; the Patriarch: "Glory to You our God, glory to You." "O heavenly King"; the Trisagion, "Lord, have mercy" (12 times), Glory, Now and ever, "O come let us worship" (3 times) and Psalm 50 is read. Then the Canon "With the wave of the sea" with the Verse "Glory to You our God, glory to You" in 6; and after each Ode, the Irmos; the Kathisma is not chanted. At the 4th Ode, the Deacons, vested, exit the Sanctuary with the Dikirotrikira. The Patriarch, having venerated the Holy Icons and having prepared as usual for the Liturgy, enters the Holy Sanctuary and vests with full Hierarchical Vesture, as do all the [participating] Hierarchs.
units.english_cohort_translation: Around the Fifth Hour of the night [11:00 p.m.], we enter into the church. The Priest: **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός*); the Patriarch: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers, **"Lord, have mercy"** [12 times], **"Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**, **"Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God"** [three times], and Psalm 50 [LXX: "Have mercy on me, O God..."] is read plainly. Then the Canon in Tone 6: **"Of old the surge of the sea covered the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves..."** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*) is chanted for six Troparia, with the refrain: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"**; and after each Ode, the Heirmos is chanted slowly as Katavasia; the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] is not chanted.

RITUAL ORDER
OF THE SERVICES
OF THE PENTIKOSTARION

THE SUNDAY OF PASCHA

About the 5th hour of the night {11 PM} we enter the Church; the Priest: "Blessed is our God"; the Patriarch: "Glory to You our God, glory to You." At the 4th Ode, the Deacons, vested, exit the Sanctuary with the Dikirotrikira. The Patriarch, having venerated the Holy Icons and having prepared as usual for the Liturgy, enters the Holy Sanctuary and vests with full Hierarchical Vesture, as do all the [participating] Hierarchs. After the 9th Ode of the Canon, the Trisagion is said from within the Sanctuary, then the Apolytikion "When You did descend unto death," the Ektenis and Dismissal. Then the Patriarch,¹ preceded by the Hierarchs, exits the Holy Sanctuary, chanting slowly with them "Your Resurrection, Christ Savior," which is repeated also by the Choirs until they [the procession of the clergy] reach the place

units.slavonic_incipit: τῶν Χορῶν ἕως οὗ φθάσωσιν εἰς
units.slavonic_diplomatic: τῶν Χορῶν ἕως οὗ φθάσωσιν εἰς προσδιωρισμένην ἐξέδραν· ὁ Ἀρχιδιάκονος τότε ἐκφωνεῖ *Καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ καταξιωθῆναι ἡμᾶς*, καὶ ὁ Πατριάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον *Ὀψὲ σαββάτων τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ*¹ (Αὐτὸ εἶναι τὸ ἴδιο Εὐαγγέλιον ὅπερ ἀναγινώσκεται εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν τῆς πρωΐας· ὅρα κάτωθεν σημ. 2.) καὶ οἱ Χοροὶ τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη [Δέσποτα]*, εἶτα λαβὼν τὸ θυμιατόν, θυμιᾷ τρὶς τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον καὶ ἐκφωνήσας *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ καὶ ἀδιαιρέτῳ Τριάδι*, ψάλλει τὸ Τροπάριον *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ νεκρῶν* τρίς, καὶ οἱ Χοροὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἑξάκις, τοῦ Πατριάρχου θυμιῶντος καὶ λέγοντος τοὺς τέσσαρας Στίχους *Ἀναστήτω ὁ Θεός*, καὶ μετ’ αὐτοὺς τὸ *Δόξα*, καὶ τὸ *Καὶ νῦν*· ἐπὶ τέλους ὁ Πατριάρχης ψάλλει τὸ αὐτὸ θυμιῶν τοὺς Ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ λαπούς, ὁ δὲ Ἀρχιδιάκονος λέγει τὴν Μ. Συναπτὴν *Ἐν εἰρήνῃ τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*, ὁ Πατριάρχης τὴν Ἐκφώνησιν *Ὅτι πρέπει σοι πᾶσα δόξα*, καὶ οὕτως εἰσερχόμεθα ἐν τῷ Ναῷ μετὰ τῆς αὐτῆς παρατάξεως, τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἀρχομένου ψάλλειν τὸν Κανόνα *Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα λαμπρυνθῶμεν λαοί*, μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων Ἀρχιερέων, ἀνὰ ϛ΄ Τροπάρια ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ μετὰ Στίχου *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου Κύριε*· εἰς τὰ δύο δὲ τελευταῖα *Δόξα* καὶ τὸ *Καὶ νῦν*· μεθ’ ἑκάστην Ὠδὴν ἡ Καταβασία, ἡ Αἴτησις καὶ ἡ Ἐκφώνησις· εἰς μὲν τὴν α΄ Ὠδήν, *Ὅτι σὸν τὸ κράτος*, εἰς δὲ τὴν γ΄ *Ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*, εἰς τὴν δ΄ *Ὅτι ἀγαθὸς καὶ φιλάνθρωπος*, εἰς τὴν ε΄ *Ὅτι ἡγίασται καὶ δεδόξασται*, εἰς τὴν ϛ΄ *Σὺ γὰρ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεύς*, εἰς τὴν ζ΄ *Εἴη τὸ κράτος*, εἰς τὴν η΄ *Ὅτι ηὐλόγηται [Σου τὸ Ὄνομα] καὶ δεδόξασται*, εἰς τὴν θ΄ *Ὅτι σὲ αἰνοῦσι πᾶσαι αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν*· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ *Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον* χῦμα· ἀφ’ ϛ΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἡμέρας μετὰ τῶν Στίχων, εἶτα τὸ *Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ* τρίς, ἅπαξ ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατριάρχου καὶ δὶς ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, μετὰ δὲ τὸ *Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς*, ψάλλεται ἡ ζ΄ καὶ ἡ η΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ μετ’ αὐτὴν ὁ Μ. Ἀρχιδιάκονος ἐκφωνεῖ *Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*, καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν ἑξῆς Μεγαλυναρίων·

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 1. [2.] Εἴθισται ἵνα τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἀναγινώσκηται ὑπὸ πλειόνων Ἀρχιερέων καὶ Ἱερέων, περικοπτομένου τοῦ εὐαγγελικοῦ κειμένου μετὰ τὸν 10ον στίχον, ὅπερ συνάπτεται εἰς τὸν 16ον, κἀκεῖθεν μέχρι τέλους (μεταβαίνουσι δηλονότι ἀπὸ τοῦ «ἐκεῖ με ὄψονται» εἰς τὸ «οἱ δὲ ἕνδεκα μαθηταὶ») μέχρι τέλους. units.english_cohort_translation: ... which the Holy Gospel is to be read; the Archdeacon then exclaims: **"And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel, let us pray unto the Lord God"** (*Καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ καταξιωθῆναι ἡμᾶς*). The Patriarch reads the Holy Gospel: **"In the end of the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week..."** (*Ὀψὲ σαββάτων τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ*)² [Matthew 28:1–20. This is the same Gospel read at the morning Liturgy; see footnote 2 below], and the choirs sing: **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, Δέσποτα*).

units.english_cohort_translation: After the 3rd Ode, we read the Ypakoe plainly: **"Anticipating the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..."** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον*); after the 6th Ode, we recite the Kontakion, the Ikos, and the Memorial [*Hypomnema* / Synaxarion] of the day with its verses. Then is recited: **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the Holy Lord Jesus, the only sinless One..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) [three times] — once by the Patriarch and twice by the concelebrating Hierarchs. After **"Jesus having risen from the tomb, as He foretold, hath given us eternal life and great mercy"** (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ τάφου*), the 7th and 8th Odes are sung, after which the Great Archdeacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the 9th Ode is sung with the appointed Megalynaria...[^459]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: "Magnify, O my soul, Him Who suffered willingly, and was buried, and arose from the grave on the third day.
units.english_cohort_translation:
**"Magnify, O my soul, Him Who suffered willingly, and was buried, and arose from the grave on the third day!"** (*Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου τὸν ἐθελουσίως παθόντα*)
Heirmos: **"Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and do thou, O pure Theotokos, rejoice in the Resurrection of Him Whom thou didst bear!"** (*Φωτίζου, φωτίζου ἡ νέα Ἱερουσαλήμ*)...

units.slavonic_incipit: Today the whole creation is glad
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Today the whole creation is glad and does rejoice, for Christ has risen, and Hades has been despoiled.
units.english_cohort_translation:
**"Christ is the new Pascha, the living sacrificial Victim, the Lamb of God Who takes away the sin of the world!"** (*Χριστὸς τὸ καινὸν Πάσχα*)
Troparion: **"O Thy divine, O Thy beloved, O Thy sweetest voice! For Thou hast truly promised to be with us unto the end of the age, O Christ; and holding this as an anchor of hope, we the faithful rejoice!"** (*Ὢ θείας, ὢ φίλης*)...

units.slavonic_incipit: Jerusalem." The Petition, and the Exapostilarion
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Jerusalem." The Petition, and the Exapostilarion "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal" (3 times). At the Praises: the 4 Resurrection Stichira "We praise, O Christ" and the Stichira "A sacred Pascha" with their verses.
units.english_cohort_translation: At the Praises, we set eight stichoi and chant the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1: **"We hymn Thy saving Passion, O Christ, and glorify Thy Resurrection!"** (*Ὑμνοῦμέν σου Χριστὲ τὸ σωτήριον Πάθος*)... and the four Stichera of Pascha in Tone 5 with their verses of Psalm 67 LXX: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*). Then we chant "Glory... Both now and ever...": Paschal Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another. Let us say, Brethren, even to those who hate us; let us forgive all things at the Resurrection, and thus let us cry:"** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*) ³ until the words **"and thus let us cry"**, at which point the Second Choir sings the customary melody of **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*); then the First Choir chants the same, and again the Second Choir repeats it, and the Divine Liturgy begins.[^460]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: THE LITURGY 2.    The Archdeacon exclaims "Bless, Master," the Priest intones "Blessed is the Kingdom," and the Choirs sing "Amen," and immediately from the Sanctuary is sung "Christ is risen" (3 times).
units.english_cohort_translation: 2.    The Archdeacon exclaims: **"Bless, Master!"** (*Εὐλόγησον Δέσποτα*). The Priest intones: **"Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία*), and the choirs sing: **"Amen."** Directly from within the Sanctuary, the celebrant sings: **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) [three times]; then the choirs chant it six times with the Paschal Verses of Psalm 67 LXX, and the last repetition is intoned again from within the Sanctuary.

units.slavonic_incipit: Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν Σῶμα Χριστοῦ μεταλάβετε
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν Σῶμα Χριστοῦ μεταλάβετε Μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχὴν τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη τρὶς χῦμα ⁶, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ὁ Κατηχητικὸς λόγος τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου Εἴ τις εὐσεβὴς καὶ φιλόθεος ⁷, εἰς τὸ τέλος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου Ἡ τοῦ στόματός σου καθάπερ, εἶτα Εὐλογία Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἐκφωνοῦντος εἰς τὸ τέλος Χριστὸς ἀνέστη τρίς, καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀποκρινομένου ὡσαύτως τρὶς Ἀληθῶς ἀνέστη, ὁ Πατριάρχης Δόξα τῇ αὐτοῦ τριημέρῳ ἐγέρσει, ὁ λαὸς Προσκυνοῦμεν αὐτοῦ τὴν τριήμερον ἔγερσιν· καὶ ἐπὶ τέλους ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ὁλόκληρον. Μετὰ τὴν Ἀπόλυσιν, ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς οὕτως ἐνδεδυμένοι, προπορευομένων λαμπάδων καὶ Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ τῆς λοιπῆς παρατάξεως, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ἀνέρχονται εἰς τὸ Μέγα Συνοδικόν, ἔνθα ψάλλεται ὁ Πολυχρονισμὸς τοῦ Πατριάρχου κατὰ τὸ ἔθος ⁸.

Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως *Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*, Κοινωνικὸν *Σῶμα Χριστοῦ μεταλάβετε* Μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχὴν τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* τρὶς χῦμα ⁶, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ὁ Κατηχητικὸς λόγος τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου *Εἴ τις εὐσεβὴς καὶ φιλόθεος* ⁷, εἰς τὸ τέλος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου *Ἡ τοῦ στόματός σου καθάπερ*, εἶτα Εὐλογία Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἐκφωνοῦντος εἰς τὸ τέλος *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* τρίς, καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀποκρινομένου ὡσαύτως τρὶς *Ἀληθῶς ἀνέστη*, ὁ Πατριάρχης *Δόξα τῇ αὐτοῦ τριημέρῳ ἐγέρσει*, ὁ λαὸς *Προσκυνοῦμεν αὐτοῦ τὴν τριήμερον ἔγερσιν*· καὶ ἐπὶ τέλους ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* ὁλόκληρον. Μετὰ τὴν Ἀπόλυσιν, ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς οὕτως ἐνδεδυμένοι, προπορευομένων λαμπάδων καὶ Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ τῆς λοιπῆς παρατάξεως, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*, ἀνέρχονται εἰς τὸ Μέγα Συνοδικόν, ἔνθα ψάλλεται ὁ Πολυχρονισμὸς τοῦ Πατριάρχου κατὰ τὸ ἔθος ⁸.

units.english_cohort_translation: ...is of Israel's fountain." ⁴ **"Save us, O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead, who sing to Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Σῶσον ἡμᾶς, Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). units.english_cohort_translation: At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and do thou, O pure Theotokos, rejoice in the Resurrection of Him Whom thou didst bear!"** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ μεταλάβετε*).

units.english_cohort_translation: At the end is chanted the Dismissal Troparion of Saint John Chrysostom in Tone 8: **"Grace shining forth from thy mouth like a radiant torch has enlightened the universe; it has disclosed to the world the treasures of poverty, and demonstrated to us the height of humility; but as thou dost instruct us by thy words, Father John Chrysostom, intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved!"** (*Ἡ τοῦ στόματός σου καθάπερ*); then the blessing of the Lord, and the solemn Dismissal by the Patriarch, who exclaims at the end: **"Christ is risen!"** (three times), the people responding thrice: **"Truly He is risen!"** The Patriarch exclaims: **"Glory to His holy third-day Resurrection!"**, the people responding: **"We worship His third-day Resurrection!"**; at the end the Patriarch sings the entire Troparion: **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**.

units.english_cohort_translation: 8. From this day until Saturday of Bright Week, as well as on the day of the Apodosis, instead of the Hours, Compline, and Midnight Office, the following Service is performed: After "Blessed is our God," we chant "Christ is risen" (three times), then "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" (three times), and the following hymns once each: "Anticipating the dawn," "Though Thou didst descend into the grave," "In the tomb bodily," Glory, "As life-bearing," Now and ever, "That which is sanctified by the Most High"; then "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), Glory, Now and ever, "More honorable than the Cherubim," and "Through the prayers of our holy fathers," and once again "Christ is risen" (three times) etc. This service is performed three times in place of the Hours, Compline, and Midnight Service, as we have said before.

units.slavonic_incipit: Διακόνων προενδεδυμένων τὰς οἰκείας στολάς· ἄρχονται
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Διακόνων προενδεδυμένων τὰς οἰκείας στολάς· ἄρχονται δὲ οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλειν καθ' ὃν καιρὸν ἐνδύεται ὁ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων τὸ Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα ἀργόν, ἀκολούθως, προπορευομένων τῶν Λαμπαδούχων, τῶν Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ τοῦ Πριμικηρίου, καὶ τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ἕπονται οἱ Ἱερεῖς, οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς, οἱ Διάκονοι μετὰ Δικηροτρικήρων καὶ μετ' αὐτοὺς ὁ Πατριάρχης φέρων τὴν ῥάβδον καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον (καὶ περιστοιχίζομενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Μ. Λογοθέτου, τῶν Πρέσβεων τῶν Ὀρθοδόξων Κρατῶν καὶ τῶν Λογάδων τοῦ Γένους).*
units.english_cohort_translation: Διακόνων προενδεδυμένων τὰς οἰκείας στολάς· ἄρχονται δὲ οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλειν καθ' ὃν καιρὸν ἐνδύεται ὁ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων τὸ *Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα* ἀργόν, ἀκολούθως, προπορευομένων τῶν Λαμπαδούχων, τῶν Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ τοῦ Πριμικηρίου, καὶ τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*, ἕπονται οἱ Ἱερεῖς, οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς, οἱ Διάκονοι μετὰ Δικηροτρικήρων καὶ μετ' αὐτοὺς ὁ Πατριάρχης φέρων τὴν ῥάβδον καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον (καὶ περιστοιχίζομενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Μ. Λογοθέτου, τῶν Πρέσβεων τῶν Ὀρθοδόξων Κρατῶν καὶ τῶν Λογάδων τοῦ Γένους).* Ἐν τοιαύτῃ παρατάξει κατέρχονται εἰς τὸν Ναόν, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, τῶν Ἱερέων καὶ Διακόνων εἰσέρχεται κατ' εὐθεῖαν εἰς τὸ Ἱερόν, καὶ λαβὼν θυμιατὸν θυμιᾷ πρὸ τῆς ἁγίας Τραπέζης, εἶτα ἐκφωνεῖ *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ Ὁμοουσίῳ*, καὶ ψάλλει τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*, κατὰ τὴν ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ ἐν § 1 διάταξιν· ἀκολούθως ὁ Ἀρχιδιάκονος λέγει τὴν Μ. Συναπτήν, ὁ Πατριάρχης τὴν Ἐκφώνησιν *Ὅτι πρέπει σοι*. Εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ *Τὸν πρὸ αἰώνων ἐκ Πατρὸς* κατὰ σειρὰν ϛ΄· τούτων ψαλλομένων, ὁ Πατριάρχης προπορευομένου τοῦ Πριμικηρίου μετὰ τοῦ Διβαμβούλου, θυμιᾷ τὰς εἰκόνας καὶ ἅπαντα τὸν λαὸν καὶ ἐπανερχόμενος ἵσταται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον· ὁ α΄ Χορὸς *Δόξα, Τὸν σωτήριον ὕμνον, Καὶ νῦν*, ὁ β΄ τὸ *Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιὰ τοῦ νόμου*. Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, τὸ *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* ἀργῶς ὁλόκληρον ἔξω, εἶτα εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ψάλλων τὸ Μ. Προκείμενον *Τίς Θεὸς Μέγας*, ὅπερ οἱ Χοροὶ ἐπαναλαμβάνουσι μετὰ τῶν Στίχων καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Πατριάρχης *Καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ καταξιωθῆναι ἡμᾶς*, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον *Οὔσης ὀψίας* μέχρι τοῦ *Οὐ μὴ πιστεύσω*, κατὰ περιόδους ἐπαναλαμβανομένας καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, τῶν Ἱερέων καὶ τῶν Διακόνων. Μετὰ τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*, ἡ Ἐκτενής, τὸ *Καταξίωσον Κύριε*, *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν*, ἡ ἐκφώνησις *Εἴη τὸ κράτος*, καὶ ψάλλεται ὑπὸ τοῦ α΄ Χοροῦ τὸ Ἀπόστιχον Στιχηρὸν *Ἡ Ἀνάστασίς σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*, καὶ ἀκολούθως τὰ Στιχηρὰ *Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*, καὶ τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* γ΄· τούτου ψαλλομένου, ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς ἐξέρχονται τοῦ Ἱεροῦ καὶ ἀνέρχονται αὖθις εἰς τὸ Μ. Συνοδικὸν μετὰ τῆς αὐτῆς παρατάξεως καὶ ἐκεῖ ποιεῖ τὴν Ἀπόλυσιν, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸν Πολυχρονισμὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὕτω λαμβάνει πέρας ὁ Ἑσπερινός.

units.english_cohort_translation: At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), the six Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2 are chanted in sequence, beginning with: **"Before the ages, begotten of the Father, God the Word incarnate of the Virgin Mary, come, let us worship; for having endured the Cross, He was delivered over to burial, as He Himself willed, and having risen from the dead, He saved me, the wandering man!"** (*Τὸν πρὸ αἰώνων ἐκ Πατρὸς*). While these are being chanted, the Patriarch, preceded by the Primikirios with the *divamvoulon* [two-branched candlestick], censes the icons and all the people, and returning stands upon the Throne.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Gospel "When it was evening" up to "I will not believe," is read in segments and in sequence by the Hierarchs, Priests and Deacons. After "Many years," the Ektenis, the "Vouchsafe, O Lord," then "Let us complete our evening prayer." After the Exclamation "May the might," the First Choir chants the Resurrection Apostichon "Your Resurrection, Christ Savior,"
units.english_cohort_translation: After **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), the Augmented Litany, **"Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin"** (*Καταξίωσον Κύριε*), and **"Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν*) are recited. After the Exclamation: **"Blessed and glorified be the might of Thy kingdom..."** (*Εἴη τὸ κράτος*), the First Choir chants the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 2: **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, hath enlightened the whole universe and recalled Thine own creation: O almighty Lord, glory to Thee!"** (*Ἡ Ἀνάστασίς σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*); then follow the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*), "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"It is the day of Resurrection..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), and **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ΤΗ ΔΕΥΤΕΡΑ ΤΗΣ ΔΙΑΚΑΙΝΗΣΙΜΟΥ 4.    Εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὴν ἀντὶ Μεσονυκτικοῦ ὡρισμένην Ἀκολουθίαν (βλ. § 2, σημ. 8), ὁ Ἱερεὺς ἐνδυθεὶς πᾶσαν τὴν ἱερατικὴν στολὴν ἵσταται μετὰ θυμιατοῦ ἐνώπιον τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης καὶ θυμιῶν ἐκφωνεῖ Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ· ἀκολούθως ψάλλει τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄ ὡς διετυπώθη χθὲς ἐν § 1, εἶτα Συναπτή, ἡ Ἐκφώνησις Ὅτι πρέπει σοι πᾶσα δόξα καὶ ψάλλεται ὁ τῆς Ἀναστάσεως Κανὼν ὡς χθὲς ἀπαραλλάκτως· ἀλλ' ἀφ' ϛ΄ μόνον τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ· μετὰ τὴν η΄ Ὠ- δήν, ὁ Διάκονος λέγει Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας (δὶς, κατὰ τὸ ἀρχαῖον Τυπικόν). Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ δ΄ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ πᾶσα κτίσις, καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερὸν μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτῶν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄ καὶ ἄρχεται ἡ Λειτουργία.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 5.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα κτλ. ὡς χθές· μετὰ τὸ Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε [ἀντὶ τοῦ Τρισαγίου Ὕμνου], ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν Σῶμα Χριστοῦ, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη· μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχήν, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄ χῦμα, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_incipit: ΤΗ ΠΑΡΑΣΚΕΥΗ ΤΗΣ ΔΙΑΚΑΙΝΗΣΙΜΟΥ Ψάλλεται ἡ
units.slavonic_diplomatic: ΤΗ ΠΑΡΑΣΚΕΥΗ ΤΗΣ ΔΙΑΚΑΙΝΗΣΙΜΟΥ Ψάλλεται ἡ Ἀκολουθία τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου τῆς Ζωοδόχου Πηγῆς 6.    Τῇ Πέμπτῃ ἑσπέρας, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ϛ΄ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ Νίκην ἔχων Χριστέ, καὶ δ΄ τῆς Ζωοδόχου Πηγῆς, δευτεροῦντες τὸ α΄, Δόξα, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Πηγή, Καὶ νῦν, Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον Ἀγαπήσω σε, Κύριε, ἡ ἰσχύς μου μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, ὧν ἄρχεται ὁ β΄ Χορός, Τὴν Ἀνάστασίν

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Midnight Service (see Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest vested with all his priestly vestments stands with the censer before the Holy Altar Table and censing exclaims "Glory to the holy and consubstantial"; then he sings "Christ is risen" (three times) as prescribed yesterday in Paragraph 1. Then follow the Litany and the Exclamation "For to You belong all glory." Then the Resurrection Canon is chanted exactly as yesterday; except that, after the 6th Ode, only the Kontakion is said, and immediately after we recite "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; after the 8th Ode, the Deacon chants "The Theotokos," and the 9th Ode is sung with the Megalynaria.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4.    At Matins, following the prescribed service which replaces the Midnight Office (see Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest, vested in all his priestly vestments, stands with the censer before the Holy Table and censing exclaims: **"Glory to the holy, and consubstantial, and life-creating, and undivided Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ*); then he sings **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times) as prescribed yesterday in Paragraph 1. Then follow the Litany and the Exclamation: **"For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship..."** (*Ὅτι πρέπει σοι πᾶσα δόξα*). Then the Paschal Canon of the Resurrection is chanted exactly as yesterday; except that, after the 6th Ode, only the Kontakion is said, and immediately after we recite **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) [once]; after the 8th Ode, the Deacon chants **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον*), and the 9th Ode is sung with the Megalynaria. The Exaposteilarion: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητὸς*) is chanted twice, according to the ancient Typikon. At the Praises: the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2: **"Let every breath and all creation glorify Thee, O Lord..."** (*Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ πᾶσα κτίσις*) and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"It is the day of Resurrection..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), and the Divine Liturgy begins.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 5.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons etc. as yesterday. After "As many as have been baptized" [chanted instead of the Trisagios Hymn], the Apostolos and Gospel of the day. At "Especially," "The Angel cried out . . . Shine, shine," Communion Hymn "[Receive] the body of Christ." then "Christ is risen." After the Prayer behind the Amvon, we intone "Christ is risen"
units.english_cohort_translation: 5.    At the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons etc. are celebrated as yesterday. After **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*) [chanted in place of the Trisagion Hymn], the Epistle and Gospel of the day are proclaimed. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace... Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**. After the Prayer behind the Ambo, we intone **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** three times plainly, and the Dismissal is pronounced.

units.english_cohort_translation:
FRIDAY OF BRIGHT WEEK
The Service of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos
of the
Life-Giving Fountain is Chanted 6.    On Thursday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant six Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3: **"Holding the victory over Hades, O Christ, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross..."** (*Νίκην ἔχων Χριστέ*) and four of the Life-Giving Fountain, repeating the first: **"Who can declare thy mighty wonders, O Fountain?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Πηγή*). "Glory...": **"Who can tell of thy mighty acts, O undefiled Fountain?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Πηγή*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 3: **"Who would not admire, who would not praise thy childbirth without seed, O all-pure Virgin?..."** (*Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε*). The Entrance is made with the censer; **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*) and the Prokimenon: **"I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my foundation, my refuge, and my deliverer!"** (*Ἀγαπήσω σε, Κύριε, ἡ ἰσχύς μου*, Ps. 17:2–3 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha, which are begun by the Second Choir: **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior..."** (*Τὴν Ἀνάστασίν σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*)...[^464]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 7.    Τῇ Παρασκευῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, ψάλλεται ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ ὁ τῆς Θεοτόκου ἀνὰ δ΄ Τροπάρια, εἰς τὸν τῆς Θεοτόκου λέγομεν Στίχον Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε, εἰς τὸ τέλος ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς ἡ Καταβασία, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄ κτλ. ὡς ἐν § 4. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠ- δῆς τὸ Κοντάκιον τοῦ Πάσχα χῦμα, καὶ ψάλλεται τὸ Κάθισμα Τὴν ἀέναον κρήνην καὶ ζωηρὰν ἅπαξ· ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος τῆς Θεοτόκου, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας, οἱ Στίχοι καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Ζωοδόχου Πηγῆς, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ γ΄ κτλ. καὶ ἀκολούθως ἡ ζ΄ καὶ η΄ Ὠδὴ τῶν Κανόνων· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων, εἰς τὸν τῆς Θεοτόκου Κανόνα Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τὸ τῆς Θεοτόκου. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄, τῆς Θεοτόκου γ΄ καὶ τὸ Πάσχα ἱερόν, ** ** (Σημ. Μεταφραστοῦ· Ἐνῷ τὸ παρὸν Τυπικὸν ὑποδεικνύει τὸ σύνολον 8 Στιχηρῶν [4 Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, 3 Στιχηρὰ τῆς Θεοτόκου, καὶ τὸ πρῶτον Στιχηρὸν τοῦ Πάσχα Πάσχα Ἱερόν], εἷς μεταγενέστερος τρόπος ἀκολουθεῖ τὴν σειρὰν τοῦ Πεντηκοσταρίου, ἐν ᾗ ψάλλομεν 4 Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, 4 Στιχηρὰ τῆς Θεοτόκου, καὶ 4 Στιχηρὰ τοῦ Πάσχα, δηλ. 12 Στιχηρὰ ἐν συνόλῳ. Ὅρα Ἡμερολόγια [HABNA] 1985, σελ. 85· 1990, σελ. 106· 1992, σελ. 108, ὡς καὶ τὰ Ἡμερολόγια 1996, σελ. 197 καὶ 1999, σελ. 300).

units.english_cohort_translation: ...Choir: **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, the angels hymn in heaven: and make us worthy here on earth to glorify Thee with a pure heart!"** (*Τὴν Ἀνάστασίν σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*), and the three Prosomia of the Theotokos; "Glory...": **"Let us sound the trumpet of hymns, O ye lovers of the feast, let us leap for joy in songs, and let us dance exultantly in the ever-flowing Fountain of the Queen of all!..."** (*Σαλπίσωμεν φιλέορτοι ἐν ὕμνοις*); "Both now and ever...": **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) (three times), and Dismissal.*

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Theotokos (4 hymns); the verse for the Canon of the Theotokos is "All-holy
units.english_cohort_translation: 7.    On Friday at Matins, we chant the Canon of Pascha and the Canon of the Theotokos, with four Troparia for each ode; the verse for the Canon of the Theotokos is **"Most Holy Theotokos, save us!"** (*Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε, σῶσον ἡμᾶς*); at the conclusion of each Ode, the Katavasia, and **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times) etc. as in Paragraph 4. After the 3rd Ode, we recite the Kontakion of Pascha plainly, and we chant the Kathisma: **"The ever-flowing and living fountain..."** (*Τὴν ἀέναον κρήνην καὶ ζωηρὰν*) (once); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Theotokos, the Synaxarion of the Menaion, and the Hypomnema of the Life-Giving Fountain with its verses. Then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) (three times) etc., and then follow the 7th and 8th Odes of the Canons; then the 9th Ode with the Megalynaria; at the Canon of the Theotokos the verse: **"Most Holy Theotokos, save us!"**. The Exaposteilarion of Pascha and that of the Theotokos. At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera, three Stichera of the Theotokos, and the first Paschal Sticheron: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*).**

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 9.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, λέγεται ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα (ὡς προεσημειώθη ἐν § 2, σημ. 8). Μετὰ δὲ τὸ Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός, ψάλλεται τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἅπαξ ἐκ τοῦ Βήματος καὶ ἐκ τῶν Χορῶν ἀνὰ μίαν φορὰν καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Προοιμιακὸς καὶ τὸ α΄ Κάθισμα τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ ς΄ Ἰδιόμελα κατὰ σειράν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, τὸ Προκείμενον Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 10.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ψάλλεται ὁ Τριαδικὸς Κανὼν τοῦ α΄ ἤχου, εἶτα ἡ Λιτὴ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, τὰ γ΄ Καθίσματα ἐκ β΄ (Εὐλογητάρια οὐ λέγονται σήμερον χάριν τῆς Δεσποτικῆς ἑορτῆς, ὡς σημειοῦσι καὶ τὰ ἀρχαῖα Τυπικὰ) καὶ εὐθὺς οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ δ΄ ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον⁹ καὶ ὁ Κανὼν εἰς ς΄ ἄνευ Στίχων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Ὡς ἐν μέσῳ τῶν Μαθητῶν σου, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἑορτῆς, αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ τοῦ Κανόνος, ἡ Καταβασία Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . .

Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, τὸ Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν δίς, καὶ ὁ Στίχος Ὑψοῦτε Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν¹⁰ καὶ τὰ Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ α΄ δὶς καὶ τὸ ἕτερον ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ γ΄ Προσόμοια εἰς δ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον.

Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, τὸ Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν δίς, καὶ ὁ Στίχος Ὑψοῦτε Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν¹⁰ καὶ τὰ Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ α΄ δὶς καὶ τὸ ἕτερον ἅπαξ. The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 7: **"While the tomb was sealed, Thou, O Life, didst shine forth from the grave, O Christ God..."** (*Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος*) three times, and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Apolytikion three times; then the Psalter and the Polyeleos. The three
units.english_cohort_translation: 10.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, we chant the Triadic Canon in Tone 1, then the Liti of the Feast, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right to glorify Thee, God the Word..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion three times; then the Psalter and the Polyeleos (Pss. 134–135 LXX). The three Kathismata twice each (Resurrectional Evlogitaria are not chanted today since it is a Master Feast of the Lord, as the ancient Typika note) and immediately the Anavathmoi of Tone 4 (First Antiphon: **"From my youth..."**) and the Prokimenon in Tone 4: **"Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem"** (*Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 147:1 LXX) [Note 9] and the Canon of the Feast with six Troparia without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoe in Tone 6: **"As Thou didst stand in the midst of Thy disciples, O Savior, giving them peace: come also unto us and save us!"** (*Ὡς ἐν μέσῳ τῶν Μαθητῶν σου*); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"With his inquisitive right hand, Thomas explored Thy life-giving side, O Christ God..."** (*Τῇ φιλοπράγμονι δεξιᾷ*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Feast. The Katavasias of Pascha (**"It is the day of Resurrection..."**) and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (First Eothinon: Matthew 28:16–20); then the 9th Ode of the Canon is sung, the Katavasia: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace... Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Then **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (twice), and the Verse: **"Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy!"** (*Ὑψοῦτε Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν*, Ps. 98:5 LXX) [Note 10] and the Exaposteilaria: **"With my hand have I explored Thy side, O Compassionate One..."** (*Ἐμῇ χειρὶ ἠρεύνησα*) — the first one twice and the second one once. At the Praises: the three Prosomia to 4, "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"Eight days after Thy Resurrection, O Jesus our King..."** (*Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ*). Great Doxology and the Dismissal Troparion.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 12.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ ἑσπέρας, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα τὰ γ΄ τῶν Αἴνων Στιχηρὰ Μετὰ τὴν ἐκ τάφου σου, καὶ τὰ γ΄ τοῦ Ἁγίου τῆς ἡμέρας, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν εἰς ἦχον α΄ Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον Τίς Θεὸς Μέγας μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτοῦ.
units.english_cohort_translation: 12.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ ἑσπέρας, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα τὰ γ΄ τῶν Αἴνων Στιχηρὰ Μετὰ τὴν ἐκ τάφου σου, καὶ τὰ γ΄ τοῦ Ἁγίου τῆς ἡμέρας, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν εἰς ἦχον α΄ Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον Τίς Θεὸς Μέγας μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Στιχηρὸν Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχάς, καὶ τὰ β΄ Κατανυκτικὰ Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ, τὸ εἰς τὸν α΄ ἦχον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος ἅπαξ, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 14.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικόν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον, Καθίσματα εἰς τὴν α΄ Στιχολογίαν τὰ γ΄ Ἀναστάσιμα Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτήρ, κτλ. εἰς τὴν β΄ Στιχολογίαν Τῷ φόβῳ τῶν Ἑβραίων δίς, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ καὶ ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, ὁ Κανὼν τῆς ἑορτῆς μετὰ Στίχων καὶ ὁ τοῦ Μηναίου. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Κάθισμα τοῦ Μηναίου καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας, αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα, ἡ θ΄ τῆς ἑορτῆς, ἡ Καταβασία Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, τὰ β΄ Ἐξαποστειλάρια ἀνὰ μίαν. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, γ΄ Ἀναστάσιμα τῆς

units.english_cohort_translation: ...the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: **"While the tomb was sealed..."** (*Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος*), and the Kontakion: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*). The Trisagion Hymn, the Epistle (Acts 5:12–20) and Gospel (John 20:19–31) of the Feast. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos of the Feast: **"O Thou radiant lamp and Mother of God, unsetting torch of the divine Glory, thee do we magnify in hymns!"** (*Σὲ τὴν φαεινὴν λαμπάδα*). Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem"** (*Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 147:1 LXX), and then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**. After the Prayer behind the Ambo, **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Feast. At "Especially," "O You shining lamp," Communion Hymn "Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem," and then "Christ is risen." After the
units.english_cohort_translation: 12.    On Sunday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the three Stichera of the Praises: **"After Thine awesome Resurrection from the tomb..."** (*Μετὰ τὴν ἐκ τάφου σου φρικτήν*) and the three Stichera of the Saint of the day from the Menaion; "Glory... Both now and ever..." in Tone 1: **"When the doors were closed..."** (*Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων*). Entrance with the censer, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*), and the Great Prokimenon: **"What God is as great as our God? Thou art the God Who workest wonders!"** (*Τίς Θεὸς Μέγας ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν; Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια*, Ps. 76:14 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Sticheron: **"Our evening prayers receive, O holy Lord..."** (*Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχάς*) and the two Penitential Stichera; "Glory... Both now and ever..." in Tone 1: **"Eight days after Thy Resurrection, O Jesus our King..."** (*Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"While the tomb was sealed..."** (once), and Dismissal.
