units.english_cohort_translation: 13.    On Friday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the first three Stichera of the Feast: **"When the doors were closed..."** (*Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων*) and three Stichera of the Menaion; "Glory...": **"When the doors were closed..."**; "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 1: **"The Joy of all the world, who sprang forth from mankind and gave birth unto the Master, the gate of heaven: let us hymn Mary the Virgin!..."** (*Τὴν παγκόσμιον δόξαν*); and the Prokimenon of the day. At the Aposticha: the four Resurrectional Stichera; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"O Lover of mankind, great and unsearchable is the multitude of Thy compassions!..."** (*Φιλάνθρωπε μέγα καὶ ἀνείκαστον*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"While the tomb was sealed..."** (three times), and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 14.    On Saturday at Matins, after the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion three times; then the Psalter. For the Kathismata of the First Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia] we chant the three Resurrectional Kathismata in Tone 1: **"Thy tomb, O Savior, the soldiers guarding became as dead men..."** (*Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτήρ*), etc.; for the Second Stasis, **"For fear of the Jews was Thy tomb sealed, O Savior..."** (*Τῷ φόβῳ τῶν Ἑβραίων*) (twice). Then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), and Psalm 50 (read plainly), the Canon of the Feast with verses, and the Canon of the Menaion. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma of the Menaion and that of the Feast; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, and the Menologion of the Saints of the day. The Katavasias of Pascha, the 9th Ode of the Feast, and the Katavasia: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace... Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). The Exaposteilaria once each. At the Praises: the three Resurrectional Stichera of...[^467]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 17.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς Κανών, ἡ Λιτὴ τῶν Μυροφόρων καὶ τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινόν, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον, ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων ¹¹. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, τὰ β΄ Καθίσματα, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῶν Μυροφόρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Μυροφόρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τῶν Μυροφόρων. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, Ἀναστάσιμα τῆς Ὀκτωήχου δ΄ καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, τὸ Ἑωθινὸν Μετὰ μύρων προσελθούσαις, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία _____________________________ 11. Ὁ Κανὼν τῶν Μυροφόρων, ὡς ἀναγινωσκόμενος ἐν ταῖς ἄλλαις ἡμέραις τῆς ἑβδομάδος, καταλιμπάνεται συνήθως σήμερον· τὸ αὐτὸ συμβαίνει καὶ διὰ τὰς ἀκολούθους Κυριακάς, τοῦ Παραλύτου, τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος καὶ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ.

units.english_cohort_translation: 15.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: **"While the tomb was sealed..."** (*Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος*) and the Kontakion: **"With his inquisitive right hand, Thomas explored Thy life-giving side, O Christ God..."** (*Τῇ φιλοπράγμονι δεξιᾷ*); the Epistle (Acts 5:21–33) and Gospel (John 3:22–33) of the day. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos of the Feast: **"O Thou radiant lamp and Mother of God, unsetting torch of the divine Glory, thee do we magnify in hymns!"** (*Σὲ τὴν φαεινὴν λαμπάδα*). Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem"** (*Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 147:1 LXX), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**, **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"**, and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Lord, O Jerusalem," "Christ is risen," "Blessed be the name of the Lord"
units.english_cohort_translation: 16.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant seven Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2 and three of the Myrrh-bearers; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"The Myrrh-bearing Women, reaching Thy tomb at deep dawn, sought Thee to anoint Thine immaculate Body with myrrh!..."** (*Αἱ Μυροφόροι Γυναῖκες*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 2: **"The shadow of the law passed away when grace arrived..."** (*Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιὰ τοῦ νόμου*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 2: **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, hath enlightened the whole universe..."** (*Ἡ Ἀνάστασίς σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Paschal Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, Joseph taking Thee down from the Tree with Nicodemus wept and lamented..."** (*Σὲ τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον τὸ φῶς*). The three Dismissal Troparia of the Myrrh-bearers: 1. Tone 2: **"The noble Joseph, taking down Thine immaculate Body from the Tree..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσήφ*), 2. "Glory...": **"When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brilliance of Thy Godhead..."** (*Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*), 3. "Both now and ever...": **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women, the Angel standing by the tomb cried aloud: Myrrh is fitting for the dead, but Christ is shown to be a stranger to corruption!..."** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί*), and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 17.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 2, the Liti of the Myrrh-bearers, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, **"The noble Joseph..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσήφ*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 2, the Anavathmoi of Tone 2, and the Prokimenon in Tone 2: **"Arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which Thou hast commanded..."** (Ps. 7:7 LXX). The Canon of Pascha with the two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus [Note 11]. After the 3rd Ode, the two Kathismata; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 2: **"Thou didst command the myrrh-bearing women to rejoice, O Christ God..."** and the Ikos of the Myrrh-bearers, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers. The Katavasias of Pascha and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Second Eothinon: Mark 16:1–8); then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia. The Exaposteilarion of Pascha: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητὸς*) and that of the Myrrh-bearers: **"Listen, ye women, to the voice of joy: having trampled down tyrannical Hades..."** (*Γυναῖκες ἀκουτίσθητε*). At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2, and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": the Second Eothinon Doxastikon in Tone 2: **"Coming with myrrhs, Mary's companions were perplexed..."** (*Μετὰ μύρων προσελθούσαις*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). units.slavonic_diplomatic: 18.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικόν. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὰ γ΄ Ἀπολυτίκια κατὰ σειράν, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον τοῦ Πάσχα, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν Σῶμα Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 19.    Τῇ Παρασκευῇ τῆς αὐτῆς ἑβδομάδος ἑσπέρας, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ γ΄ τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Μυροφόρων πρῶτα Στιχηρὰ καὶ γ΄ ἐκ τοῦ Μηναίου, Δόξα, Αἱ Μυροφόροι γυναῖκες, Καὶ νῦν, Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιά. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ δ΄ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Σὲ τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον τὸ φῶς, τὰ γ΄ Ἀπολυτίκια τῶν Μυροφόρων καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 21.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανών, τὸ τῆς Λιτῆς Δόξα, Ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρᾳ, Καὶ νῦν, Ναὸς καὶ πύλη, καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον δίς, καὶ ἅπαξ τὸ Θεοτοκίον, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος· τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον· ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Ῥῆμα Παράλυτον, Καὶ νῦν, Τὴν ὡραιότητα. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τοῦ Παραλύτου, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Παραλύτου.

units.english_cohort_translation: 18.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the three Dismissal Troparia of the Myrrh-bearers in sequence, that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion of Pascha: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*); the Epistle (Acts 6:1–7) and Gospel (Mark 15:43–16:8) of the Sunday. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and do thou, O pure Theotokos, rejoice in the Resurrection of Him Whom thou didst bear!"** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**, **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"**, and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 19.    On Friday evening of that week, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the first three Stichera of the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers and three Stichera of the Menaion; "Glory...": **"The Myrrh-bearing Women, reaching Thy tomb at deep dawn..."** (*Αἱ Μυροφόροι Γυναῖκες*); "Both now and ever...": **"The shadow of the law passed away when grace arrived..."** (*Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιὰ τοῦ νόμου*). At the Aposticha: the four Resurrectional Stichera; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment..."** (*Σὲ τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον τὸ φῶς*). The three Dismissal Troparia of the Myrrh-bearers and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Theotokion (once), the Psalter and the Amomos. The Kathismata of the
units.english_cohort_translation: 20.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant seven Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3, and three of the Paralytic, repeating the first; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"Jesus went up to Jerusalem to the Sheep's Pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porches..."** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 3: **"How can we not marvel at thy childbirth, wherein God and man are united, O all-honored Lady?..."** (*Πῶς μὴ θαυμάσωμεν*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 3: **"Thou Who by Thy Passion, O Christ, didst darken the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection didst enlighten all things: accept our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind!"** (*Ὁ τῷ πάθει σου Χριστέ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"In Solomon's porch lay a multitude of the sick, and at Mid-feast Christ found the Paralytic who had been lying there thirty and eight years..."** (*Ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τοῦ Σολομῶντος*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 3: **"Let the heavens rejoice, let earthly things be glad; for the Lord hath wrought might with His arm!..."** (*Εὐφραινέσθω τὰ Οὐράνια*); the Theotokion in Tone 3: **"Thou Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin, and didst endure the Cross, O Good One, and didst despoil death by death, and as God didst reveal the Resurrection: overlook not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thine own hand!..."** (*Σὲ τὴν μεσιτεύσασαν*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: First and Second Stasis [Stichologia], the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the
units.english_cohort_translation: 21.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 3; at the Liti, "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"At the Sheep's Pool a man lay sick for thirty and eight years..."** (*Ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρᾳ*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"A temple and gate art thou, a palace and throne of the King, O all-honored Virgin..."** (*Ναὸς καὶ πύλη*); and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 3 (twice) and the Theotokion (once), the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 3, the Anavathmoi of Tone 3, and the Prokimenon in Tone 3: **"Chant unto our God, chant! Chant unto our King, chant!"** (*Ψάλατε τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν, ψάλατε*, Ps. 46:7 LXX). The Canon of Pascha with its two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma in Tone 3: **"A word alone paralyzed the limbs of the sick man..."** (*Ῥῆμα Παράλυτον*); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Kathisma in Tone 4: **"Awed by the beauty of thy virginity and the exceeding brilliance of thy purity, Gabriel cried aloud unto thee, O Theotokos: What praise worthy of thee shall I offer?..."** (*Τὴν ὡραιότητα*). After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 3: **"As of old Thou didst raise up the Paralytic, O Lord, by Thy divine presence: so raise up my soul, paralyzed by grievous sins and shameful deeds!..."** and the Ikos of the Paralytic, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Paralytic. The Katavasias of Pascha and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Third Eothinon: Mark 16:9–20); then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia...[^469]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 22.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικὸν τοῦ Πάσχα. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Εὐφραινέσθω τὰ Οὐράνια, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον τοῦ Πάσχα, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα, Συμφώνως Παρθένε¹², Κοινωνικὸν Σῶμα Χριστοῦ.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Τῌ ΤΕΤΑΡΤῌ ΤΗΣ ΜΕΣΟΠΕΝΤΗΚΟΣΤΗΣ 23.    Τῇ Τρίτῃ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ὁ Προοιμιακός, εἰς δὲ τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα τὰ γ΄ Προσόμοια Πάρεστιν ἡ μεσότης ἡμερῶν εἰς ς΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης. Εἴσοδος, τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα Πεντηκοστῆς ἐφέστηκεν, Στίχοι Μνήσθητι τῆς συναγωγῆς σου ἧς ἐκτήσω ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς, καὶ Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς Βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων εἰργάσατο σωτηρίαν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 24.    Τῇ Τετάρτῃ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικόν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἶτα τὰ δύο Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας ἐκ β΄, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ καὶ ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα. Οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἄνευ στίχων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὰ β΄ Καθίσματα, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἑορτῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Θάλασσαν ἔπηξας, εἶτα ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ τῶν δύο Κανόνων, ἡ Καταβασία Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον δίς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ Προσόμοια εἰς δ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Φωτισθέντες ἀδελφοί, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον.

units.english_cohort_translation: ...the two Theotokia. The Exaposteilarion of Pascha: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητός*), and that of the Paralytic: **"The all-compassionate Lord..."** (*Ὁ παντοδύναμος Κύριος*). At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3, and the first Paschal Sticheron: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"O Lord, the Paralytic..."** (*Κύριε τὸν Παράλυτον*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another!..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world: let us sing unto Him Who arose from the tomb, the Author of our life!..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Psalm. At "Lord, I have cried" we chant the 3 Stichira "Now has come the midpoint of the days" in six (i.e., twice each), Glory, Now and ever, "As the Feast comes to its midpoint." Entrance, the Prokimenon of the day and the Readings. At the Aposticha: the 3 Idiomela "The midpoint of the days of Pentecost has arrived," with the Verses "Remember Your congrega- tion, which You have purchased from the beginning," and "God, our King from before the ages, has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth,"
units.english_cohort_translation: 22.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Paschal Antiphons and the Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 3: **"Let the heavens rejoice, let earthly things be glad!..."** (*Εὐφραινέσθω τὰ Οὐράνια*), that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion of Pascha: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*). The Epistle (Acts 9:32–42) and Gospel (John 5:1–15) of the Sunday. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα*), with the Ninth Heirmos of the Canon: **"With one voice, O Virgin, we bless thee: Hail, gate of the Lord, through which none may pass!..."** (*Συμφώνως Παρθένε*) [Note 12]. Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 24.    On Wednesday at Matins, after the Midnight Service, the Trisagion, the Apolytikion and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikion (three times), the Psalter; then the Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis
units.english_cohort_translation: 23.    On Tuesday evening, after **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), we recite the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX). At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the three Prosomia: **"Now has come the midpoint of the days..."** (*Πάρεστιν ἡ μεσότης ἡμερῶν*) to six (i.e., twice each); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"As the Feast comes to its midpoint, O Christ God..."** (*Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης*). Entrance with censer, the Prokimenon of the day, and the Old Testament Readings (Micah 4:2–3, 5; 5:2–5, 8; Isaiah 55:1–3, 6–11; Proverbs 9:1–11 LXX). At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela: **"The midpoint of the days of Pentecost has arrived..."** (*Πεντηκοστῆς ἐφέστηκεν*), with the appointed Verses: **"Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning"** (*Μνήσθητι τῆς συναγωγῆς σου ἧς ἐκτήσω ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς*, Ps. 73:2 LXX), and **"God is our King before the ages: He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth"** (*Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς Βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων εἰργάσατο σωτηρίαν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς*, Ps. 73:12 LXX); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast, provide Thou my thirsty soul with the water of piety, as Thou didst cry unto all, O Savior: Whosoever thirsts, let him come unto Me and drink! O Well-spring of our life, Christ God, glory to Thee!"** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*) three times, and Dismissal.

Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"As the Feast comes to its midpoint, O Christ God..."** (*Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης*). units.english_cohort_translation: 24.    On Wednesday at Matins, after the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8 (three times); then the Psalter; then the two Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], twice each. Then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) and Psalm 50 recited plainly. Both Canons without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the two Kathismata; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 4: **"As the Feast of the Law is at midpoint, O Creator and Master of all, Thou didst say unto those present, O Christ God: Come and draw forth the water of immortality!..."** (*Τῆς ἑορτῆς τῆς νομικῆς μεσαζούσης*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Feast. The Katavasias: **"Thou didst make the sea a wall..."** (*Θάλασσαν ἔπηξας*); then the 9th Ode of both Canons, and the Katavasia: **"Virginity is alien to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins; yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished!..."** (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων*); the Exaposteilarion: **"Having arrived at the midpoint of the feasts..."** (*Ὁ τὸν κρατῆρα ἔχων*) twice. At the Praises: three Prosomia to four (repeating the first); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 4: **"Having been enlightened, brethren, by the Resurrection of Christ the Savior..."** (*Φωτισθέντες ἀδελφοί*). Great Doxology and the Dismissal Troparion.[^470]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 25.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικὸν τοῦ Πάσχα. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον τῆς ἑορτῆς· ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων ἡ παρθενία, Κοινωνικὸν Ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα, Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Τῌ Ε΄ ΚΥΡΙΑΚῌ ΑΠΟ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΣΧΑ 26.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, ὁ Προοιμιακὸς καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ τῆς Μεσοπεντηκοστῆς γ΄ καὶ γ΄ τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος. Δόξα, Παρὰ τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ Ἰακώβ, Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ διὰ σε θεοπάτωρ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Κύριε ἀνελθὼν ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ, καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν. Δόξα, τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, Καὶ νῦν, τῆς ἑορτῆς Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 27.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανών, τὸ Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, τῆς Λιτῆς Ἀγαλλιάσθω σήμερον φαιδρῶς, καὶ τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δίς, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος· τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον.
units.english_cohort_translation: 26.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, ὁ Προοιμιακὸς καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ τῆς Μεσοπεντηκοστῆς γ΄ καὶ γ΄ τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος. Δόξα, Παρὰ τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ Ἰακώβ, Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ διὰ σε θεοπάτωρ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Κύριε ἀνελθὼν ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ, καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν. Δόξα, τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, Καὶ νῦν, τῆς ἑορτῆς Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_incipit: Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν δύο Θεοτοκίων, Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ α΄ Κάθισμα τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ β΄ τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, καὶ τὸ γ΄ αὖθις τῆς ἑορτῆς. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν δύο Θεοτοκίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα, τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Ἡ πηγὴ τῆς ζωαρχίας, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.english_cohort_translation: 25.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Paschal Antiphons and Entrance Hymn. After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast; the Epistle (Acts 14:6–18) and Gospel (John 7:14–30) of the day. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: the Ninth Heirmos of Mid-Pentecost: **"Virginity is alien to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins; yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished!..."** (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων ἡ παρθενία*). Communion Hymn: **"He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him. Alleluia!"** (*Ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα*, John 6:56), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 26.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 4, three of Mid-Pentecost, and three of the Samaritan Woman; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"By Jacob's well Jesus found the Samaritan woman: He Who covers the earth with clouds asks water of her..."** (*Παρὰ τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ Ἰακώβ*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 4: **"The grandparent of God for Thy sake, David the Prophet, melodiously sang concerning thee unto Him Who wrought great things in thee..."** (*Ὁ διὰ σὲ θεοπάτωρ*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 4: **"O Lord, when Thou didst ascend the Cross, Thou didst wipe away our ancestral curse..."** (*Κύριε ἀνελθὼν ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory...": of the Samaritan Woman, in Tone 8; "Both now and ever...": of the Feast, in Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Having learned the joyful proclamation of the Resurrection from the angel..."** (*Τὸ φαιδρὸν τῆς Ἀναστάσεως*), the Dismissal Troparion of the Feast in Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Communion Hymn "He who eats My flesh," "Christ is risen," "Blessed be the name of the Lord," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 27.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 4, the "Glory... Both now and ever..." of the Liti: **"Let heaven and earth exult today in joy, for Christ hath appeared in the flesh as man!..."** (*Ἀγαλλιάσθω σήμερον φαιδρῶς*), and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4 (twice) and that of the Feast (once); the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 4, the Anavathmoi of Tone 4, and the Prokimenon in Tone 4. The Canon of Pascha with the two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus. After the 3rd Ode, the first Kathisma of the Feast, the second of the Samaritan Woman, and the third again of the Feast. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"Having come to the well in faith, the Samaritan woman beheld Thee, the Water of Wisdom; and having drunk abundantly, she inherited the heavenly kingdom, ever praised in songs!"** (*Πίστει ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ φρέατι*) and the Ikos of the Samaritan Woman, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman. The Katavasias of Pascha (**"It is the day of Resurrection..."**) and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Fourth Eothinon: Luke 24:1–12); then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia. The Exaposteilaria: of Pascha, of the Samaritan Woman, and of the Feast. At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 4, and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"The well-spring of the beginning of life, Jesus our Savior, having come to the well of the Patriarch Jacob..."** (*Ἡ πηγὴ τῆς ζωαρχίας*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Τῌ ΣΤ΄ ΚΥΡΙΑΚῌ ΑΠΟ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΣΧΑ 29.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, ὁ Προοιμιακὸς καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ ζ΄ καὶ γ΄ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Δόξα, Κύριε παράγων ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, Καὶ νῦν, Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα σωτῆρα Χριστόν, καὶ τὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον, καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 30.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανών, τὸ Δόξα τῆς Λιτῆς, Καὶ νῦν, Νεῦσον παρακλήσεσι, καὶ τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον δίς, καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Δεσπότης δίς, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τοῦ Τυφλοῦ, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς.
units.english_cohort_translation: 30. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον δίς, καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Δεσπότης δίς, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τοῦ Τυφλοῦ, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων, ἡ Καταβασία Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ τὰ β΄ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Δεσπότης δίς, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τοῦ Τυφλοῦ, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων, ἡ Καταβασία Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ τὰ β΄ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.english_cohort_translation: *Rubrical Note:* The Service of the Samaritan Woman is chanted only on Sunday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, on which day its Apodosis is celebrated. On Monday and Tuesday we chant the Afterfeast hymns of Mid-Pentecost. On Wednesday we celebrate the Apodosis of Mid-Pentecost, the Service being chanted as prescribed in Paragraphs 23–25, except for the Old Testament Readings. The Epistle and Gospel are of the day.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: THE SIXTH SUNDAY FROM EASTER 29.    On Saturday evening following the Introductory Psalm and the
units.english_cohort_translation: 29.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant seven Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 5, and three of the Blind Man; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"Lord, passing by on the way, Thou didst find a man blind from his birth..."** (*Κύριε παράγων ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 5: **"In the Red Sea there was once depicted an image of the unwedded bride..."** (*Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 5: **"Thou Who didst take flesh, O Christ our Savior, and yet wast not parted from the heavens..."** (*Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα σωτῆρα Χριστόν*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"O Sun of Righteousness, Christ God, Who by Thy pure touch didst grant light to both eyes of him who from his mother's womb was deprived of light..."** (*Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, Who for our salvation was born of the Virgin, let us faithful praise and worship!..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), the Theotokion in Tone 5: **"Hail, impassable Gate of the Lord!..."** (*Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, Who for our salvation was born of the Virgin, let us faithful praise and worship!..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), the Theotokion in Tone 5: **"Hail, impassable Gate of the Lord!..."** (*Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 30.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 5, the "Glory..." of the Liti, and "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"Incline to the entreaties of thy servants, O all-blameless one..."** (*Νεῦσον παρακλήσεσι*), and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5 (twice) and the Theotokion (once); the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 5, the Anavathmoi of Tone 5, and the Prokimenon in Tone 5. The Canon of Pascha with the two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma in Tone 8: **"As the Master of all and the Fashioner, passing by on the way, Thou didst find a blind man seated and lamenting..."** (*Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Δεσπότης*) (twice); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 4: **"My soul's eyes being blind, I come unto Thee, O Christ, as the man blind from birth, crying unto Thee in repentance: Thou art the most radiant Light of those in darkness!"** (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*) and the Ikos of the Blind Man, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Blind Man. The Katavasias: **"Let us sing unto the Savior God, Who led the people through the sea with dry feet..."** (*Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ*) and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Fifth Eothinon: Luke 24:12–35); then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia, and the Katavasia: **"Thee who art beyond human mind and word, who hast given birth in time unto the Timeless One, the faithful with one accord do magnify!"** (*Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν*). The Exaposteilarion of Pascha: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητός*) and the two Exaposteilaria of the Blind Man: **"Passing by, our Savior found the blind man..."** (*Παράγων ὁ Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν*). At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 5, and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"Who can tell of Thy mighty acts, O Christ, or who can recount the multitudes of Thy wonders?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ τοῦ Σαββάτου ἑσπέρας τῆς Ὀκτωήχου δ΄ Στιχηρὰ Διὰ τοῦ Τιμίου σου Σταυροῦ, Ὁ τὴν Ἀνάστασιν διδούς, Μέγα θαῦμα καὶ τὸ Ἀπόστιχον Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα, μετὰ τῶν στίχων Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσε κτλ. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 33.    Τῇ Τρίτῃ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικόν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ ἅπαξ τὸ Θεοτοκίον, τὸ Ψαλτήριον, τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας τὰ ἐν τῇ Τετάρτῃ σημειούμενα, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ, ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς καὶ ὁ Κανὼν τῆς Κυριακῆς Σταύρωσιν ἑκούσιον, οὗ ὁ Στίχος Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι, καὶ ὁ Προεόρτιος Ἄνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μετὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ Στίχου.

Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ ἅπαξ τὸ Θεοτοκίον, τὸ Ψαλτήριον, τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας τὰ ἐν τῇ Τετάρτῃ σημειούμενα, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ, ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς καὶ ὁ Κανὼν τῆς Κυριακῆς Σταύρωσιν ἑκούσιον, οὗ ὁ Στίχος Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι, καὶ ὁ Προεόρτιος Ἄνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μετὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ Στίχου. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Ὠμμάτωσας Χριστέ, καὶ τὸ ἕτερον Ἐτέχθης ὡς αὐτός. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ τῆς Κυριακῆς, καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ, καὶ στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, ἡ Καταβασία Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, τὰ β΄ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ Ἐξαποστειλάρια. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ γ΄, τὰ τῶν Αἴνων τῆς Κυριακῆς, καὶ τὰ γ΄ πρῶτα ἑσπέρια τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον.

units.english_cohort_translation: 34.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικόν. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, καὶ Κοντάκιον Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν τῆς ἡμέρας, Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.english_cohort_translation: 32.    On Monday evening, the Apodosis of the Service of the Blind Man takes place. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the six Idiomela from the Pentekostarion which are indicated in the Vespers of Tuesday evening, in order; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"Who can tell of Thy mighty acts, O Christ?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 5: **"In the Red Sea there was once depicted an image of the unwedded bride..."** (*Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ*). At the Aposticha: the four Saturday evening Stichera of the Octoechos in Tone 5: **"By Thy precious Cross hast Thou put the devil to shame, O Christ..."** (*Διὰ τοῦ Τιμίου σου Σταυροῦ*), **"He Who has granted resurrection unto the human race..."** (*Ὁ τὴν Ἀνάστασιν διδούς*), **"O great wonder! The Creator of invisible things..."** (*Μέγα θαῦμα*), and the Apostichon: **"Thou Who didst take flesh, O Christ our Savior..."** (*Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα σωτῆρα Χριστόν*), with the verses: **"The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty!"** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν*, Ps. 92:1 LXX) etc.; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"O Sun of Righteousness, Christ God..."** (*Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), the Theotokion in Tone 5: **"Hail, impassable Gate of the Lord!..."** (*Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 33.    On Tuesday at Matins, after Midnight Service, the Trisagion, the
units.english_cohort_translation: 33.    On Tuesday at Matins, after the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5 (twice) and the Theotokion (once), then the Psalter. The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], which are indicated on Wednesday morning; then we recite **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), Psalm 50, and the Sunday Canon: **"Having accepted a voluntary crucifixion, O Master..."** (*Σταύρωσιν ἑκούσιον*), with the Verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι*), and the Forefeast Canon: **"Up unto the Father hast Thou ascended, O Christ God..."** (*Ἄνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα*) with the same Verse. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma in Tone 4: **"Thou didst give eyes to him who was blind from birth, O Christ..."** (*Ὠμμάτωσας Χριστέ*) and the other one: **"Thou wast born as such, O blind man..."** (*Ἐτέχθης ὡς αὐτός*). After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday of the Blind Man, and the Menologion of the Saints of the day. The Katavasias: **"Let us sing unto the Savior God..."** (*Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ*); and we chant **"More honorable than the Cherubim..."** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*) with the Katavasia: **"Thee who art beyond human mind and word..."** (*Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν*). The two Exaposteilaria of the Blind Man. At the Praises: three Resurrectional Stichera of the Sunday in Tone 5, and the first three Vespers hymns of the Blind Man; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"Who can tell of Thy mighty acts, O Christ?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*).

After the Entrance, the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5, that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion in Tone 4: **"My soul's eyes being blind, I come unto Thee, O Christ..."** (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*). At "Especially", **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure, and the Mother of our God!..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), the Communion Hymn of the day: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens, praise Him in the highest! Alleluia!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion: **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.[^473]

units.slavonic_incipit: Τῌ ΤΕΤΑΡΤῌ ΤΗΣ ΣΤ΄ ΕΒΔΟΜΑΔΟΣ Η
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Τῌ ΤΕΤΑΡΤῌ ΤΗΣ ΣΤ΄ ΕΒΔΟΜΑΔΟΣ Η ΑΠΟΔΟΣΙΣ ΤΗΣ ΕΟΡΤΗΣ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΣΧΑ 35.    Τῇ Τρίτῃ ἑσπέρας ἀναγινώσκεται ἡ θ΄ ὥρα τρίψαλμος, ἐν ᾗ λέγομεν Ἀπολυτίκιον Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον, καὶ Κοντάκιον Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα· εἶτα ἀντὶ τοῦ Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς λέγεται (ὡς εἴθισται νῦν) Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ ψάλλεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἱερέως ἔσωθεν τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη γ΄ καὶ ἀνὰ γ΄ ὑπὸ [ἑκάστου] τῶν Χορῶν, καὶ ἅπαξ αὖθις ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἱερέως. [Σημειωτέον ὅτι ἡ τάξις τοῦ Πεντηκοσταρίου ἁπλῶς λέγει· «Καὶ ψάλλομεν τὸ Χριστὸς Ἀνέστη, μετὰ τῶν στίχων αὐτοῦ ὅπως ἔγινε τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Πάσχα.» Ὡς φαίνεται, ἀπαιτεῖται ἐδῶ ἡ ἰδία τάξις, δηλαδή, ἐὰν ἕκαστος τῶν δύο Χορῶν ψάλλει τὸ Χριστὸς Ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄, τότε ἔχομεν τὸ σύνολον τῶν 10 ὅπως εἰς τὸ Πάσχα.]

units.slavonic_incipit: Εἶτα ἡ Συναπτή. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Εἶτα ἡ Συναπτή. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν Στιχηρὰ τῆς Ὀκτωήχου Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχὰς κατὰ σειρὰν ς΄. Δόξα, Τὸν τῷ Πατρὶ συνάναρχον, Καὶ νῦν, Τὴν παγκόσμιον δόξαν. Εἴσοδος, καὶ τὸ τῆς ἡμέρας Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὸ Στιχηρὸν Τῷ πάθει σου Χριστέ, καὶ τὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη τρίς, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 36.    Τῷ πρωῒ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον μετὰ τὸ μεσονυκτικὸν τοῦ Πάσχα (ὅρα ἐν § 2 ὑποσημ. 8) ὁ Ἱερεὺς θυμιῶν ἐνώπιον τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης ἐκφωνεῖ Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ, καὶ ψάλλει τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ὡς χθές· εἶτα ἡ Συναπτὴ καὶ ψάλλεται ὁ Κανὼν εἰς δ΄, ἡ Καταβασία ὁμοῦ, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη γ΄, τὸ Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἡ Αἴτησις καὶ ἡ Ἐκφώνησις ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ γ΄, τὸ Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡ ζ΄ καὶ η΄ τοῦ Κανόνος Ὠδή· εἶτα Τὴν θεοτόκον, καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ἐκ γ΄. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ Στιχηρὰ Ὑμνοῦμέν σου Χριστὲ εἰς δ΄ καὶ τὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη τρίς, καὶ ἄρχεται ἡ Λειτουργία.

units.english_cohort_translation: 35.    On Tuesday evening the Ninth Hour is read as tri-psalmic (i.e., involving three psalms: Psalms 83, 84, 85 LXX), at which we say the Dismissal Troparion: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), and the Kontakion: **"My soul's eyes being blind, I come unto Thee, O Christ..."** (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*); then, instead of the usual **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**, the Priest exclaims (as is the custom now): **"Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and indivisible Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ*). Then the Priest inside the Sanctuary chants **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) three times; this hymn is chanted also three times by each of the two Choirs, and again immediately once by the Priest from the Sanctuary [Note: The rubrics of the Pentekostarion state simply: "And we chant Christ is risen with its verses, exactly as was done on the day of Pascha." Apparently, this exact order is what is actually being called for here: if each of the two Choirs chants "Christ is risen" three times, we have the sum total of 10 times, as on the day of Pascha].

units.english_cohort_translation: Then the Litany follows. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the six Stichera of the Octoechos in Tone 5: **"Accept our evening prayers, O holy Lord, and grant unto us remission of sins; for Thou alone art He Who didst manifest the Resurrection unto the world!"** (*Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχάς*) in order; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"Him Who is co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, let us praise..."** (*Τὸν τῷ Πατρὶ συνάναρχον*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 1: **"The Joy of all the world, who sprang forth from mankind and gave birth unto the Master..."** (*Τὴν παγκόσμιον δόξαν*). Entrance with censer, and the Prokimenon of the day: **"Thy mercy, O Lord, shall pursue me all the days of my life!"** (*Τὸ ἔλεός σου, Κύριε*, Ps. 22:6 LXX). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 5: **"By Thy Passion, O Christ, hast Thou darkened the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection hast Thou enlightened all things..."** (*Τῷ πάθει σου Χριστέ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another!..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 36.    In the morning at Matins, after the Midnight Office of Pascha (see Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest censing in front of the Holy Table exclaims: **"Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and indivisible Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**, and chants **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) as yesterday; then the Litany, and the Paschal Canon is chanted with four Troparia for each ode including the Katavasia. Then we chant **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), the hymn: **"Jesus, having arisen from the tomb, as He foretold, hath given unto us life eternal and great mercy!"** (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ τάφου*), the Litany, and the Exclamation at the end of each Ode. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoe: **"Coming before the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..."** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον*) (recited plainly); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** and the Ikos of Pascha, then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the holy Lord Jesus..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) (three times), and **"Jesus, having arisen from the tomb..."** (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς*); then the 7th and 8th Odes of the Canon are chanted. Then the deacon or priest proclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light, honoring her in hymns, let us magnify!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the 9th Ode is chanted with the Megalynaria of Pascha. The Exaposteilarion: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst arise..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητός*) (three times). At the Praises: the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1: **"We praise Thy saving Passion, O Christ, and glorify Thy Resurrection!"** (*Ὑμνοῦμέν σου Χριστέ*) and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), and the Divine Liturgy begins.[^474]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 37.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικόν. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον, Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν τοῦ Πάσχα, Χριστὸς ἀνέστη. Μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχήν, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄ χῦμα, Ἀπόλυσις καὶ Ἀπόδοσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 38.    Τῇ Τετάρτῃ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὴν Θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα, ὁ Ἱερεὺς Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ Προοιμιακὸς μετὰ τοῦ Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν ἐκ γ΄. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ [ε]1 Ἰδιόμελα Ὁ Κύριος ἀνελήφθη εἰς ς΄ δευτεροῦντες τὸ α΄. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τῶν κόλπων τῶν Πατρικῶν. Εἴσοδος, τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις μετὰ τοῦ Ὁ ἐν δόξῃ ἀναληφθεὶς ἀφ᾿ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς Οὐρανοὺς καὶ ἐν δεξιᾷ καθίσας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς . . .

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 39.    Τῇ Πέμπτῃ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ἡ Λιτή, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος· τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν ἐκ β΄, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοί, τὸ α΄ Ἀντίφωνον τοῦ δ΄ ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, Κύριος ἐν φωνῇ σάλπιγγος, τὸ Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ τὸ γ΄ Ἑωθινὸν Εὐαγγέλιον, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι, καὶ ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα. Δόξα, Ταῖς τῶν Ἀποστόλων, Καὶ νῦν, Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου, ὁ Στίχος Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεὸς καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Σήμερον ἐν Οὐρανοῖς αἱ ἄνω δυνάμεις. Οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι εἰς ς΄ καὶ εἰς δ΄ ἄνευ στίχων· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα ἅπαξ, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς Ὑπόμνημα. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Θείῳ καλυφθείς, εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ Θ΄ ὁ μὲν α΄ Κανὼν ἄνευ Στίχου, ὁ β΄ μετὰ τοῦ Μεγαλυναρίου Ἄγγελοι τὴν ἄνοδον τοῦ Δεσπότου . . . πῶς μετὰ δόξης ἐπήρθη ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς εἰς τὰ ἄνω· ἡ Καταβασία Χαίροις Ἄνασσα, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον ἐκ γ΄. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ γ΄ Προσόμοια εἰς δ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἐτέχθης ὡς αὐτὸς ἠθέλησας, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ.

units.slavonic_incipit: Aposticha: the three Idiomela, Glory, Now
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Aposticha: the three Idiomela, Glory, Now and ever, "God is gone up in a shout." The Apolytikion three times and Dismissal with the following prologue: "You who gloriously ascended from us to the Heavens and sat at the right hand of God the Father, Christ our true God . . ."
units.english_cohort_translation: 37.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons and the Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance we chant **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), the Ypakoe, and the Kontakion. Instead of the Trisagion Hymn we chant **"As many as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia!"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*); the Epistle and the Gospel of the day. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee!..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Communion Hymn of Pascha: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*). After the Prayer behind the Amvon, **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times) recited plainly, the Dismissal, and the Apodosis.

units.english_cohort_translation: 38.    On Wednesday evening, after the Ninth Hour of Pascha, the Priest intones **"Blessed is our God..."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς*), and the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) begins with **"Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God"** (three times). At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the five Idiomela: **"The Lord ascended into the heavens, that He might send the Paraclete unto the world..."** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἀνελήφθη*) to six, repeating the first hymn; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"Without parting from the Fatherly bosom, O sweetest Jesus..."** (*Τῶν κόλπων τῶν Πατρικῶν*). Entrance with censer, the Prokimenon of the day, and the Old Testament Readings (Isaiah 2:2–3; 62:10–63:3, 7–9; Zechariah 14:1, 4, 8–11 LXX). At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet..."** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God, having gladdened Thy disciples with the promise of the Holy Spirit, they having been assured by the blessing that Thou art the Son of God, the Redeemer of the world!"** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*) three times, and the Dismissal with the following appointed prologue: **"He Who ascended in glory from us into the heavens and sat at the right hand of God the Father, Christ our true God..."** (*Ὁ ἐν δόξῃ ἀναληφθεὶς ἀφ᾿ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς Οὐρανοὺς καὶ ἐν δεξιᾷ καθίσας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*).

units.english_cohort_translation: 39.    On Thursday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Liti, then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ascended in glory..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion (three times); then the Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata in order, twice each; the Anavathmoi: the first Antiphon of Tone 4 (**"From my youth many passions war against me..."**), and the Prokimenon: **"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet!"** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, Κύριος ἐν φωνῇ σάλπιγγος*, Ps. 46:5 LXX), **"Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord!"** (*Πᾶσα πνοὴ*), and the Third Matins Gospel (Mark 16:9–20), **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), and Psalm 50 recited plainly. "Glory...": **"Through the intercessions of the Apostles..."** (*Ταῖς τῶν Ἀποστόλων*); "Both now and ever...": **"Through the intercessions of the Theotokos..."** (*Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*); the Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy..."** (*Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεὸς*), and the Idiomelon: **"Today the heavenly powers in the heavens marvel seeing our nature ascend..."** (*Σήμερον ἐν Οὐρανοῖς αἱ ἄνω δυνάμεις*). Both Canons, the first to six and the second to four, without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma (once); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 6: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes, and united things on earth with the heavenly, Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Feast. The Katavasias: **"Covered by a divine cloud, he that was slow of tongue proclaimed the Law written of God..."** (*Θείῳ καλυφθείς*); then the 9th Ode is chanted: the first Canon without verses, and the second Canon with its Megalynarion: **"Ye Angels, marveling at the ascension of the Master, how with glory He was taken up from earth unto the heights..."** (*Ἄγγελοι τὴν ἄνοδον τοῦ Δεσπότου . . . πῶς μετὰ δόξης ἐπήρθη ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς εἰς τὰ ἄνω*); the Katavasia: **"Rejoice, O Queen, boasting of virgins and mothers!..."** (*Χαίροις Ἄνασσα*), then the Exaposteilarion: **"While the disciples looked on, Thou wast taken up, O Christ, unto the Father, to sit beside Him..."** (*Τῶν Μαθητῶν ὁρώντων σε*) (three times). At the Praises: the three Prosomia to four (repeating the first); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 2: **"Thou wast born as Thou Thyself didst will; Thou didst appear as Thou Thyself didst wish; Thou didst suffer in the flesh, O our God..."** (*Ἐτέχθης ὡς αὐτὸς ἠθέλησας*)...[^475]

units.english_cohort_translation: The Entrance Hymn: **"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet! Save us, O Son of God, Who didst ascend in glory from us into the heavens, save us who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, Κύριος ἐν φωνῇ σάλπιγγος· Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν δόξῃ ἀναληφθείς...*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*), the Kontakion: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*)...[^476]

units.slavonic_incipit: Εὐαγγέλιον. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Σὲ τὴν
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Εὐαγγέλιον. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, Κοινωνικὸν Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, μετὰ τὸ Κοινωνικὸν τὸ Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις ἡ καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ 13 Τῌ Ζ΄ ΚΥΡΙΑΚῌ ΤΩΝ ΑΓΙΩΝ ΠΑΤΕΡΩΝ ΤΗΣ ΕΝ ΝΙΚΑΙᾼ Α΄ ΣΥΝΟΔΟΥ 41.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν Ἀναστάσιμα γ΄, τῆς Ἀναλήψεως γ΄ καὶ τῶν Πατέρων δ΄. Δόξα, Τὰς μυστικὰς σήμερον, Καὶ νῦν, Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε. Εἴσοδος Φῶς ἱλαρόν, τὸ Προκείμενον καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Τὴν ἐτήσιον μνήμην σήμερον, Καὶ νῦν, τῆς ἑορτῆς, Κύριε τὸ μυστήριον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Δόξα, τὸ τῶν Πατέρων, Καὶ νῦν, τὸ Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον, καὶ Οἶκος τὰ τῶν Πατέρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Πατέρων. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Θείῳ καλυφθείς, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἐξαποστειλάριον, τὸ τῶν Πατέρων, καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῶν Πατέρων δ΄. Δόξα, Τῶν Ἁγίων Πατέρων ὁ χορός, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη. Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Apolytikion of the Resurrection, Glory that of the Fathers, Now and ever, "You have ascended in glory," and Dismissal.
units.english_cohort_translation: 41.    In Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant three Resurrectional Stichera of Tone 6, three of the Ascension, and four of the Fathers; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"Let us extol today the mystical trumpets of the Spirit, the God-bearing Fathers..."** (*Τὰς μυστικὰς σήμερον*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion of Tone 6: **"Who would not call thee blessed, O all-holy Virgin?..."** (*Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε*). Entrance with censer, **"O Joyful Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokimenon of the day: **"The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty!"** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν*, Ps. 92:1 LXX), and the Old Testament Readings (Genesis 14:14–20; Deuteronomy 1:8–11, 15–17; 10:14–21 LXX). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Stichera; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 4: **"Let us faithfully celebrate today the yearly commemoration of the God-bearing Fathers..."** (*Τὴν ἐτήσιον μνήμην σήμερον*); "Both now and ever...": of the Feast, in Tone 4: **"O Lord, having fulfilled the mystery hidden from the ages..."** (*Κύριε τὸ μυστήριον*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion of Tone 6, "Glory...": that of the Fathers in Tone 8: **"Most glorified art Thou, O Christ our God, Who hast established our Fathers as luminous stars upon the earth..."** (*Ὑπερδεδοξασμένος εἶ*); "Both now and ever...": that of the Ascension in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 42.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon, the Glory of the Liti "Of the Apostolic traditions," Now and ever of the Feast "Lord, when You did fulfill the mystery of the economy"; then the "It is meet,"
units.english_cohort_translation: 42.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 6, the "Glory..." of the Liti: **"Keeping the Apostolic traditions..."** (*Ἀποστολικῶν παραδόσεων*); "Both now and ever...": of the Feast: **"O Lord, having fulfilled the mystery of the dispensation..."** (*Κύριε τῆς οἰκονομίας πληρώσας τὸ μυστήριον*); then the Triadic hymns: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Fathers: **"Most glorified art Thou, O Christ our God..."** (*Ὑπερδεδοξασμένος εἶ*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Resurrectional Kathismata in order, the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 6, the Anavathmoi of Tone 6, and the Prokimenon of Tone 6. The Canons: the Resurrectional Canon, that of the Feast, and that of the Fathers. After the 3rd Ode [Translator's Note: We recite the Kontakion of the Ascension: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*). Note that this is indicated both in the Pentekostarion and in the Imerologia [IEP] 1998 and 1999; though the Typikon itself is not clear on this issue, it appears that a look at the Protheoria (Violakis, p. 22, § 25) supports this practice], then the Kathisma of the Fathers and that of the Feast. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"The preaching of the Apostles and the dogmas of the Fathers confirmed the one Faith for the Church..."** (*Τῶν Ἀποστόλων τὸ κήρυγμα*) and the Ikos of the Fathers, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Fathers. The Katavasias: **"Covered by a divine cloud..."** (*Θείῳ καλυφθείς*), and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Tenth Eothinon: John 21:1–14); then we chant with verses: **"More honorable than the Cherubim..."** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*). Exaposteilaria: the Resurrectional Exaposteilarion, that of the Fathers, and that of the Feast. At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 6 and four of the Fathers; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"The choir of the Holy Fathers, coming together from the ends of the earth..."** (*Τῶν Ἁγίων Πατέρων ὁ χορός*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 2: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις*). Great Doxology and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).[^477]

units.english_text: 42.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 6, the "Glory..." of the Liti: **"Keeping the Apostolic traditions..."** (*Ἀποστολικῶν παραδόσεων*); "Both now and ever...": of the Feast: **"O Lord, having fulfilled the mystery of the dispensation..."** (*Κύριε τῆς οἰκονομίας πληρώσας τὸ μυστήριον*); then the Triadic hymns: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Fathers: **"Most glorified art Thou, O Christ our God..."** (*Ὑπερδεδοξασμένος εἶ*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Resurrectional Kathismata in order, the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 6, the Anavathmoi of Tone 6, and the Prokimenon of Tone 6. The Canons: the Resurrectional Canon, that of the Feast, and that of the Fathers. After the 3rd Ode [Translator's Note: We recite the Kontakion of the Ascension: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*). Note that this is indicated both in the Pentekostarion and in the Imerologia [IEP] 1998 and 1999; though the Typikon itself is not clear on this issue, it appears that a look at the Protheoria (Violakis, p. 22, § 25) supports this practice], then the Kathisma of the Fathers and that of the Feast. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"The preaching of the Apostles and the dogmas of the Fathers confirmed the one Faith for the Church..."** (*Τῶν Ἀποστόλων τὸ κήρυγμα*) and the Ikos of the Fathers, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Fathers. The Katavasias: **"Covered by a divine cloud..."** (*Θείῳ καλυφθείς*), and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Tenth Eothinon: John 21:1–14); then we chant with verses: **"More honorable than the Cherubim..."** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*). Exaposteilaria: the Resurrectional Exaposteilarion, that of the Fathers, and that of the Feast. At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 6 and four of the Fathers; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"The choir of the Holy Fathers, coming together from the ends of the earth..."** (*Τῶν Ἁγίων Πατέρων ὁ χορός*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 2: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις*). Great Doxology and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).[^477]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 43.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῶν Πατέρων. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς τῶν Πατέρων, καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ· Κοντάκιον Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας οἰκονομίαν· Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον· εἰς τὸ Μετὰ φόβου Θεοῦ Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 44.    Τῇ Παρασκευῇ ἑσπέρας, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ς΄ Στιχηρά, Μαρτυρικὰ δ΄ (ἐκ τῆς Ὀκτωήχου) Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε, καὶ γ΄ τῶν Κεκοιμημένων Τῶν ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος σήμερον νεκρῶν, Δόξα, Θρηνῶ καὶ ὀδύρομαι, Καὶ νῦν, Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε, ἀντὶ Προκειμένου ψάλλεται τρεῖς φορὰς τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα ἐκ γ΄ μετὰ τῶν ὡρισμένων στίχων εἰς τὰς δύο τελευταίας φοράς. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὸ Μαρτυρικὸν Ὁ Σταυρός σου Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δύο Νεκρώσιμα μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτῶν. Δόξα, Ἀρχή μοι καὶ ὑπόστασις, Καὶ νῦν, Πρεσβείαις τῆς τεκούσης σε, τὸ Νῦν ἀπολύεις, καὶ εὐθὺς ψάλλεται ὁ Κανὼν Ἐν οὐρανίοις θαλάμοις μετὰ τῶν Στίχων Πρεσβείαις τῶν Μαρτύρων σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, ἀνάπαυσον τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν δούλων σου, καὶ τὸ Αἱ ψυχαὶ αὐτῶν ἐν ἀγαθοῖς αὐλισθήσονται, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ. Ἀπ᾿ θ΄ ὁ Εἱρμός, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, Δόξα, τὸ τέλος Ἐν σοὶ γὰρ τὴν ἐλπίδα κτλ. Καὶ νῦν, Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος καὶ λιμένα ἔχομεν, εἶτα Μετὰ Πνευμάτων δικαίων κτλ. καὶ μνημονεύονται ἐπὶ τῶν κολλύβων τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν Κεκοιμημένων, ὡς ἐσημειώθη ἐν τῷ Τριῳ

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 44.    On Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried" we chant six verses and the 4 Martyrika {from the Oktoichos} "Your Martyrs, O Lord," and 3 for the Reposed "Today, those who have died in times past," Glory, "I weep and I lament," Now and ever, "Who would not call you blessed." Instead of the Prokimenon, we chant "Alleluia" three times with the verses designated to be sung only at the last two times. At the Aposticha: the
units.english_cohort_translation: 43.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Typika and the Beatitudes of Tone 6 to four, and four hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Fathers. After the Entrance, the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion of Tone 6, that of the Feast (Ascension), that of the Fathers, and that of the Patron Saint of the Church; the Kontakion: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*). The Epistle (Acts 20:16–18, 28–36) and Gospel (John 17:1–13) of the Sunday. At "Especially", **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*). Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens, praise Him in the highest! Alleluia!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX). At "With the fear of God...", we chant the Dismissal Troparion of the Ascension: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*). Then **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

On Friday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant six Stichera: four Martyrika from the Octoechos: **"Thy Martyrs, O Lord..."** (*Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε*), and three for the Reposed: **"Today, those who have died from time immemorial..."** (*Τῶν ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος σήμερον νεκρῶν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"I weep and I lament when I contemplate death..."** (*Θρηνῶ καὶ ὀδύρομαι*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 8: **"Who would not call thee blessed, O all-holy Virgin?..."** (*Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε*). In place of the Prokimenon, we chant **"Alleluia"** three times, with the appointed verses chanted for the last two times. At the Aposticha: the Martyrikon: **"Thy Cross, O Lord..."** (*Ὁ Σταυρός σου Κύριε*), and the two Stichera of the Reposed with their verses. "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"My beginning and foundation was Thy creative command..."** (*Ἀρχή μοι καὶ ὑπόστασις*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"By the intercessions of her who gave birth unto Thee, O Christ..."** (*Πρεσβείαις τῆς τεκούσης σε*). The prayer **"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..."** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*), and immediately we chant the Canon: **"In the heavenly bridal chambers..."** (*Ἐν οὐρανίοις θαλάμοις*) with the Verses: **"Through the intercessions of Thy Martyrs, O Christ God, give rest to the souls of Thy servants!"** (*Πρεσβείαις τῶν Μαρτύρων σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, ἀνάπαυσον τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν δούλων σου*) and **"Their souls shall dwell with good things"** (*Αἱ ψυχαὶ αὐτῶν ἐν ἀγαθοῖς αὐλισθήσονται*, Ps. 24:13 LXX), chanting "Glory...", "Both now and ever..." in each Ode. After the 9th Ode, the Heirmos, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*); "Glory...": the ending: **"For in Thee have they placed their hope, our Maker and Creator and God"** (*Ἐν σοὶ γὰρ τὴν ἐλπίδα*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"Thee do we have as a rampart and haven..."** (*Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος καὶ λιμένα ἔχομεν*); then the Troparia: **"With the souls of the righteous departed, give rest to the soul of Thy servant, O Savior..."** (*Μετὰ πνευμάτων δικαίων*), and the names of the Reposed are commemorated over the Kolyvo [boiled wheat], as noted in the Triodion...[^478]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 45.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικὸν τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος· εἶτα τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτοῦ καὶ τῶν Ἀπολυτικίων, ὡς ἐλέχθη ἐν τῷ Σαββάτῳ πρὸ τῆς Ἀπόκρεω· τὸ Ψαλτήριον, τὰ Καθίσματα, καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, καὶ μνημονεύονται τὰ ὀνόματα ὡς χθὲς ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ — τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, καὶ μετὰ τὴν Ἐκφώνησιν, {τὸ Κάθισμα} Ἀνάπαυσον Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν, {Δόξα,} Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου ἀνατείλας· εἶτα ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς καὶ ὁ Κανὼν Ψυχῶν πασῶν ὁ Δεσπότης μετὰ τῶν ὡρισμένων Στίχων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα, καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τοῦ Τριῳδίου· εἶτα ψάλλεται ὁ Εἱρμὸς τῆς η΄ Ὠδῆς Ἔκστηθι φρίττων Οὐρανέ, καὶ στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, ὁ Εἱρμὸς Ἀπορεῖ πᾶσα γλῶσσα, τὰ β΄ Ἐξαποστειλάρια. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ δ΄ Στιχηρὰ Φοβερὸν τὸ τέλος τὸ τοῦ θανάτου, Δόξα, Ὡς ἄνθος μαραίνεται, Καὶ νῦν, Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, τὸ Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει χῦμα, ἡ Συναπτή, καὶ τὰ δ΄ Ἀπόστιχα Ἔχων ἀκατάληπτον, Δόξα, Ἄλγος τῷ Ἀδάμ, Καὶ νῦν, Ὤφθης ἐνδιαίτημα, τὸ Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὰ δύο Τροπάρια, Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, καὶ τὸ Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος.

units.english_cohort_translation: 46.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα, Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι, μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, τὸ Κοντάκιον Μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων ἀνάπαυσον Χριστέ (ὅρα ς΄ Ὠδὴν τοῦ ἑσπερινοῦ Κανόνος). Ἀπόστολος Νεκρώσιμος, καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω, ἀντὶ τοῦ Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς, Ὁ βάθει σοφίας φιλανθρώπως πάντα οἰκονομῶν¹⁴· εἶτα ψάλλεται τὸ Μετὰ πνευμάτων δικαίων, καὶ μνημονεύονται τὰ ὀνόματα πάντων τῶν ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος κεκοιμημένων εὐσεβῶν καὶ Ὀρθοδόξων Χριστιανῶν κτλ. καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.english_cohort_translation: 45.    On Saturday at Matins, after the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*), and the Six Psalms; then **"Alleluia"** with its verses and the Dismissal Troparia, as prescribed on the Saturday before Meatfare Sunday; the Psalter, the Kathismata, and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma), and the names of the Reposed are commemorated as yesterday at Vespers; the Evlogitaria, and after the Exclamation, the Kathisma: **"Give rest with the righteous, O our Savior, unto Thy servants..."** (*Ἀνάπαυσον Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν*); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"O Thou Who didst dawn from the Virgin..."** (*Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου ἀνατείλας*). Then Psalm 50, and the Canon: **"O Master of all souls..."** (*Ψυχῶν πασῶν ὁ Δεσπότης*) with the prescribed verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma and the Theotokion. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"With the Saints grant rest, O Christ, unto the souls of Thy servants, where there is neither pain, nor grief, nor sighing, but life everlasting!"** (*Μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων ἀνάπαυσον*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Triodion; then we chant the Heirmos of the 8th Ode: **"Be astonished and tremble, O heaven..."** (*Ἔκστηθι φρίττων Οὐρανέ*), we chant with verses: **"More honorable than the Cherubim..."** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*), the Heirmos: **"Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee as is meet..."** (*Ἀπορεῖ πᾶσα γλῶσσα*), and the two Exaposteilaria. At the Praises: the four Stichera: **"Dreaded is the end, the coming of death..."** (*Φοβερὸν τὸ τέλος τὸ τοῦ θανάτου*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"As a flower fades, and as a shadow passes away, so is every man dissolved..."** (*Ὡς ἄνθος μαραίνεται*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 8: **"Thou art our God, Who in wisdom hast fashioned all things..."** (*Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*); the prayer **"To Thee belongs glory..."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) recited plainly, the Litany, and the four Aposticha: **"Having an inconceivable depth of compassions, O Christ..."** (*Ἔχων ἀκατάληπτον*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"A pain unto Adam was the eating of the tree of old in Eden..."** (*Ἄλγος τῷ Ἀδάμ*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"Thou hast been seen as a dwelling-place, O unwedded Virgin..."** (*Ὤφθης ἐνδιαίτημα*); then **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to chant unto Thy name, O Most High"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, Ps. 91:1 LXX); the Trisagion, the two Dismissal Troparia: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*) and **"Thee do we have as a rampart and haven..."** (*Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος καὶ λιμένα ἔχομεν*).

units.english_cohort_translation: 46.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord..."** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*). After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*), that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion: **"With the Saints grant rest, O Christ..."** (*Μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων ἀνάπαυσον*) (see the 6th Ode of the Vespers Canon). The Epistle of the Reposed (1 Thessalonians 4:13–17) and Gospel of the day (John 21:15–25). At "Especially", **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*). Communion Hymn: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken unto Thyself, O Lord; and their memorial is unto generation and generation. Alleluia!"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω*, Ps. 64:4 LXX). In place of **"We have seen the true Light..."** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), we chant the Dismissal Troparion: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom providing for all with love of mankind..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας φιλανθρώπως πάντα οἰκονομῶν*) [Note 14]; then we chant **"With the spirits of the righteous departed..."** (*Μετὰ πνευμάτων δικαίων*), and the names of all the deceased pious and Orthodox Christians from time immemorial are commemorated, etc., and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: 47.    In Great Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX), we do not chant the Psalter [Translator's Note: The Pentekostarion prescribes the First Kathisma of the Psalter: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX]. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we set ten verses and chant the three Idiomela of Tone 1: **"We celebrate Pentecost and the coming of the Spirit..."** (*Πεντηκοστὴν ἑορτάζομεν*) to five...[^479]

units.slavonic_diplomatic: ἤχου Πεντηκοστὴν ἑορτάζομεν εἰς ε΄ καὶ τὰ ε΄ τοῦ β΄ ἤχου Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς εἰς ς΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δεῦτε λαοί, Εἴσοδος, τὸ Φῶς ἱλαρόν, τὸ Προκείμενον Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν, καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα Ἀγνοοῦντα τὰ ἔθνη, Κύριε, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Γλῶσσαί ποτε, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐκ γ΄ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις Ὁ ἐν εἴδει πυρίνων γλωσσῶν οὐρανόθεν καταπέμψας τὸ πανάγιον Πνεῦμα ἐπὶ τοὺς ἁγίους αὐτοῦ Μαθητὰς καὶ Ἀποστόλους Χριστὸς κτλ.
